jobs.title: Associate General Counsel, Privacy – Remote (USA) (993-SLS)
jobs.excerpt: Our client, the company behind the fastest open-source analytical database in the world and a mission-driven, fast-growing private cloud company and leader in real-time analytics, data warehousing, and data observability, has exclusively engaged Solutus Legal Search to assist its executives in hiring an attorney to serve as Associate General Counsel, Privacy.
jobs.description:
Our client, the company behind the fastest open-source analytical database in the world and a mission-driven, fast-growing private cloud company and leader in real-time analytics, data warehousing, and data observability, has exclusively engaged Solutus Legal Search to assist its executives in hiring an attorney to serve as Associate General Counsel, Privacy.

The Role

    Reporting to the General Counsel, this attorney will own the company’s global privacy legal function, serving as the company’s principal legal advisor on domestic and international privacy and data protection matters, as well as be the Legal Team’s principal partner with the Security Team. This attorney will partner closely with business teams to develop and implement practical, business-oriented approaches to complex privacy issues and build scalable processes that support the company’s continued growth.

    This is a build role: you will take a growing set of privacy obligations, customer commitments, and regulatory exposures and turn them into a coherent, well-documented program that scales with the business. You will be the privacy expert in the room for product and engineering decisions, the person Sales and Legal turn to on DPAs and cross-border transfer questions and data flow mapping, and the legal lead alongside Security and GRC functions on security commitments, audits, and incident response. You will operate as an individual contributor, with the expectation that you build a team as the program matures. This role suits someone who is comfortable with technical depth. You will be reading data flow diagrams, asking engineers precise questions about where data is stored and who can reach it, and giving answers a product team can actually implement.

What You'll Do

    Own the global privacy program

  • Advise on domestic and international privacy and data protection laws and regulations, including GDPR, HIPAA, CCPA/CPRA, other U.S. state and international privacy laws, and international data transfer requirements.
  • Own the data subject request process end to end, along with the privacy elements of vendor and subprocessor diligence.
  • Track regulatory and enforcement developments across jurisdictions and translate them into concrete changes to our product, contracts, and internal practices — not just memos.
  • Conduct and oversee privacy risk assessments, including data protection impact assessments (DPIAs), transfer impact assessments, and related documentation.

    • Manage and build out the function

  • Enhance and mature the company’s privacy program to continue meeting evolving regulatory requirements. Scale core program components with respect to data subject rights requests, privacy notices, consent management, impact assessments, and policy management.
  • Maintain the program's operating machinery: records of processing, data inventories and mapping, retention schedules, DPIAs and transfer impact assessments, and privacy policies and notices.
  • Deliver privacy and security training that people remember, and drive internal awareness across engineering, sales, marketing, partner relationships and support.
  • Manage outside counsel and privacy vendors against a budget.
  • Serve as, or manage the relationship with, our EU representative and data protection officer arrangements as required.
  • Advise Marketing on adtech, cookies and tracking technologies, and electronic marketing compliance.
  • Report to leadership on privacy and security risk and support Board and audit reporting on the program.

    • Counsel product and engineering

  • Embed with product and engineering teams as they design features, giving privacy-by-design guidance early enough to shape architecture rather than block launches.
  • Advise on data residency and localization, telemetry and usage data, encryption and key management, access controls, logging, anonymization and pseudonymization, and retention and deletion mechanics.
  • Advise on AI and machine learning features — training data provenance, customer data use restrictions, model and vendor terms, and emerging AI regulatory requirements.

    • Support commercial contracting

  • Own our DPA and its negotiation strategy, including standard contractual clauses, the UK IDTA and Addendum, and other transfer mechanisms; negotiate the privacy and security terms in customer and vendor agreements.
  • Serve as escalation point for Legal and Deal Desk on privacy and security terms, and build the playbooks, fallback positions, and self-service guidance that let the rest of the team resolve most of these without you.
  • Support enterprise, public sector, and regulated-industry deals with sector-specific requirements, including HIPAA business associate agreements and financial services and payments obligations.

    • Partner with Security and GRC

  • Serve as legal counsel to the Security organization on our security commitments, control frameworks, and audit and certification programs — SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, PCI DSS, and the frameworks we take on next.
  • Lead the legal workstream in security incident response: assess breach notification obligations across jurisdictions and contracts, manage regulator and customer notification, direct outside counsel and forensics under privilege, and run tabletop exercises with Security.
  • Advise on law enforcement and government data requests, preservation obligations, and the policies governing how we respond.
  • Support the GRC and Compliance functions on customer security questionnaires, trust center content, and the accuracy of our public privacy and security representations

Requirements:

  • Strong academic credentials and membership in good standing with at least one U.S. state bar.
  • 7-10+ years of relevant legal experience, with strong training at a top-rated national or international law firm. Law firm and in-house experience at a high-growth B2B SaaS company, preferably in the data infrastructure sector.
  • Significant experience advising on domestic and international privacy and data protection matters.
  • Deep knowledge of global privacy laws and regulatory frameworks, including GDPR, HIPAA, CCPA/CPRA, other U.S. state and international privacy laws, cross-border data transfer requirements, and evolving privacy and data governance regulations.
  • Experience advising business and technical teams on privacy issues across the product lifecycle, including with respect to AI, machine learning, and emerging technologies, is strongly preferred.
  • Experience supporting security matters, including with respect to customer-facing security commitments, security incident support, and related regulatory requirements, is preferred.
  • Excellent judgment, strong business orientation, and ability to translate complex legal issues into practical advice.
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills and the ability to work effectively with executives and cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Exceptional attention to detail, strong organizational skills, and ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-moving, high-growth environment.

The current targeted base salary for this position ranges from $260,000 - $295,000, plus equity and a generous benefits package. Actual compensation is determined based on several factors, including a candidate’s qualifications, number of years of directly relevant experience, and location.

Solutus has been selected as the retained representative on this desirable search. Resumes submitted directly to our client will be forwarded to Solutus for review and evaluation.

Ref. #993-SLS

jobs.title: Head of Legal
jobs.excerpt: Thank you for considering Tailscale.  If this job description resonates with you, please apply.
jobs.description:
Thank you for considering Tailscale. If this job description resonates with you, please apply. Frequently cited statistics show that people who identify with historically marginalized groups are likely to apply to jobs only if they meet 100% of the qualifications. We encourage you to help us break that statistic!

About Tailscale

Tailscale is making safe connection effortless by delivering software that makes it easy to securely interconnect people and their devices, no matter where they are. From hobbyists to multinational corporations, teams of every size use Tailscale each day to protect their networks, share access to internal tools, and more. We're building a future for the Internet that's easy, sensible, and safe, like it used to be. Founded in 2019 and fully distributed, we're backed by Accel, CRV, Insight, Heavybit, and Uncork Capital.

About the Role

Tailscale is looking for a pragmatic, business-minded Head of Legal to build and lead our legal function through our next stage of growth.

As Tailscale’s senior legal leader, you’ll partner with executives and teams across the company to navigate complex legal and business considerations, manage risk, and build the capabilities needed to support a growing, globally distributed technology company.

This is an opportunity to shape how Legal operates at Tailscale. You’ll establish priorities, advise on important company and product decisions, and determine the right combination of internal talent, outside counsel, processes, and systems to support the business. An early priority will be strengthening our commercial legal capabilities, including hiring a dedicated leader to own contracts and help scale our approach to commercial transactions.

You may already lead a broad legal organization, or you may be an experienced legal leader who has taken on progressively greater responsibility and is ready to step into the top legal role for the first time.

Key Responsibilities

  • Build and evolve the strategy, priorities, operating model, and team for Tailscale’s legal function.
  • Serve as a trusted advisor to executives and cross-functional leaders, translating legal complexity into clear, practical business guidance.
  • Help leaders identify material risks, evaluate tradeoffs, and move forward with appropriate safeguards.
  • Partner with Product, Engineering, Security, Sales, Finance, People, Operations, Marketing, and other teams on company priorities.
  • Advise across a range of matters that may include corporate governance, product development, open-source software, intellectual property, privacy, data, AI, security, employment, commercial relationships, compliance, and international operations.
  • Build scalable legal processes, policies, systems, and decision-making frameworks without creating unnecessary complexity.
  • Determine which legal capabilities should be developed internally, delegated to future team members, or supported by outside counsel.
  • Hire and empower legal team members, including building a dedicated commercial legal capability.
  • Select and manage outside counsel across the countries where Tailscale operates, balancing expertise, responsiveness, cost, and business impact.
  • Coordinate guidance across jurisdictions and translate local requirements into practical, consistent company practices.
  • Support strategic partnerships, corporate initiatives, and other business-critical matters as Tailscale continues to grow.
  • Anticipate emerging legal and regulatory developments and help the company prepare for what comes next.

What We Are Looking For

  • Significant legal experience, including meaningful in-house experience within a technology company and a track record of helping legal functions scale in startup or high-growth environments.
  • A law degree and active membership in at least one applicable bar or equivalent authorization to practice law.
  • Progressive growth in the scope, complexity, ownership, and influence of your work.
  • Broad business judgment and the ability to navigate legal issues beyond a single area of specialization.
  • Experience advising executives and senior leaders on complex or consequential decisions.
  • The ability to understand business goals, identify material risks, and recommend practical paths forward.
  • Experience partnering effectively with technical, operational, and commercial teams.
  • Familiarity with the legal considerations facing a growing software or technology company.
  • Experience working with outside counsel and turning specialized advice into clear recommendations for the business.
  • A track record of building or improving legal capabilities, teams, programs, processes, or areas of practice.
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to make complex issues understandable to different audiences.
  • Sound judgment, curiosity, and the confidence to challenge constructively when needed.
  • Comfort operating in ambiguity and moving between strategic leadership and hands-on execution.
  • Admission and good standing with at least one applicable state, provincial, or other recognized bar association.

Nice to Have

We do not expect candidates to bring experience in every area below. Relevant experience may include:

  • Developer tools, infrastructure, cloud, networking, cybersecurity, data, or another technically complex software environment.
  • Open-source software, licensing, developer ecosystems, APIs, integrations, marketplaces, or technology partnerships.
  • Product counseling, privacy, data governance, cybersecurity, intellectual property, or emerging technology.
  • AI-enabled products or the use of AI within company operations.
  • Cloud, on-premises, self-hosted, or hybrid software offerings.
  • Data residency, sovereignty, localization, or cross-border data considerations.
  • Supporting employees or business operations across multiple countries.
  • Corporate governance, financing, strategic transactions, or board-related matters.
  • Building or scaling a legal function within a growth-stage company.
  • Hiring, developing, or leading in-house legal professionals.

How You’ll Work

At Tailscale, Legal is a thoughtful and pragmatic partner. You’ll seek to understand the goals behind the work, help teams evaluate tradeoffs, and build frameworks that enable people to make sound decisions with increasing independence.

You’ll thrive in this role if you enjoy building, are curious about technical products, and want to shape a legal function as the company grows. You know when to engage directly, when to bring in specialized expertise, and when to empower others to lead.

As a company, we strive to maintain fair and equitable compensation practices within our team across all roles and all levels. Tailscale's compensation package includes base salary, equity, and comprehensive benefits. The salary range displayed on each job posting represents the target range for a new hire's base salary. Individual offers may vary based on experience and skill set.

CAN Pay Range
$298,820—$427,460 CAD

What We Offer

  • An inclusive, flexible environment where you can be your authentic self. We recognize the impact of diverse voices and backgrounds on the growth of our people, product, and company. And that flexibility in how and when you work empowers our team to integrate work and life.
  • A competitive total compensation package. This includes a base salary, an equity incentive plan and variable commission (for quota-based roles).
  • Comprehensive group benefits with no waiting period. Take advantage of coverage for health, vision, dental, and more for you and your family!
  • Remote first company—most of our teams work fully remotely. Enjoy a change of scenery wherever you can get wifi, participate in virtual and in-person social events, and leverage our corporate co-working program to visit WeWork (or other similar spaces near you). Some roles require in-office collaboration depending on team needs, which will be clearly noted in the job description.
  • Employer-funded retirement contributions. Tailscale will match your retirement contributions dollar-for-dollar, up to a maximum annual employer contribution equal to 0.75% of your eligible compensation.
  • Connect with other Tailscalars IRL. Attend our annual company retreat, participate in team off-sites, and collaborate in person with teammates across Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, and Singapore. We support intentional in-person connection through team travel and distributed collaboration.
  • Support for your personal and professional development. Grow your career thoughtfully with $1500 USD annually for professional development, or take advantage of mentorship, coaching, and internal promotion opportunities.
  • Paid time off and a healthy work-life integration. Our flexible, paid time off program supports you for any situation life throws your way, whether moving homes or travelling the world!
  • A build-your-own home office setup. You choose your own company-owned laptop (Mac or PC), receive a monthly home internet reimbursement, and $500 USD to customize your workstation to make it your own.
  • Paid parental leave program. We care about your life outside of work and encourage new parents to take advantage of parental leave top-ups (20 weeks for birthing parents, 16 weeks for non-birthing parents).

Tailscale is committed to providing an accessible and inclusive hiring process. If you require an accommodation at any stage of the recruitment process or related to any aspect of this role, please contact your recruiter.

Our hiring process uses AI-assisted tools to help screen and assess candidates. All hiring decisions are made by people.

If you are motivated by meaningful challenges and want your impact to be real, measurable, and global, you will find purpose here.

About Us

Our AI-native platform unifies protection across endpoint, cloud, identity, data, and AI systems to deliver autonomous detection and response with clarity and speed. By combining real-time analytics, intelligent automation, and a unified data foundation, we reduce noise, simplify complexity, and empower security teams to focus on what truly matters.

Our teams are builders, problem-solvers, and innovators committed to shaping the future of security. If you are excited to solve hard problems alongside talented, mission-driven people, we invite you to help us build a safer future for humanity.

Why SentinelOne?

AI is redefining how the world operates and rewriting the rules of security in real time, and SentinelOne was built for this moment. jobs.excerpt: Project OverviewWe are sourcing independent Vocal Audio Specialists to provide their expertise for an AI audio model training project.
jobs.description:
Project Overview

We are sourcing independent Vocal Audio Specialists to provide their expertise for an AI audio model training project. As AI models increasingly generate and interpret human musicality and vocal nuances, their accuracy relies entirely on robust, high-fidelity training data. The objective of this project is to autonomously record clean, professional-grade audio detailing human vocal pitch changes by performing consistent, highly controlled humming exercises.

Project Deliverables & Scope

Operate autonomously to generate precise audio assets and structured training data. Expected deliverables include:

  • Vocal Recording & Pitch Execution: Recording clean, pitch-stable humming takes with dynamic control (e.g., humming softly without disappearing or louder without distorting), while strictly following tonal prompts (e.g., "hum a major 3rd," "stay in key").
  • Rhythmic & Melodic Consistency: Demonstrating a solid "internal metronome" to follow beats and executing highly repeatable tasks, such as humming the exact same melody multiple times with minimal variation.
  • Audio Engineering & Quality Control: Applying professional recording competence—including proper mic proximity, gain/input controls, and gain staging—to ensure distortion-free, high-fidelity audio capture within a controlled environment.
  • Strict Instruction Adherence: Accurately executing highly specific vocal directions (e.g., "flat tone, no vibrato") to generate clean, reliable, and standardized data for model training.

Required Expertise

To successfully fulfill the deliverables of this project, Contractors must possess strong musical literacy paired with reliable home recording capabilities.

Core skillset includes:

  • Demonstrable musical literacy and performance history (e.g., choir, band, a cappella, live gigs, audio engineering, or music production) with a calm, controlled voice and a highly trained ear for pitch stability.
  • Hands-on experience in Voice Over (VO) work, studio recording, or prior AI audio training projects. (Candidates completely new to recording workflows will not meet the quality threshold for this project).
  • Strong technical recording competence, including a deep understanding of gain staging, microphone technique, and how to operate recording equipment effectively.
  • A meticulous, detail-oriented approach to following instructions and maintaining rhythmic and tonal consistency across multiple recorded takes.
  • Required Asset: Must possess a controlled, quiet home recording environment capable of capturing clean audio free from background noise, clipping, or room echo.

We offer a pay range of $6-to-$65 per hour, with the exact rate determined after evaluating your experience, expertise, and geographic location. Final offer amounts may vary from the pay range listed above. As a contractor you’ll supply a secure computer, professional recording equipment, and high‑speed internet; company‑sponsored benefits such as health insurance and PTO do not apply.

Engagement Type: Freelance / Independent Contractor

Workplace Type: Remote

Marketing and Public Relations Director (Volunteer)

Mothers to Daughters

About Mothers to Daughters:

Mothers to Daughters (M2D) is a 501(c)(3) non-profit dedicated to empowering women across generations through leadership and entrepreneurship training, educational workshops, and networking opportunities. Through intergenerational mentorship and community service, M2D advances gender equality, fosters leadership, and equips women to drive social and economic change in their communities. This handbook outlines our values, policies, and operational procedures to guide team members in fulfilling our mission.

Our Mission at Mothers to Daughters is to accelerate the personal and professional growth of women by connecting them with the lived experiences, authentic insights, and transformative wisdom of successful women. Through intergenerational mentorship, we foster a legacy of economic empowerment, social resilience, and impact-driven innovation, equipping women to lead, innovate, and build sustainable solutions that transcend generations.

Our Vision is a world where women of all generations thrive through the power of intergenerational wisdom, driving inclusivity and gender equity for lasting global impact. By bridging generations, amplifying voices, and breaking down barriers, we aim to create a future where women are elevated to the heights they deserve—leading, innovating, and shaping a more equitable and prosperous world for all.

Our Core Values at Mothers to Daughters are:

  • UnwaveringRespect

    • We honor diverse perspectives and experiences, fostering an environment where every voice is valued.

    • We believe in mutual respect between generations, recognizing the wisdom of experience and the disruptive innovation of youth.

    • We encourage bold yet respectful dialogue in discussions around gender equality, relationships, and personal development.

  • Purpose driven-Trust

    • We prioritize transparency, accountability, and credibility, ensuring that our members, mentors, and sponsors feel confident in our work.

    • We believe trust is the cornerstone of meaningful mentorship, enabling honest, courageous conversations and impactful guidance.

    • We commit to upholding the integrity of our mission, maintaining the highest ethical standards in all our partnerships and programs.

  • Synergistic Collaboration

    • We recognize that transformative change happens when we work together across generations, cultures, and industries.

    • We actively forge alliances with organizations that align with our mission, including men’s groups working toward gender equity.

    • We foster a culture of dynamic knowledge-sharing, ensuring that mentorship is a two-way exchange where both mentors and mentees grow together.

  • Transformational Empathy

    • We understand that each woman’s journey is unique, committing to creating a safe space for shared experiences and personal growth.

    • We recognize societal and personal challenges women face and approach solutions with compassion and pragmatic action.

    • We champion vulnerability as a strength, encouraging open discussions about both breakthroughs and setbacks.

  • Impact-Driven Entrepreneurial Spirit

    • We believe in equipping women with the skills, mindset, and resources to take ownership of their futures—whether through career advancement, leadership, or business ventures.

    • We encourage innovation, agility, and adaptability, ensuring our programs evolve to meet the shifting needs of our global community.

    • We emphasize bold resilience, helping women break barriers, embrace risk, and lead with confidence.

  • Unapologetic Authenticity

    • We embrace and celebrate individuality, encouraging women to bring their whole selves to the table.

    • We champion unapologetic self-expression, ensuring that every woman’s voice is heard, respected, and amplified.

    • We commit to honest, transparent communication, rejecting performative feminism in favor of practical, high-impact actions that drive real change.

  • Future-focused Innovation

    • We embrace bold, transformative thinking, pushing boundaries to create solutions that redefine possibilities for women.

    • We leverage technology, data, and creativity to amplify mentorship, leadership, and economic empowerment initiatives.

    • We foster a culture of continuous learning and reinvention, ensuring that women stay ahead in an ever-evolving global landscape.

Position Overview:

The Marketing & PR Director will lead the development and execution of strategic marketing, communications, and public relations initiatives to elevate M2D’s brand, expand community engagement, and support program growth. Reporting to the Board, this leader will drive brand awareness, strengthen stakeholder relationships, and ensure consistent messaging across all platforms. The Director will oversee marketing campaigns, media outreach, digital strategy, community events, and partnerships, while aligning efforts with M2D’s mission of empowering young women through mentorship. This role also involves leading a high-performing team, managing budgets, and supporting fundraising and membership growth through compelling storytelling and targeted outreach.

Key Deliverables:

  • Develop and implement communication strategies to bring awareness to M2D vision, mission, goals, and services.

  • Responsible for actively driving M2D’s marketing, advertising, PR, media, communications, promotional activities, and all opportunities for growth, expansion, and partnerships that increase brand loyalty and exposure

  • Ensure all business decisions are consistent with the brand's image while meeting the budget requirements, and assess the performance of all marketing campaigns

  • Supervise the regular risk assessment and suggest mitigation strategies

jobs.description:
Job Description:

We are Omnissa!

Omnissa is the first AI-driven digital work platform, built to support flexible, secure, work-from anywhere experiences. We integrate industry-leading solutions—including Unified Endpoint Management, Virtual Apps and Desktops, Digital Employee Experience, and Security & Compliance—into a seamless, autonomous workspace that adapts to how people work. Our platform boosts employee engagement while optimizing IT operations, security, and cost.

Guided by our Core Values—Act in Alignment, Build Trust, Foster Inclusiveness, Drive Efficiency, and Maximize Customer Value—we’re growing rapidly and committed to delivering meaningful impact. If you're passionate about shaping the future of work, we’d love to hear from you.

At Omnissa, we are committed to maintaining a fair, consistent, and secure hiring process for all candidates. As part of this approach, we use standard interview and verification practices designed to ensure alignment and protect both candidates and the organization. These practices are applied thoughtfully and with respect for candidate privacy.

What is the opportunity?

Omnissa is seeking a Product Manager to run day-to-day product management for Workspace ONE Launcher and support the go-to-market motion for our frontline worker portfolio. Frontline is where device management stops being an IT abstraction and becomes the shift itself: a nurse at a workstation cart, a warehouse picker on a shared rugged handheld, a retail associate on a checkout tablet. You'll own the backlog for the application those workers touch every shift, work directly with engineering to ship it, and partner with Product Marketing and the field to bring it to market. You'll report to the product leader for the Google & Frontline portfolio and work alongside a senior PM on portfolio strategy, giving you a defined scope to own and room to grow into broader product direction. Here is a breakdown:

  • Own the Workspace ONE Launcher backlog across single-app and multi-app modes, staged and shared device check-in/check-out, and managed home screen experiences on Android.
  • Write Epics and user stories with precise, testable acceptance criteria, and groom the backlog with engineering to keep sprints loaded and unblocked.
  • Contribute to the frontline roadmap by researching customer requirements, sizing opportunities, and recommending prioritization to the portfolio product leader.
  • Partner with UX on Launcher end-user and administrator workflows, reviewing designs against Material Design standards and real frontline usage conditions such as gloved hands, low light, and offline devices.
  • Support frontline go-to-market execution with Product Marketing, Sales, and Solution Engineering, contributing feature messaging, launch checklists, release notes input, and demo content.
  • Run release readiness for Launcher, coordinating with Documentation, Release Management, Localization, and Support so each release ships with complete collateral.
  • Participate in customer and prospect calls to gather requirements, validate designs, and follow up on committed feature requests.
  • Track product usage and adoption metrics for Launcher, building recurring reporting that shows where customers succeed and where they stall.
  • Triage inbound feature requests and escalations, partnering with Support and Engineering to reproduce issues, assess impact, and route fixes into the backlog.
  • Maintain internal enablement material for Launcher, including demo environments, FAQs, and enablement decks for customer-facing teams.
  • Author and review customer-facing technical content covering Launcher configuration, deployment, and troubleshooting.

What will you bring to Omnissa?

  • 3+ years in product management, product marketing, technical marketing, solutions engineering, systems engineering, or another customer-facing enterprise software role.
  • Direct professional experience in enterprise mobility, unified endpoint management, mobile application development, or frontline worker technology; this role assumes you have worked in or adjacent to this space before.
  • Working knowledge of Android device management, including Android Enterprise enrollment modes, dedicated and fully managed deployments, and managed configurations.
  • Demonstrated ability to write clear requirements and ship features with an engineering team on an agile cadence.
  • Comfort presenting to customers & internal stakeholders and translating technical detail into plain language.
  • Strong written communication skills, with the ability to author accurate customer-facing content.
  • Collaborative working style, with a track record of driving work forward across teams you don't own.
  • Data-driven approach to prioritization, with experience using product analytics or usage telemetry.
  • Hands-on experience with Workspace ONE UEM or a comparable enterprise endpoint management platform.
  • Exposure to frontline verticals such as retail, healthcare, logistics, transportation, or manufacturing, including shared device and shift-based work patterns.
  • Familiarity with rugged device ecosystems or Android OEM programs.

Location: Canada or United States

Location Type: REMOTE / HYBRID (if near Atlanta)
Travel Expectations: 5% - expect to travel to occasional conferences and customer visits.
Education: Bachelor’s degree preferred, or equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience.

Compensation: The typical base salary for this role is between USD $124,000 – $180,000 per year and it may be eligible for participation in a corporate bonus program. Actual compensation offer may vary from posted hiring range based upon geographic location, work experience, education, skill level, or other relevant factors. In addition to competitive compensation, Omnissa offers a variety of benefits such as employee ownership, health insurance, 401k with matching contributions, disability insurance, paid-time off, growth opportunities, and more.

Omnissa is an Equal Employment Opportunity company and Prohibits Discrimination and Harassment of Any Kind:
Omnissa is committed to the principle of equal employment opportunity and to providing a work environment free of discrimination and harassment. All employment decisions at Omnissa are based on business needs, job requirements and individual qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion, ancestry, ethnicity, national, social or ethnic origin, sex (including pregnancy), age, physical, mental or sensory disability, HIV status, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, marital, civil union or domestic partnership status, past, present, or prospective service in the uniformed services, family medical history or genetic information, family or parental status, veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable laws or regulations in the locations where we operate. Omnissa will not tolerate discrimination or harassment based on any of these characteristics. Omnissa welcomes applicants of all ages. Omnissa will provide reasonable accommodations to applicants and employees who have protected disabilities consistent with applicable federal, state and local law.

This job requisition is not eligible for employment-based immigration sponsorship by Omnissa.

Senior Advisor – Utilities Business Development

About Voyage Advisory
Voyage Advisory is a boutique management consulting firm that helps organizations elevate service, drive performance, and power transformation. We partner with clients across customer experience, operations, technology, and organizational change initiatives, delivering practical solutions and measurable results.

As we continue to grow, we are seeking an experienced utilities industry leader to serve as a Senior Advisor focused on business development and strategic relationship cultivation.

Position Overview
The Senior Advisor – Utilities Business Development will leverage an established network of utilities industry relationships to identify opportunities, create introductions, and help expand Voyage Advisory's presence within the utilities market.

This is not a traditional, end-to-end sales role, since Voyage's internal team supports proposal development, SOWs, and contracting. Rather, we are seeking a highly respected industry veteran who understands the challenges facing utilities organizations, maintains strong executive-level relationships, and can help connect Voyage with decision-makers who may benefit from our consulting services, and is expected to help guide those relationships toward closed business.

This is a flexible, part-time position requiring approximately 10–30 hours per month. While the schedule is flexible, this is an active, accountable role with defined performance expectations, not an informal referral arrangement.

Key Responsibilities
  • Leverage existing relationships within the utilities industry to identify potential opportunities for Voyage Advisory.
  • Introduce Voyage leadership to executive decision-makers and key stakeholders.
  • Serve as a trusted advisor regarding industry trends, challenges, and market opportunities.
  • Represent Voyage Advisory in industry conversations, events, conferences, and networking opportunities for sales and marketing purposes.
  • Provide insight into emerging client needs and strategic priorities.
  • Collaborate with Voyage leadership to develop targeted growth strategies within the utilities sector.
  • Work closely with Voyage's internal team on proposals, SOWs, and other deal mechanics.
  • Attend a standing internal sales meeting and maintain accurate, up-to-date records in Voyage's sales CRM.
  • Meet quarterly performance targets tied to pipeline contribution and closed business, consistent with the paid nature of this role.
  • Participate in occasional prospect meetings and business development discussions.
  • Help strengthen Voyage's reputation and visibility within the utilities marketplace.
  • May have the opportunity to get involved in Voyage consulting engagements as a Senior Advisor, for those who are interested in additional project work.

Qualifications
Required
  • 15+ years of leadership experience within the utilities industry.
  • Extensive network across electric, gas, water, or multi-service utility organizations.
  • Relationships with utility executives responsible for customer operations, contact centers, field operations, technology, digital transformation, and enterprise operations.
  • Prior management consulting experience with a recognized consulting firm or substantial consulting leadership experience.
  • Extensive network of executive-level relationships across utilities companies, or related industry segments.
  • Demonstrated ability to build trusted relationships with senior leaders.
  • Excellent communication and executive presence.
  • Experience working on enterprise business development, ideally including: management consulting proposals and solutions
Preferred
  • Former utility executive, consulting partner, business unit leader, or transformation executive.
  • Experience working with regulated utilities and utility modernization initiatives.
  • Personal rapport with C-suite and senior executives at utilities organizations Voyage is currently targeting.

Work Arrangement
  • Part-time (approximately 10–30 hours per month)
  • Remote
  • Occasional travel may be required

What Success Looks Like
Success in this role is measured by the ability to create meaningful introductions, generate qualified opportunities, help convert those opportunities into closed or signed business, and help Voyage Advisory establish and expand strategic relationships within the utilities industry.

Compensation Structure
Compensation involves a competitive hourly rate. In addition, there will be a commission structure put in place tied to business development and referral success.

Job Title: Vendor & Third-Party Management Quality & Compliance Manager

Job Overview
The position provides Quality Assurance support for Global Medical Affairs Vendor & Third-Party Management, primarily through the management of quality events, quality issues, deviations, and Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPAs), as well as audit support and audit readiness. The role also supports Research Collaboration (RC) due diligence and selected non-vendor third-party assessment activities and contributes to third-party quality risk management, compliance, and continuous process improvement.

Quality Events, CAPAs and Audit Readiness
• Manage Quality Events (QEs), Quality Issues (QIs), deviations, and related investigations in collaboration with relevant stakeholders.
• Act as Deviation Owner, as appropriate, and support CAPA definition, implementation, tracking, effectiveness assessment, and closure.
• Support internal and external audits, audit readiness activities, and the remediation of audit findings.

V&TPM Quality Risk Management and Compliance
• Support third-party governance and oversight activities from a quality and compliance perspective.
• Support and contribute to third-party Quality Risk Assessments (QRAs) and ensure assessments are completed, documented, and maintained for relevant GMA activities, including non-interventional studies (NIS), real-world evidence and real-world data (RWE/RWD) activities, Research Collaborations (RCs), and partnerships. Follow up on identified risks and associated mitigation actions, as appropriate.
• Identify, assess, and escalate potential risks arising from third-party due diligence, qualification, and oversight activities.
• Ensure compliance with applicable SOPs, business guidance documents, quality standards, and regulatory requirements.

Research Collaboration/non-vendor Due Diligence and Assessment
• Support Research Collaboration (RC) and other selected third-party (non-vendor) due diligence and assessment activities, as required.
• Ensure the quality, accuracy, and completeness of due diligence and assessment documentation in TPM systems and tools.
• Coordinate with internal stakeholders and third parties to obtain information and documentation required for due diligence and assessment activities.
• Support the maintenance and continuous improvement of TPM due diligence tools, including TPIAT (Third-Party Impact & Assessment Tool).

Process Improvement, Training and Stakeholder Collaboration

• Lead and/or contribute as a subject matter expert to the design, revision, implementation, and continuous improvement of GMA V&TPM quality, compliance, governance processes, standards, procedures, and guidance documents.

• Support the development, revision, and implementation of relevant procedures, standards, and guidance documents.

• Provide V&TPM quality and compliance expertise, guidance, and training to operational teams and stakeholders.

  • Experience working with external suppliers, research partners, and cross-functional stakeholders within a pharmaceutical company or CRO environment. Emphasis on business, experience with clinical/medical affairs processes and activities and associated external services, with excellent understanding of study management.

  • Strong understanding of clinical and Medical Affairs processes, study management activities, and associated external services.

  • Good knowledge of the regulatory requirements in Clinical Research and drug development:

  • In-depth knowledge of the international pharmaceutical product development process

jobs.description:
This is a technical, behind-the-scenes role responsible for supporting the execution and quality of the organization's quantitative research.

You will work across studies to ensure surveys are programmed correctly, data is clean and accurate, and reporting outputs are client-ready. This includes program checking, data scanning and cleaning, data processing, report population, and rigorous numerical QC.

This is an ideal role for someone who enjoys the technical and operational side of quantitative research, has exceptional attention to detail, and naturally notices when something in the data doesn’t look right.

Duties and Responsibilities

Survey Programming & QA

  • Review programmed surveys against questionnaires for accuracy and consistency
  • Test survey logic, skips, piping, randomization, quotas, calculations, and respondent flow
  • Conduct soft-launch data checks and identify potential programming or fieldwork issues
  • Partner with researchers and programming vendors to troubleshoot and resolve issues

Data Quality & Processing

  • Scan and clean respondent-level data throughout fieldwork and at study close
  • Identify poor-quality respondents, inconsistent responses, suspicious open ends, speeders, straightliners, and other data-quality concerns
  • Investigate unexpected data patterns and troubleshoot potential programming, sampling, or data-processing issues
  • Support recodes, derived variables, banners, crosstabs, weighting, and significance testing
  • Review data tables and other outputs for accuracy and consistency

Reporting & Analysis Support

  • Populate PowerPoint reports with survey data, including charts and tables
  • Check bases, percentages, significance, calculations, and data labels
  • Conduct rigorous numerical QC of client deliverables
  • Troubleshoot discrepancies across raw data, tables, and reporting outputs
  • Prepare clean, analysis-ready data and outputs for research teams

Operational Excellence

  • Serve as a centralized resource for quantitative research quality and technical execution
  • Develop and improve standardized processes for program checking, data cleaning, reporting, and QC
  • Identify opportunities to automate or streamline repetitive quantitative workflows
  • Learn and leverage AI-powered tools and platforms to improve efficiency and quality

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree (market research, psychology, sociology, business, communications, or related field preferred)
  • 0–2 years of experience (internships count)
  • High attention to detail
  • Strong analytical and writing skills
  • Proficiency in Excel and PowerPoint (experience with survey or analytics tools a plus)
  • Ability to manage multiple deadlines in a remote environment

Landscape Developer – UK & Ireland

32-40 hours per week | Preferred: Remote within UK or Ireland | One-year contract with possibility of extension

Preferred starting date: 1 December 2026

Are you passionate about driving systemic change in landscape restoration through strategic partnerships, finance and fundraising, and collaborative learning? Do you thrive in complex, multi-stakeholder environments and enjoy bridging gaps between funders, governments, and grassroots initiatives? This could be the role for you!

About the Role

Commonland supports a growing network of landscape scale restoration initiatives across the UK and Ireland. Through long-term, collaborative Learning and Social Lab networks, we aim to strengthen leadership, enhance enabling conditions, and address systemic barriers to holistic landscape restoration and regeneration. This goes beyond one-off workshops: we are working together with our partners to consciously develop multi-year, systemic multistakeholder processes that move from building shared understanding, to experimentation and action, helping key actors tackle root causes of degradation and build regenerative landscapes. This role includes regular travel within the UK and Ireland, with occasional international travel.

The impact you make:

  • Support landscape partners across the UK & Ireland with direct strategic support and connect with system-level actors (companies, funders, government bodies, foundations, and knowledge institutions).

  • Secure funding and financing mechanisms by unlocking Ireland’s incoming nature restoration law funding and engaging the UK nature finance & funding landscape, and matchmaking between finance providers and landscape partners.

  • Co-design innovative responses to systemic barriers to- and opportunities for holistic landscape restoration, leveraging existing relationships to bring about systemic changes.

  • Co-develop a comprehensive fundraising strategy, identifying and mapping UK, Irish, and European public/private funding opportunities.

  • Support landscape partners in developing systemic innovations (e.g., bioregional finance, payment for ecosystem services, learning networks) and scaling credible alternatives to current economic models.

  • Organise learning sessions to build partners’ fundraising and facilitation capacity, aligning with the regions evolving social innovation lab structure.

  • Collaborate with Commonland’s global learning community to share insights and ensure strategic alignment with the European Landscape restoration community.

What You Bring

You are someone who:

  • Designs partnerships, programmes and processes: You build processes grounded in ambition to create long-term, holistic and regenerative system change, balancing structure with adaptability.

  • Thinksin systems: Connect themes (e.g., upland dynamics, agri-food innovation), can sit with the discomfort of complexity, and intentionally and attentionally guide others through change.

  • Communicates with empathy and understanding: You listen deeply, build trust across diverse stakeholders, and foster inclusive collaboration with stakeholders.

  • Operates from shared purpose: You connect people, ideas, and interests to unlock collective potential.

  • Learns and adapts: You’re open-minded, curious, and quick to adjust to emerging needs and insights while maintaining the momentum.

  • Results-driven: You combine innovative thinking with structured execution to deliver tangible outcomes.

You also bring:

  • Several years experience in partnership development, landscape restoration and/or fundraising with a track record in the UK/Ireland.

  • Solid understanding of the UK/Ireland’s environmental, agricultural, or rural and sustainable development sectors.

  • Strong nature finance & funding literacy, including a clear view of where funding and market-based finance mechanisms deliver and where they don't, and interest in regenerative, new economy and bioregional approaches.

  • Fluency in English; additional bioregional languages (e.g., Welsh, Irish) are a plus.

  • A broad network of stakeholders working in landscape restoration in the UK/Ireland.

What We Offer

  • A purpose-driven role where your work directly contributes to restoring the conditions that create thriving landscapes and shaping a regenerative future.

  • A competitive gross monthly salary between €5,100 and €6,000 (based on 40 hours/week), tailored to your level of experience and local cost of living.

  • Flexibility to work remotely, with the freedom to design your workday to suit your life and energy, as well as work commitments and fixtures.

  • Room to grow, with opportunities for personal and professional development through learning, reflection, and experimentation including a personal learning budget of 1,750 GBP/ 2,000 euro per year.

  • A supportive team culture that values creativity, collaboration, and continuous learning.

Commonland Foundation

Commonland is an international non-profit that supports people and organisations to restore landscapes and shape a regenerative future for all. With our holistic approach – underpinned by the 4 Returns Framework – people and organisations all over the world are working with nature and their community to restore landscapes. Our core values are empowering each other, putting words into action, and being compassionate & honest.

How to Apply

We are excited to learn more about you and how your competencies fit this role. Because your answers play a key role in our initial selection process, we encourage you to provide thoughtful responses. About Young Americans For Liberty

Founded after the 2008 Ron Paul Presidential Campaign, Young Americans for Liberty (YAL) is the nation’s largest pro-liberty youth movement, building a powerful network of activists to transform states into beacons of freedom.

We drive real change in America by working through our "Build - Elect - Pass" model:

  1. Build: We are building the largest nationwide movement of committed youth activists on American college campuses, with pro-liberty students fighting on hundreds of campuses across the country.
  2. Elect: We mobilize our base of committed youth activists to be the grassroots muscle on campaigns of principled liberty legislators through Operation Win at the Door. Since 2018, we've built a coalition of 400 active legislators in our National Liberty Legislator Coalition, and thousands of YAL-recruited students have knocked on over 6 million doors to turn out the vote.
  3. Pass: We train this coalition of principled liberty legislators to pass transformative policy at the state level. This coalition has already passed over 1,250 pro-liberty bills spanning from Universal School Choice, to Constitutional Carry, to major tax cuts and so much more. You can view the full list of bills passed at.

Mission & Vision

Our mission is to identify, educate, train, and mobilize youth activists committed to the ideals of liberty and the Constitution. Our vision is to create Liberty Lighthouse States that will Transform Our States into Beacons of Liberty. YAL also works to achieve this vision by electing liberty legislators and passing liberty legislation.

Our Values & Culture

YAL's culture is built on 5 foundational values:

  1. Goal Setting: We orient our work towards specific goals that align with achieving our long-term vision.
  2. Trust the Truth: We pursue the truth and are honest in all we do, even when it’s difficult. There should never be a situation where lying is the right answer if we’re truthful from the beginning.
  3. Grassroots Mobilization: We win on principle by generating grassroots pressure on the politicians. Unless you are politically feared, you will not be politically respected. Education alone is not enough.
  4. Principle: We believe in liberty — which provides the freedom to choose and requires taking responsibility for your choices — and individual rights — which must be respected at all times.
  5. Power of the Individual: We recognize everyone has an innate ability to make a difference. Therefore, we are dedicated to aligning your goals and developing your strengths so you can unlock your full potential.

Candidates who will fit in with YAL's culture tend to be principled, entrepreneurial, passionate, and comfortable with ambitious goals and a fast-paced work environment.

Most people complain about politics. A select few organize to change it.

Young Americans for Liberty is looking for several Activism Coordinators to recruit, mobilize, and develop activists who are willing to take action in defense of liberty.

If you've built a chapter, organized an event, recruited volunteers, or led a grassroots effort on campus, this is an opportunity to take those skills into a paid role and help build the liberty movement beyond your own campus.

This role is ideal for current students, recent graduates, and emerging grassroots leaders who want to continue organizing, developing activists, and advancing liberty through real-world action.

Success in this role depends on your ability to build relationships, motivate volunteers, and turn supporters into well-trained activists who consistently take action. You will help create grassroots pressure around YAL's priorities by organizing people, growing engagement, and supporting educational and advocacy efforts throughout your assigned territory.

This is a relationship-driven role that requires strong communication, organization, and follow-through. You will regularly communicate with activists, support chapter leaders, and create opportunities for members to become more effective activists and engage in meaningful action.

This position reports directly to the Activism Director.

📍 Location: Remote (travel required within an assigned territory)

🕒 Schedule: Part-time, hourly (approximately 20 hours per week)

What you'll do

Mobilize activists and drive action

  • Organize and execute grassroots educational and advocacy campaigns
  • Mobilize activists to participate in legislative and grassroots efforts
  • Coordinate activist participation in training opportunities, events, and initiatives
  • Maintain regular communication regarding opportunities for involvement

What Success Looks Like

The Virtual Territory Business Manager (VTBM) is a virtual sales professional responsible for driving launch readiness, successful product commercialization, and sustaining business growth within assigned territory through primarily digital and remote interactions. As the primary point of contact for the eye care community, the VTBM develops trusted partnerships with Retina specialists, comprehensive ophthalmologists, optometrists, genetic counselors, academic medical centers, referral networks, and other key healthcare stakeholders to educate on disease state, identify appropriate patients, and support the adoption of innovative therapies.

By leveraging customer insights, market analytics, competitive intelligence, and territory performance data, the VTBM identifies opportunities, prioritizes accounts, anticipates barriers to adoption, and implements targeted strategies that accelerate market uptake and optimize territory performance. Working collaboratively with cross-functional partners including Market Access, Marketing, Medical Affairs, Commercial Operations, and other field-based teams, the VTBM ensures coordinated execution of launch strategies, customer engagement initiatives, and access solutions that enhance customer experience and support patient access.

The Virtual Territory Business Manager must demonstrate effective virtual account management skills and engage nurses, pharmacists, physicians, genetic counselors, office administrators, and support staff through digital platforms to increase awareness of the brand and disease state.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Translate national brand strategy into a territory business strategy and corresponding tactical plan while meeting activity, access, and sales objectives.
  • Drive product adoption through pre-call planning, listening, probing, clinical messaging impact, and supporting complex patient access education.
  • Build and maintain proficiency in the disease state, patient journey and product knowledge to deliver compelling clinical and diseases state awareness aligned with approved messaging and compliance standards.
  • Conduct high-quality virtual customer engagements utilizing approved promotional materials, digital resources, and compliant messaging.
  • Establish and maintain productive relationships with ophthalmologists, retina specialists, inherited retinal disease (IRD) specialists, genetic counselors, and other key stakeholders through telephone, video conferencing, email, and approved digital communication channels.
  • Leverage digital engagement tools, analytics, and customer insights to prioritize opportunities and maximize business impact.
  • Exhibit an ownership mindset by emphasizing customer prioritization, thoughtful resource allocation, and an analytical view of opportunities.
  • Monitor and adapt based on lead/lag indicators (identified patients, referral pathways, diagnostic odyssey engagement, specialty pharmacy pull-through) and escalate competitive intelligence and field insights to sales leadership.
  • Maintain accurate and timely documentation of customer interactions, account plans, and territory activities within approved CRM systems.
  • Demonstrate a commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion through continuous development, modeling inclusive behaviors, and proactively managing bias.
  • All other duties as assigned.

KEY COMPETENCIES:

  • Strategic thinking and execution excellence
  • Demonstrated advanced clinically based selling skills
  • Collaborative and adaptable ways of working
  • High-level customer partnership and development
  • Patient centric mindset
  • Strong business acumen and market insight with an ownership mindset
  • Cross-functional influence and collaboration
  • Adaptability in complex, evolving markets

COMMUNICATION SKILLS:

  • Effectively communicate approved clinical and scientific information related to the brand to healthcare professionals, ophthalmologists, IRD specialists, genetic counselors, and office staff through virtual engagements.
  • Deliver compelling disease state education and product information while remaining compliant with company policies and regulatory requirements.
  • Conduct impactful video meetings, virtual presentations, webinars, and remote educational programs with healthcare professionals and office personnel.

MINIMUM KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:

The requirements below represent the experience, education, knowledge, skills, and abilities needed for this role.

Education:

  • Bachelor’s degree in a related field.

Experience:

  • Minimum of 3-5 years of pharmaceutical, biotechnology, specialty healthcare sales, inside sales, virtual sales, or customer engagement experience with a demonstrated record of business success.
  • Ophthalmology experience strongly preferred.
  • Virtual pharmaceutical sales or omnichannel customer engagement experience preferred.
  • Strong understanding of ophthalmology practices, retina centers, academic medical centers, referral networks, and the ophthalmology market landscape.
  • Knowledge of inherited retinal diseases, ophthalmology treatment pathways, and patient identification processes preferred.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop, execute, and manage strategic account plans in a virtual environment.
  • Proven success in developing customer relationships and influencing treatment adoption through remote engagement channels.

  • Demonstrated success utilizing digital engagement strategies to drive customer adoption and business performance.

jobs.excerpt: Lightly AG is a Zurich-based AI company and ETH/HSG spin-off, backed by Y Combinator and top-tier investors.
jobs.description:
Lightly AG is a Zurich-based AI company and ETH/HSG spin-off, backed by Y Combinator and top-tier investors. Our machine learning and computer vision technology is trusted by global leaders in autonomous driving, medical imaging, and visual inspection.

We’re looking for researchers with strong Machine Learning / AI backgrounds to support an AI evaluation project focused on scientific peer review. You’ll evaluate reviews generated by agentic AI systems and compare them against expert human peer reviews of ML/AI research papers.

This is a remote, project-based contractor opportunity with flexible working hours.

Tasks

What you'll be doing

  • Read and scan ML/AI research papers to understand their core contributions, methodology, experiments, and claims
  • Review the original human peer reviews to establish an expert baseline for each paper
  • Evaluate AI-generated peer reviews against that baseline using a structured scoring rubric
  • Assess the technical accuracy, analytical depth, constructive value, and novelty/significance assessment of each AI review
  • Identify hallucinations, unsupported claims, missed technical issues, or valuable insights surfaced by the AI reviewers
  • Compare two AI-generated reviews side-by-side and determine where one provides stronger or more useful analysis
  • Search and verify relevant academic literature using sources such as Google Scholar, arXiv, or Semantic Scholar, including checking whether cited prior work was available before the paper’s submission date
  • Provide concise, evidence-based rationales explaining your evaluation decisions and consistently apply the project rubric

The evaluation specifically looks at whether agentic AI reviewers can provide meaningful value beyond expert human reviewers—for example, by identifying relevant prior literature that humans missed, questioning important assumptions, or resolving inconsistencies using evidence.

Requirements

You're a strong candidate if you:

  • Have a Master’s, PhD, or are currently pursuing graduate study in Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Computer Science, Statistics, or a closely related technical field
  • Have contributed to at least one scientific/research paper, ideally as a first author, although co-authors and other substantial contributors are also welcome
  • Have experience critically reading ML/AI research papers, including evaluating methodology, experimental design, results, limitations, and scientific claims
  • Are familiar with major ML/AI research venues, such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, CVPR, or comparable conferences and journals
  • Have prior academic peer-review experience, ideally for an ML/AI conference or journal — strongly preferred
  • Are comfortable conducting academic literature searches and verifying prior work, publication dates, citations, and novelty claims
  • Have strong analytical and written communication skills and can distinguish meaningful technical concerns from superficial criticism
  • Can provide clear, concise, evidence-based rationales for your decisions
  • Can consistently apply detailed evaluation guidelines and scoring rubrics across multiple papers and reviews
  • Have strong attention to detail, particularly when identifying factual inaccuracies or hallucinated technical claims

Benefits

  • Fully remote and flexible — work from anywhere
  • Part-time contractor role with flexible hours
  • Work directly on the evaluation of cutting-edge agentic AI systems for scientific research
  • Apply your ML/AI research expertise to help measure and improve the quality of AI-generated scientific peer review

Send us your CV along with a brief note about your research background and areas of expertise. Please include any relevant publications, as well as previous peer-review experience for conferences, journals, workshops, or similar academic venues.

If applicable, we'd also love to know which ML/AI research areas and conferences you’re most familiar with.

We look forward to hearing from you!

Care Specialists

US Commercial, Market Access – Remote

Pharvaris is a Nasdaq listed late-stage biotech company developing bradykinin B2 receptor antagonists for bradykinin-mediated angioedema (including hereditary angioedema), with offices in Switzerland (Zug), the Netherlands (Leiden) and the USA (greater Boston area). We aim at bringing new, more convenient options to people who suffer sudden and prolonged attacks of swelling in multiple areas of the body including the airway, which can be life-threatening.

We have a culture built on the core values of considering others care-fully, leading with trust, ensuring rigor and diversity of thought, and contributing freely. Our company is driven by individuals committed to developing breakthrough therapies which can have a real impact on people’s lives. If you are looking for a place where your work can have meaning, and you can make a difference – Pharvaris is the place for you!

We are excited to be building our commercial business infrastructure to prepare for our first commercial launch. We are actively recruiting for the Patient Services Team, and we are looking for dynamic and experienced Care Specialiststo join our team and report to the Lead, Care Specialists.

The Care Specialist will exercise independent judgment and sound business discretion in administering complex patient-access operations for an assigned geography. This role assesses patient, provider, payer, and reimbursement needs; determines appropriate access-support strategies, case actions, and escalation pathways for complex or non-routine matters; interprets and applies patient-services policies and payer requirements; and serves as a knowledgeable resource for patients, healthcare providers, partners, insurance companies, and internal stakeholders seeking access to Pharvaris products. The role also provides case-management oversight for an assigned caseload while identifying risks, trends, barriers, and opportunities for process improvement that may require escalation, management recommendation, or broader patient-support program improvements impacting launch readiness and ongoing program effectiveness.

Location:

Pharvaris has offices in Switzerland (Zug), the Netherlands (Leiden) and the U.S. (greater Boston area) and, at Pharvaris, we promote and enable a flexible, hybrid work-environment and support our talent to be home based and work virtually. Whilst this is a remote role, you must be located in the US with a preference to the geography you cover or East Coast /Boston area.

Responsibilities:

  • Independently assess patient and caregiver access needs and determine appropriate support strategies to facilitate timely access to therapy
  • Exercise discretion in overseeing and prioritizing assigned caseload activities, identifying access barriers, determining next steps, and advancing cases through required access processes
  • Interpret patient-services policies and payer requirements to guide complex benefits investigations, prior authorization and appeal support, and stakeholder communications
  • Maintain case documentation for the assigned geography and use case insights to identify reimbursement trends, access risks, and opportunities for process improvement
  • Oversee resolution of complex patient-access matters, evaluate reimbursement pathways, and determine appropriate escalation or resolution strategies within delegated authority
  • Serve as an internal reimbursement subject matter expert by guiding cross-functional partners on payer requirements, access barriers, and strategic case considerations
  • Provide ongoing adherence and compliance support to patients in alignment with program requirements and approved processes
  • Contribute insights and recommendations in patient services and commercial strategy meetings based on reimbursement trends, case escalations, and program performance
  • Lead special projects and recommend operational improvements that enhance patient-support program efficiency, compliance, scalability, and launch readiness
  • Serve as a compliance role model for the commercial organization and broader Pharvaris community by identifying compliance concerns and recommending appropriate improvements
  • Conduct all activities with the highest ethical standards and in compliance with applicable legal and regulatory requirements, including the U.S. Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, U.S. anti-kickback laws, and the PhRMA Code

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree preferred; equivalent experience in rare disease patient support services, access and reimbursement, or related biotech/pharmaceutical roles involving independent decision-making may be considered
  • Minimum of 7 years of progressive case management experience required, including responsibility for evaluating complex patient-access matters, determining appropriate resolution pathways, and managing non-routine reimbursement issues; rare disease experience strongly preferred
  • Demonstrated experience supporting patients, caregivers, and healthcare providers in a call center, customer service, or patient support environment requiring professional judgment, prioritization, and effective issue resolution
  • Advanced experience supporting pharmacy and medical benefit investigations, prior authorizations, appeals, reimbursement processes, and case escalations requiring analysis of payer requirements and application of program guidelines
  • Strong understanding of commercial and government payer requirements, coverage policies, access pathways, and the ability to interpret and apply those requirements to complex patient-access situations
  • Ability to identify reimbursement trends, assess access risks, recommend process improvements, and communicate strategic insights to internal stakeholders and management
  • Proven ability to work independently in a remote environment, exercise discretion with sensitive patient and reimbursement information, and manage priorities across an assigned geography
  • Ability to travel up to 10% as business needs require

We are looking for someone that has:

  • Patient first mindset
  • Collaborative Influence & Relationship Agility
  • Analytical & Problem-Solving Skills
  • Creative thinker

Pharvaris is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. The base salary range for this role is $110,000-$150,000 per year. Actual compensation will depend on various factors, including but not limited to depth of experience, skill set, overall performance, and education. Pharvaris believes in providing a competitive compensation and benefits package. Base salary is just one component of our competitive total rewards strategy. In addition to compensation, this role offers the unique opportunity to help build and shape an early-stage commercial organization, meaningful ownership through equity, workplace flexibility, and flexible time off. We encourage candidates who are motivated by the full opportunity and alignment with our mission to apply, even if their current compensation falls outside the stated range.
