jobs.description:
Thanks for your interest in Oklo! We are searching for an Product Manager to join our New Product Introduction team, focused on nuclear reactor products. We are looking to fill this position immediately.

Position Description

Oklo’s Product Managers are responsible for identifying, defining, developing, and deploying new products that advance the company’s mission. These products may involve new applications of Oklo’s technology, capabilities incorporated into future deployments, or offerings that create additional value for customers and stakeholders.

The Product Manager works across engineering, commercial, operations, licensing, manufacturing, supply chain, and other functions to translate promising ideas into well-defined, deployable products. This role establishes the product vision, identifies customer and business needs, defines requirements and success criteria, and guides the product through technical development and deployment.

This is a highly technical product role. The Product Manager must be able to understand complex engineered systems, work closely with technical teams, and make thoughtful tradeoffs among performance, cost, schedule, risk, manufacturability, licensing, and customer value. Successful candidates may come from a product management background with strong engineering experience or may be engineers who are excited to take broader ownership of product strategy and deployment.

Specific responsibilities may include:

  • Identifying and evaluating opportunities for products, capabilities, and applications of Oklo nuclear reactor technology.
  • Developing clear product visions, value propositions, business cases, and deployment strategies.
  • Working with customers, partners, commercial teams, and internal stakeholders to understand needs and translate them into actionable product requirements.
  • Partnering closely with engineering teams to define product functionality, technical requirements, interfaces, performance objectives, and acceptance criteria.
  • Building and maintaining product roadmaps that connect technical development with commercial opportunities and deployment objectives.
  • Guiding reactor technology products from early concept and feasibility assessment through design, development, validation, and deployment.
  • Establishing appropriate product development plans, decision points, maturity criteria, and measures of success.
  • Leading cross-functional trade studies and decisions involving technical performance, safety, cost, schedule, licensing, manufacturability, operability, and commercial value.
  • Ensuring development work is appropriately sized and focused on resolving the most important product risks and uncertainties.
  • Coordinating across engineering, licensing, procurement, supply chain, manufacturing, operations, finance, and commercial teams to maintain alignment and execution.
  • Identifying reactor technology product risks, dependencies, and critical decisions and ensuring they are clearly owned and resolved.
  • Communicating reactor technology product priorities, technical considerations, decisions, and progress to company leadership and other stakeholders.
  • Supporting design reviews, customer engagements, partner discussions, procurement activities, and deployment planning.
  • Developing a strong understanding of the technical and regulatory environment affecting the product and incorporating relevant constraints into reactor product strategy.
  • Gathering feedback from testing, deployment, operations, customers, and partners to guide continued product improvement.
  • Establishing clear reactor technology product ownership and maintaining accountability for overall product outcomes throughout the product lifecycle.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of experience in product management, engineering, systems engineering, technical program management, or a similar role developing complex technical products.
  • Specific experience with nuclear reactor technology in areas such as design, safety, licensing, construction, or operations.
  • An engineering degree or equivalent experience working directly with engineered systems and technical development teams.
  • Demonstrated experience translating customer, business, or operational needs into product requirements and development priorities.
  • Experience guiding technical work from early-stage concepts toward validated, deployable solutions.
  • Ability to understand complex technical information and make informed tradeoffs involving performance, cost, schedule, risk, and customer value.
  • Experience coordinating work and decisions across multiple technical and non-technical functions.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Proven ability to operate independently in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.

Bonus Qualifications:

  • Experience developing hardware, energy systems, industrial equipment, or other complex physical products.
  • Experience as a practicing engineer or technical lead.
  • Experience with product development in regulated industries such as nuclear energy, aerospace, medical devices, or advanced manufacturing.
  • Experience developing business cases, product roadmaps, technical requirements, or deployment strategies.
  • Experience working with customers, commercial partners, vendors, or government stakeholders.
  • Familiarity with isotope production, nuclear fuel, advanced manufacturing, or related technologies.
  • Experience in a startup or rapidly scaling organization.

Competencies

Technical & Role-Specific Competencies

  • Strong technical judgment and the ability to understand complex engineered systems.
  • Ability to connect customer and business needs with feasible technical solutions.
  • Experience defining product requirements, development priorities, success criteria, and product roadmaps.
  • Strong structured problem-solving skills; able to break ambiguous opportunities into clear questions, workstreams, decisions, and deliverables.
  • Ability to evaluate and communicate tradeoffs among technical performance, safety, cost, schedule, licensing, manufacturability, operability, and commercial value.
  • Ability to guide products through multiple stages of maturity, from early opportunity identification and feasibility assessment through development and deployment.
  • Strong cross-functional leadership skills and the ability to build alignment without relying on direct authority.
  • Ability to communicate technical concepts clearly to engineering teams, company leadership, customers, partners, and other stakeholders.
  • Sound judgment regarding when additional analysis is necessary and when a product is sufficiently mature to proceed.
  • Ability to maintain focus on overall product outcomes while engaging deeply enough in technical details to support effective decisions.

Ways You Work

  • Highly organized and able to manage multiple priorities across teams.
  • Clear, concise written and verbal communicator.
  • Proactive, low-ego leader who takes ownership and follows through.
  • Comfortable navigating ambiguity and iterating as priorities evolve.
  • Curious and eager to develop a strong understanding of new technologies, markets, and customer needs.
  • Able to move comfortably between product strategy, technical detail, and execution planning.
  • Comfortable in a fast-paced, highly iterative startup environment.

Who you are:

A startup person: You aren't driven by titles or hierarchy, and prefer efficiency to excess process. You don't need or expect to have a lot of guidance but you enjoy working in a fast-paced team. If you prefer the culture and feel of a large organization, that is great, but you likely won’t enjoy working with us! There is plenty of important work and plenty of good opportunities with organizations like that.

Motivated: You are self-motivated. You bring an enthusiasm to the team, and imbue a sense of passion that goes beyond clocking in and clocking out. This isn’t about a fake or arbitrary “pieces of flair” mentality or lack of work-life balance! It is about being a part of the vision and feeling a part of reaching team goals.

A team-player: Oklo genuinely is a team. We aren’t about taking credit for ourselves, and we aren’t about pushing blame to others. We do incredible things because we work as a team.

An excellent communicator: We need a person who is not only technically competent but also a clear and upbeat communicator.

Creative: Being creative means that when things fall outside clear scopes or processes or problems arise without clear solutions, you are able to identify it as well as invent ways to solve a problem or fill a need without micromanagement. The successful person in this job will not only be creative, but also enjoy being creative and solving open-ended problems which may change day-by-day.

Detail-oriented: This focus is a big part of excellence, consistency, and quality. Excellent grammar and spelling matter for both good communication as well as the image of the company that we put forward.

About Oklo travel requirements:

Oklo requires remote employees to travel to headquarters (Santa Clara, CA) twice a quarter annually, based on business or team needs, including attendance at team meetings, off-sites, and other company events or gatherings. For the first two weeks of onboarding, employees are required to be in person at headquarters in Santa Clara, CA.

About Oklo compensation:

Salary: $140,000-$200,000

Oklo offers flexible time off, equity, bonuses, competitive pay, 401(k), health insurance (with employer contribution), HSA, FSA, flexible work hours, wellness credits, and other benefits.

This position may involve access to information subject to U.S. export control laws. Only applicants who meet the definition of a U.S. person under applicable laws may be eligible.

About Oklo Inc.: Oklo Inc. is developing fast fission power plants to deliver clean, reliable, and affordable energy at scale; establishing a domestic supply chain for critical radioisotopes; and advancing nuclear fuel recycling to convert nuclear waste into clean energy. Oklo was the first to receive a site use permit from the U.S. Department of Energy for a commercial advanced fission plant, was awarded fuel material from Idaho National Laboratory, and submitted the first custom combined license application for an advanced reactor to the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission. Oklo is also developing advanced fuel recycling technologies in collaboration with the U.S. Department of Energy and U.S. National Laboratories.

#CHOP: Oklo’s Values
Collaboration: We go further, together. We bring diverse perspectives, listen actively, and build trust through transparency and respect. We work across disciplines, sharing ownership to turn complex challenges into shared successes.
Humility: We are team players who act for the good of the company and for the world. We are focused on our mission, not personal recognition.
Ownership: We take pride in what we do and how we do it. We are proactive in finding solutions and see tasks through to completion. We are committed to delivering on our promises to provide clean, reliable, and affordable energy.
Pathfinding: We chart new ground where no path exists by approaching challenges with curiosity, courage, and creativity while navigating ambiguity.

Candidates should be aware that employment may be contingent upon successful completion of a drug screening, and employees may be subject to drug testing at any time in accordance with company policy and applicable laws.

All legitimate communications from our recruiting team— including application updates, interview requests, and job offers — will come exclusively from an @oklo.com email. Oklo will never ask for sensitive personal information, payments, or account credentials during the hiring process.

If you receive suspicious outreach or have concerns about the authenticity of any communication claiming to be from Oklo, please contact us through the official channels listed on our website.

The Opportunity:

Versant's Sports & Entertainment Digital Products division is seeking a Senior Site Reliability Engineer to help drive the reliability, scalability, and usability of internal developer platforms, tooling, and engineering workflows across a portfolio of industry-leading brands including Fandango, Fandango at Home, Rotten Tomatoes, SportsEngine, GolfNow, and GolfPass.

As a Senior Site Reliability Engineer, you will serve as a technical leader within the platform engineering ecosystem, helping shape engineering standards, drive reliability initiatives, and influence the evolution of developer experience capabilities across multiple product teams. You will partner across engineering, platform operations, and security teams to build scalable self-service capabilities, reduce operational friction, and enable teams to deliver software safely and efficiently.

Why This Role Matters:

Developer productivity is a force multiplier. By improving tooling, platform reliability, deployment workflows, and observability, this role directly impacts the speed, quality, and stability of product delivery across experiences that serve millions of sports and entertainment fans worldwide.

Work Environment:

This role is designated as fully remote and is expected to be performed from a non-Versant worksite, typically an employee's residence. While primarily remote, occasional in-person collaboration opportunities, team meetings, and business gatherings may occur throughout the year.

What You'll Do:

  • Lead the design, implementation, and operation of reliable internal developer platforms and self-service infrastructure provisioning capabilities.
  • Build, maintain, and optimize CI/CD pipelines, deployment workflows, and automation across GitHub Actions, Jenkins, ArgoCD, and related technologies.
  • Apply Site Reliability Engineering principles, including SLIs, SLOs, error budgets, and DORA metrics, to improve developer-facing systems and software delivery performance.
  • Drive adoption of engineering best practices, platform standards, and self-service capabilities across multiple engineering teams.
  • Develop and maintain golden paths, service templates, scaffolding tools, and standardized engineering workflows that accelerate software delivery and reduce operational complexity.
  • Improve local development environments, CLI tooling, environment provisioning, preview deployments, and ephemeral environments to enhance developer productivity.
  • Build observability solutions and dashboards that provide visibility into CI/CD health, deployment success, build performance, developer wait times, and platform reliability.
  • Partner with engineering teams to identify sources of operational toil and implement automation that improves efficiency, reliability, and developer experience.
  • Support cloud-native workloads and deployment patterns across containers, serverless technologies, and event-driven architectures.
  • Troubleshoot and resolve issues impacting developer workflows, including build failures, test instability, deployment issues, and environment drift.
  • Collaborate with Security and Platform Operations teams to embed secure-by-default controls and compliance guardrails into developer workflows.
  • Mentor engineers and provide technical guidance on platform architecture, automation strategies, observability, and cloud-native development practices.
  • Influence platform roadmaps and technical investments through data-driven recommendations and cross-functional collaboration.

What You Bring

  • 5+ years of experience in Site Reliability Engineering, Platform Engineering, Developer Experience, DevOps, or related engineering disciplines.
  • Experience building and supporting internal developer platforms, self-service infrastructure, or developer tooling.
  • Strong hands-on experience with CI/CD technologies, including GitHub Actions, Jenkins, ArgoCD, or similar platforms.
  • Experience with AWS cloud services and Infrastructure as Code tools such as Terraform, CloudFormation, or Pulumi.
  • Proficiency in scripting and automation using Python, Go, Bash, TypeScript, or similar languages.
  • Experience working with containerized environments and orchestration technologies including Docker, ECS, and Kubernetes.
  • Familiarity with observability practices and tools, including Datadog and application performance monitoring solutions.
  • Experience leading technical initiatives that span multiple teams or product domains.
  • Strong troubleshooting, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to create clear technical documentation, guides, and operational runbooks.
  • Experience supporting modern application frameworks and cloud-native architectures.
  • Willingness to participate in an on-call rotation supporting production systems and developer platforms.

Bonus Points:

  • AWS certifications such as Solutions Architect or DevOps Engineer.
  • Experience supporting high-scale consumer-facing digital platforms.
  • Familiarity with cloud cost optimization and FinOps practices.
  • Experience with developer portals, service catalogs, or internal platform products.

  • Trust by building reliable systems, following through on commitments, and prioritizing operational excellence.

  • Teamwork by partnering effectively across engineering, platform, security, and product teams to achieve shared goals.

  • Transparency by communicating clearly, documenting decisions, sharing knowledge, and promoting visibility into platform health and performance.

  • Agility by adapting quickly to changing priorities, embracing continuous improvement, and solving complex technical challenges.

  • Entrepreneurial Spirit by identifying opportunities for automation, innovation, and platform enhancements that improve developer productivity and business outcomes.

At Versant, you'll have the opportunity to work on technology platforms that power some of the most recognized brands in sports and entertainment. Your work will help millions of users discover content, stream experiences, connect with their communities, and engage with the activities they love.

In addition to meaningful work and opportunities for growth, Versant offers a comprehensive benefits package, a collaborative and inclusive culture, and the flexibility of a remote-first work environment. jobs.description:
POS-5690

About the Team

The Observability team owns the internal platform that gives every HubSpot engineer real visibility into how their systems behave in production. We build and operate the distributed tracing, metrics, alerting, and logging infrastructure that spans hundreds of microservices, billions of daily events, and thousands of engineers who depend on that signal to ship reliably.

We are now investing in the next generation of this platform. As HubSpot deploys AI agents and ML-powered features across the product, the team is building the tracing and telemetry primitives that make it possible to understand, debug, and trust what those systems are doing in production. This is greenfield, technically interesting work at a scale few companies operate at and we are looking for a Principal Engineer to help lead it.

About the Role

We are seeking a Principal Software Engineer to be the technical anchor for HubSpot’s Observability platform. This role sits at the intersection of large-scale distributed systems, developer platform design, and AI observability. A big part of this role is working horizontally across a large engineering org and setting patterns and standards that make it easier for teams to instrument, alert on, and reason about their services. You will also shape how we trace and understand our growing fleet of AI agents and ML systems in production: a technically distinct and increasingly critical problem.

Key Expectations

  • Observability Platform Architecture: Define the patterns and evolution of HubSpot’s core telemetry platform — distributed tracing, metrics, and structured logging — at a scale that spans hundreds of services and billions of daily events. Set the standards for how instrumentation is done across a large, polyglot engineering organization.
  • AI & Agentic Observability: Lead the technical strategy for tracing and understanding AI agents and ML-powered systems in production. Define the primitives, telemetry standards, and debugging workflows that help product engineers understand what their models and agents are doing — and build trust in those systems over time. This is greenfield and consequential work.
  • High-Cardinality, High-Throughput Systems: Architect telemetry pipelines and storage systems that handle high-cardinality data at high throughput without blowing up cost or query latency. Make principled tradeoffs between sampling, fidelity, retention, and developer ergonomics.
  • Hands-on, High-Leverage Builder: Ship production code. Lead design reviews and take high-impact initiatives end-to-end, from prototype to production system at scale. Stay close to the systems you build and be the person who can debug the hardest problems when they surface.
  • Developer Experience & Adoption: Design the instrumentation APIs and libraries that product engineers reach for, making correct observability the path of least resistance. Drive OpenTelemetry adoption across a large, polyglot codebase. Build the tooling that turns raw telemetry into actionable signal for teams operating at speed.
  • Production Intelligence & Reliability Patterns: Define patterns for SLO/SLI design, alerting philosophy, and how teams graduate from reactive to proactive incident response. Push for simplicity in a domain that wants to get complicated, and consistency where tooling can drift across a large organization.
  • Technical Leadership & Influence: Partner with infrastructure, platform, and product engineering teams to understand their signal gaps and close them. Influence technical strategy alongside engineering leadership, translating observability constraints and opportunities into product and operational decisions. Mentor senior engineers and tech leads, driving thoughtful design decisions and capturing learnings from major incidents and large-scale migrations.

What You Bring

  • Platform-Builder Experience: Proven experience building observability or telemetry tooling for internal engineering teams, rather than simply consuming it. You understand how to architect developer platforms that serve thousands of engineers across a large organization, backed by deep operational instincts and hard-earned expertise.
  • Telemetry Systems Depth: Deep expertise navigating trade-offs in telemetry pipeline design across high-cardinality data, dynamic sampling, query latency, retention economics, and data fidelity. Strong technical fluency with OpenTelemetry, distributed tracing engines, metric backends, and large-scale log ingestion infrastructure.
  • Incident Automation & Operational Excellence: Proven track record linking telemetry signals directly to automated operational workflows. You have designed architecture for real-time telemetry triggers that power automated remediation, dynamic runbooks, or AI-assisted root-cause diagnosis across microservices environments.

Why This Role, Why Now

HubSpot is scaling fast — more engineers, more microservices, more AI systems running in production — and the Observability platform is at an inflection point. The foundations are solid, but the next phase requires a different kind of investment: rethinking cardinality economics, making OpenTelemetry the default across a large polyglot org, and building an entirely new layer of AI tracing that doesn’t yet exist.

This Principal Engineer will have a direct line of sight from the architecture they design to the engineering outcomes we measure: incident response times, adoption rates, developer satisfaction, and the trust that product teams place in their production signal. The AI observability layer in particular is greenfield — there is no playbook to follow, which is exactly what makes this the right moment for the right person.

If you want to build the platform that helps thousands of engineers understand what their systems are doing — including systems powered by AI that are genuinely hard to see inside — this is the role.

Pay & Benefits

The cash compensation below includes base salary, on-target commission for employees in eligible roles, and annual bonus targets under HubSpot’s bonus plan for eligible roles. In addition to cash compensation, some roles are eligible to participate in HubSpot’s equity plan to receive restricted stock units (RSUs). Some roles may also be eligible for overtime pay. Individual compensation packages are tailored to your skills, experience, qualifications, and other job-related reasons.

This resource will help guide how we recommend thinking about the range you see. Learn more about HubSpot’s compensation philosophy.

Benefits are also an important piece of your total compensation package. Explore the benefits and perks HubSpot offers to help employees grow better.

At HubSpot, fair compensation practices aren’t just about checking off the box for legal compliance. It’s about living out our value of transparency with our employees, candidates, and community.

$313,800—$502,080 USD

At HubSpot, we value both flexibility and connection. Whether you’re a Remote employee or work from the Office, we want you to start your journey here by building strong connections with your team and peers. If you are joining our Engineering team, you will be required to attend a regional HubSpot office for in-person onboarding. If you join our broader Product team, you’ll also attend other in-person events, such as your Product Group Summit and other gatherings, to continue building on those connections.

HubSpot (NYSE: HUBS) is an AI-powered customer platform with all the software, integrations, and resources customers need to connect marketing, sales, and service. HubSpot's connected platform enables businesses to grow faster by focusing on what matters most: customers.

POSITION OVERVIEW
The Senior GIS Analyst transforms spatial, demographic, labor, and real estate data into insights that help Stream professionals and clients make better location and real estate decisions.

Working across Stream’s national platform, this individual will lead sophisticated site selection, relocation, workforce, and market analyses while developing compelling maps, dashboards, and visual narratives that support business development, client strategy, and decision-making.

This role sits at the intersection of analytics, technology, and storytelling. The successful candidate will combine advanced GIS expertise with strong business judgment and the ability to translate complex analysis into clear, actionable recommendations for brokers, clients, and internal stakeholders.

The role reports to the Director of Business and Location Intelligence, collaborates closely with local market teams across the country, and is designed as a remote U.S. position.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Location Intelligence & Advanced Analytics

  • Lead complex analyses including site selection, relocation studies, labor and workforce analytics, demographic evaluations, and market assessments.
  • Perform drive-time, distance, trade-area, and origin-destination (OD) analyses to support real estate strategy and client needs.
  • Develop weighted suitability models, spatial scoring methodologies, and other analytical frameworks to identify and compare optimal locations.
  • Integrate and analyze data from Esri, Lightcast, commercial real estate platforms, public data sources, and client-provided datasets.
  • Evaluate data sources, assumptions, and methodologies to ensure analyses are accurate, defensible, reproducible, and appropriate for client use.

Client Strategy & Data Storytelling

  • Produce high-quality maps, dashboards, StoryMaps, reports, presentations, and other client-ready deliverables.
  • Translate analytical findings into clear, visually compelling narratives and recommendations that support leasing, investment, development, and location decisions.
  • Partner with brokers and business teams to determine how spatial insights can strengthen client strategy, pitches, pursuits, and business development.
  • Ensure deliverables are polished, accurate, consistent with Stream’s brand standards, and tailored to the needs of the audience.

Business Partnership & Advisory

  • Serve as a location intelligence advisor to brokers, marketing, research, and other business teams by helping define the analytical question, select the appropriate methodology, and interpret results.
  • Act as a subject matter expert on GIS capabilities, spatial analysis, data sources, and location intelligence methodologies.
  • Consult with stakeholders to scope projects, identify the right analytical approach, and translate technical findings into business value.
  • Contribute strategic perspective on how geospatial intelligence can improve client decision-making and differentiate Stream in the marketplace.

Standards, Automation & Innovation

  • Establish and maintain GIS standards, templates, methodologies, and best practices across the national platform.
  • Identify opportunities to improve and automate GIS workflows, analytical models, and recurring deliverables using Python, ModelBuilder, and other tools.
  • Explore and apply AI, automation, and emerging analytical technologies to accelerate research, analysis, and visualization while maintaining appropriate quality controls.
  • Share knowledge, methodologies, and best practices with GIS and analytical resources across the organization.
  • Stay current with emerging tools, datasets, and trends in GIS, location intelligence, commercial real estate, and spatial analytics.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Geography, GIS, Urban Planning, Economics, Data Analytics, or a related field; equivalent experience will be considered.
  • 5+ years of progressively responsible experience in GIS, location intelligence, geospatial analytics, or a related discipline.
  • Demonstrated experience leading advanced site selection, market, demographic, workforce, or spatial analyses in a fast-paced, client-driven environment.
  • Experience translating analytical findings into recommendations for business or client audiences.
  • Portfolio or examples of advanced geospatial analysis and data visualization preferred.

REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE & SKILLS

  • Advanced proficiency in the Esri platform, including ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Online, Experience Builder, and Dashboards.
  • Strong experience with site selection, demographic analysis, labor and workforce analytics, and spatial analysis in a client-facing environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to build and interpret suitability models and other multi-variable spatial analyses.
  • Expertise in creating client-ready maps, visualizations, dashboards, reports, and presentations.
  • Ability to work with large, complex datasets from multiple sources and assess data quality, assumptions, and limitations.
  • Strong communication and consulting skills, with the ability to translate technical analysis into clear business recommendations.
  • Experience with Python, ModelBuilder, or other GIS automation tools preferred.
  • Familiarity with commercial real estate, corporate location strategy, economic development, or consulting environments strongly preferred.

jobs.excerpt: Astrana Health builds the technology that lets physician groups deliver value-based care: the systems that enables physicians to deliver higher quality care and keeps its payers, and its partners in sync.
jobs.description:
Astrana Health builds the technology that lets physician groups deliver value-based care: the systems that enables physicians to deliver higher quality care and keeps its payers, and its partners in sync. Our engineers work on anything from eligibility, claims, and authorizations data, integrations with payer and provider systems, clinical integrations, provider-facing tools, and the data platform that ties them together.
The pace varies with the work. Some of it is fast iteration with real users. Some of it touches PHI, billing, or clinical decisions and has to be right the first time. A staff engineer sets the example for knowing which is which, and for building systems that make it safe to move fast where fast is appropriate. We expect engineers to work across the whole stack. This is a hands-on role: most of a staff engineer's time is spent designing and building, and the rest is spent making other engineers' building better.
As a Staff Engineer you own a technical domain that cuts across product surfaces: the data platform, the integration layer, the clinical data model, or the shape of our services. You choose the structure everyone else builds inside, you own the consequences of those choices over years, and you are accountable for the technical quality of decisions made by people you do not manage. Your judgment is a company asset, and we expect you to use it out loud.

Our Values:
  • Put Patients First
  • Empower Entrepreneurial Provider and Care Teams
  • Operate with Integrity & Excellence
  • Be Innovative
  • Work As One Team

What You'll Do

  • Set technical direction for your domain: what we build on, what we migrate off, and what we deliberately tolerate.
  • Make and defend architecture and infrastructure choices on cost, operational burden, hiring implications, and exit cost as well as capability.
  • Build the hard core of new systems yourself, and the reference implementations and tooling that let other engineers move fast inside them.
  • Evolve existing systems: decomposition, strangler patterns, deprecations, and migrations off old paths that actually finish.
  • Design for our failure domains. Know what happens when a partner feed dies, a vendor deprecates an API, or a region goes down, and what the recovery path is.
  • Own the shape of our data. Decide how eligibility, claims, clinical, and quality data are modeled, joined, and served for both product features and analytics, and make it easy for engineers and analysts to get trustworthy answers out of it.
  • Set cross-cutting standards (schema conventions, service templates, CI/CD, environment and test-data strategy) and get them adopted.
  • Turn recurring classes of incidents into structural fixes.
  • Manage technical debt as a portfolio: what we carry, what it costs us, and what we pay down next.
  • Grow the senior bench: run technical interviews, calibrate hiring and promotion decisions, and develop senior engineers so more of them operate at a staff level.
  • Say the unpopular thing, early and clearly, to engineering and non-engineering leadership alike.

Qualifications

  • 8+ years of professional software engineering experience, including years owning systems that other engineers build on.
  • Four-year undergraduate degree in Computer Science, Mathematics, Physics, or Engineering. Rare exceptions for outstanding experience.
  • Full-stack experience. You have owned systems from the data layer through the API to the UI, and building is the bulk of your work.
  • Strong TypeScript and strong SQL, with deep experience in data modeling and data-heavy systems.
  • Data and analytics savvy. You have designed data for both transactional and analytical use, and you can look at a report and tell whether the numbers are plausible.
  • Production experience with React.
  • Docker and container-based deployment.
  • Hands-on ownership of infrastructure on at least one major public cloud (Azure, AWS, or GCP), including the cost and operational tradeoffs.
  • Strong proficiency with AI development tools such as coding agents and assistants. You use them to multiply your own and your team's output, hold their output to the same standard as any other code, have clear judgment about where they help and where they create risk, and can set that standard for other engineers.
Preferred Qualifications
  • Database modeling and migration frameworks such as Drizzle, Prisma, SQLAlchemy, or Alembic, including experience choosing one and setting conventions for a team.
  • Depth across more than one of Azure, AWS, and GCP, including cloud IAM, role design, and least-privilege access at the organization level.
  • Python.
  • Experience designing LLM-driven systems in production: tool use, retrieval-augmented generation, evaluation, cost control, and safety.
  • Healthcare data experience: eligibility, claims, clinical data, HL7/FHIR, or payer/provider integrations at multi-tenant scale.
  • Experience with HIPAA compliance, PHI handling, and audit requirements in system design.

Environmental Job Requirements and Working Conditions

  • Remote, US based position - with preference for candidates based in the greater Los Angeles area.

Sobre a BigDataCorp

A BigDataCorp é a maior datatech da América Latina, e democratiza, desde 2013, o acesso aos dados, aumentando possibilidades e certezas em um mundo repleto de incertezas.

Somos pioneiros na captura, estruturação, armazenamento e distribuição de dados no Brasil. Nosso processo é único. Já nascemos adequados à LGPD e às demais regulamentações, garantindo a origem das informações fornecidas, obtidas sempre de forma ética.

Sobre a área e a vaga

Customer Success: O time de Customer Success é, como o nome indica, responsável por garantir a satisfação e sucesso dos clientes em sua jornada de uso dos produtos da BigDataCorp. Isso inclui apoiá-los na integração das soluções, entender o negócio dos clientes para sugerir novas soluções ou melhorias nos processos, e ajudar nas interações entre os clientes e os times internos da empresa, construindo relacionamentos duradouros.

Sobre o Estágio na BigDataCorp

O Estágio na BigDataCorp tem como objetivo formar os futuros líderes e especialistas da empresa. Para isso, buscamos atrair e formar pessoas, desenvolvendo seu potencial e apoiando o seu crescimento dentro da organização. Para que isso aconteça, promovemos uma jornada completa de aprendizado: da teoria à experimentação prática, nossas pessoas estagiárias estão a todo momento absorvendo e compartilhando aprendizados e conhecimentos, entendendo, de fato, como a empresa funciona, seus objetivos e desafios reais. A pessoa escolhida trabalhará 4 horas por dia, totalizando a carga horária semanal de 20 horas, por um período de 12 a 24 meses. Como pessoa estagiária, você será conectada a um gestor e terá todo o suporte para o desenvolvimento da sua carreira. Aqui fornecemos todas as ferramentas necessárias para que você se sinta apoiado e se desenvolva em um ambiente real. Além de trabalhar em um projeto que fará diferença para nosso negócio, você terá a oportunidade de se envolver com os Biggers, potencializando seu desenvolvimento pessoal e profissional, e expandindo sua rede de contatos.

O que vai fazer no dia a dia:

  • Acompanhar a jornada do cliente desde o onboarding e primeiros passos na plataforma;
  • Entender o objetivo, contexto e caso de uso de cada cliente;
  • Apoiar o cliente na utilização das soluções, orientando sobre funcionalidades e possibilidades aderentes às suas necessidades;
  • Acompanhar integração, utilização e evolução do cliente ao longo da jornada;
  • Realizar follow-ups e manter os registros e etapas atualizados no CRM;
  • Identificar dificuldades, dúvidas, baixa utilização ou oportunidades de maior aproveitamento da plataforma;
  • Apoiar na identificação de novos casos de uso e oportunidades de expansão dentro da base;
  • Trabalhar em conjunto com os demais integrantes de CS e Comercial para garantir uma experiência próxima, ágil e orientada à geração de valor;
  • Desenvolver continuamente conhecimento sobre produtos, dados, soluções e possibilidades de aplicação da BigDataCorp.

Requirements

Habilidades necessárias:

  • Estar cursando ensino superior em Administração, Marketing, Comunicação Social, Economia, Ciências Contábeis, Relações Internacionais, Relações Públicas, Administração, Engenharia de Produção, Engenharia Civil ou áreas correlatas;

  • Facilidade e interesse em comunicação com diferentes públicos;
  • Capacidade de elaborar textos claros e objetivos;
  • Afinidade e interesse por tecnologia, soluções digitais, experiência do cliente e dados;
  • Curiosidade e facilidade para aprender novas ferramentas e produtos;
  • Capacidade analítica para compreender necessidades e casos de uso dos clientes;

Regional Clinical Affairs Manager, Electrophysiology

Working at Abbott

At Abbott, you can do work that matters, grow, and learn, care for yourself and your family, be your true self, and live a full life. You’ll also have access to:

The Opportunity

In Abbott’s Electrophysiology (EP) business, we’re advancing the treatment of heart disease through breakthrough medical technologies in atrial fibrillation, allowing people to restore their health and get on with their lives.

The EP Regional Clinical Affairs Manager is a field-based, strategic role in the clinical research space. Key responsibilities include clinical and strategic support to the Clinical Affairs Organization, with a specific focus on BU technologies and therapy areas. This role directly impacts key clinical trial and new technology approval timelines through study acceleration and enrollment driving efforts. Specific priorities include relationship development with Key Opinion Leaders (KOLs), leading new clinical site launches, identifying new clinical research partners, and developing strategic plans for research partnerships within territory.

  • Mentor and support FCS staff, with opportunity for direct-report management.

This is a project-based opportunity on an AI training platform. No fixed hours, no commitment beyond what fits your schedule. You talk, you get paid.

We're looking for bilingual speakers to record short, casual voice clips where they naturally mix English with Chinese - the way they'd actually talk in real life. No script, no scenarios, just you talking about your day, your opinions, whatever comes naturally.

Do you switch between English and Chinese mid-sentence without even thinking about it? Rant about your day, discuss your favorite show, think out loud with different languages - say it exactly how you'd say it to a friend. What if you could get paid just for recording it?

Category: Legal

Job Description: Automations and AI Integration Expert

PERMANENT AU DAYSHIFT
Remote/WFH - Philippines
Reporting to Principal / Managing Lawyer / Operations Lead, as directed

VA Rate : $15AUD per hour (Negotiable)

Role purpose:
Build, integrate and maintain practical automation and AI systems that reduce manual work, improve accuracy, protect confidentiality and support better operational decision-making across the firm.

About the role

We are seeking a highly capable Automations and AI Integration Expert to design, build and deploy scalable automation systems for a professional services environment. This is a hands-on builder role, not a passive support role. The successful candidate will identify inefficiencies, convert them into practical automation opportunities, and deliver reliable tools that improve speed, consistency and accountability.

The role will work closely with leadership and team members across operations, client service, finance, marketing and document workflows. The objective is to implement secure, well-documented automation and AI-enabled systems that reduce repetitive manual work while preserving professional judgment, confidentiality and quality
control.

Key objectives
  • Identify and automate repetitive operational, administrative, reporting and document-management tasks.
  • Integrate AI and large language model tools into controlled workflows that improve productivity without compromising confidentiality, accuracy or professional oversight.
  • Connect core business systems so information is captured once, reused safely and reported clearly.
  • Build practical internal tools, dashboards and workflow automations that are easy for staff to use and maintain.
  • Create a disciplined automation environment with clear documentation, access controls, testing and ongoing monitoring.
Key responsibilities
AI integration and automation
  • Design and implement automation workflows to eliminate repetitive manual tasks and reduce avoidableerrors.
  • Integrate AI tools and large language models, including OpenAI, Claude, Gemini and similar platforms, into appropriate business processes.
  • Build intelligent solutions for document processing, drafting support, reporting, internal communications, task triage and knowledge retrieval.
  • Develop AI-powered assistants, chatbots, intake tools and workflow automations subject to privacy, confidentiality and quality-control requirements.
  • Create prompt libraries, reusable workflow templates and governance processes for safe and consistent AI use.
Systems and software development
  • Build and maintain internal tools, web apps and automation systems that solve real operational problems.
  • Develop APIs and integrate multiple platforms, including CRM, project management, email, finance, marketing and document-management systems.
  • Customize and extend existing systems to improve efficiency, usability and reporting.
  • Own the full development lifecycle, including scoping, planning, development, testing, deployment, documentation and optimization.
  • Troubleshoot integration issues and maintain reliable automations with appropriate alerting and error- handling.
Workflow automation and integrations
  • Create end-to-end workflows using Zapier, Make, n8n, or comparable automation platforms.
  • Connect business systems such as email, calendars, CRM, file storage, task management, accounting and client communication platforms.
  • Optimize automation pipelines for reliability, security, scalability and maintainability.
  • Document workflows clearly so they can be audited, improved and maintained over time.
  • Support onboarding and offboarding workflows connected to user access, permissions and automation dependencies.
Data, reporting and dashboards
  • Build dashboards and automated reporting systems that give leadership clear visibility over key metrics andworkflow performance.
  • Design data pipelines to track operational data, KPIs, lead sources, task completion, bottlenecks and performance trends.
  • Support data-driven decision-making by producing accurate, timely and understandable reports.
  • Improve data quality by reducing duplicate entry, inconsistent records and manual reporting errors.
Security, privacy and governance
  • Apply best practices in data security, privacy, access control and system integrity.
  • Ensure automations are designed with appropriate human review points, particularly where legal, financial, client or confidential information is involved.
  • Maintain documentation of tools, credentials, dependencies, data flows and known risks.
  • Recommend sensible governance for AI use, including prompt standards, recordkeeping, review processes and restrictions on sensitive information.
Required skills and experience
  • 3-5+ years experience in automation, software development, systems integration or a closely related role.
  • Strong proficiency in at least one programming language, preferably Python or JavaScript/Node.js.

  • Experience integrating APIs and working with RESTful services, webhooks and data transformations.
  • Familiarity with AI/LLM tools, including OpenAI, Claude, Gemini and prompt design.
  • Experience with databases, including SQL or NoSQL, and sound data-handling practices.
  • Ability to diagnose business problems and convert them into simple, practical technical solutions.
  • Excellent communication skills, including the ability to explain technical concepts clearly to non-technical users.

Desirable skills and experience
  • Experience in legal, professional services, SaaS, BPO, outsourcing or service-based industries.

Success measures

  • Automations are reliable, documented and capable of being maintained without unnecessary dependency on one person.

jobs.excerpt: This position has a full salary range of $68,500 - $108,000 per year with eligibility for commission.
jobs.description:
This position has a full salary range of $68,500 - $108,000 per year with eligibility for commission. Starting salary is based on a variety of factors including, but not limited to, geographic location and experience. The target hiring range for this role is $68,500 - $85,000.

Candidates for this role must live in a major metropolitan area.

Role Overview:

The Business Development Executive will drive new revenue for Dirty Hands by selling our merchandising services to natural CPG brands. This is a hunting role. You will build your own pipeline, run discovery conversations that uncover what a brand actually needs, and move those opportunities from proposal to close.

Above all, this is an outbound role. That means creating a steady flow of your own opportunities through cold outreach, networking, store-checks, and events. The brands you close will be the ones you went out and found.

The services you sell help natural CPG brands win on the shelf. Dirty Hands is a known and respected name in the space, backed by real relationships at the store level, so you are reaching out with credibility behind you rather than starting cold every time. Success is measured on one thing, revenue closed. A healthy pipeline is how you get there, but what counts is what gets signed. This role is a strong fit if you have a track record of creating your own opportunities and carrying them through to the close.

This is a remote role. Regular team and company meetings keep everyone aligned, but you will need to be self-motivated about staying connected the rest of the time. It suits someone who has sold this way before and knows how to stay productive without an office around them.

What You’ll Own:

Prospecting & Pipeline Generation

  • Build and sustain a self-sourced pipeline through cold outreach, email, networking, store-checks, and industry events, without waiting for leads to be handed over.
  • Conduct market research to find emerging brands and untapped opportunities that fit Dirty Hands.
  • Represent Dirty Hands at trade shows and networking events, building relationships that convert into qualified opportunities.
  • Use store-level data and shelf photos captured by our field teams, along with SPINS data, to surface opportunities and show prospective brands what is happening with their products at retail.

Discovery & Selling

  • Lead discovery conversations that uncover a brand's goals, gaps, and buying criteria before proposing a solution.
  • Translate what you learn in discovery into tailored pitches and case studies that show the value of Dirty Hands' merchandising services.
  • Deliver sales presentations, pulling in data, case studies, and internal experts when they strengthen the pitch.

Follow-up, Proposals & Closing

  • Own the full deal cycle from first meeting through proposal, negotiation, and signed contract.
  • Develop and present proposals that clearly connect Dirty Hands' services to the outcomes a brand is trying to reach.
  • Drive consistent follow-up so opportunities keep moving and do not stall between stages.
  • Negotiate and close agreements that work for both the brand and Dirty Hands.

Expansion & Internal Partnership

  • Grow existing accounts by spotting new opportunities and turning strong relationships into new revenue.
  • Coordinate with strategy and merchandising leadership, pulling them in to shape offers and keeping them informed as deals develop.
  • Contribute to lead generation campaigns and pass what you are seeing in the market back to the team.

Pipeline Management & Reporting

  • Keep opportunities accurate and current in our CRM so the pipeline and forecast reflect reality.
  • Report on sales activity and progress against targets on a regular cadence.
  • Stay current on industry trends, retailer programs, competitor offerings, and Dirty Hands' internal programs to refine how you sell.

What We’re Looking For:

Three areas matter most for this role: prospecting and creating your own opportunities, running discovery and selling, and moving deals through follow-up, proposals, and close. Strength across all three is what we look for first, so be ready to show real, specific experience in each.

Experience

  • 3+ years of experience in a business development or sales role. Experience within the natural CPG industry at a brand, broker, or merchandiser is a plus.
  • A track record of prospecting and creating your own opportunities, not just working inbound or assigned leads.
  • Demonstrated success in discovery and selling, turning what you learn about a brand into a pitch that lands.
  • A proven record of carrying deals through follow-up, proposals, and to a signed close, consistently against a target.
  • Experience selling services or solutions, not only products, into CPG brands is strongly preferred.
  • Prior experience selling in a remote, self-directed role is strongly preferred. This is not a first remote job; you should already know how to run your own pipeline and stay disciplined without in-person structure.
  • An existing network of brand or retailer relationships in natural CPG is a strong plus.

Core Strengths

  • Self-motivated and resilient, able to keep building your own pipeline through the grind and the rejection that outbound selling involves.
  • A genuine listener who uncovers what a brand actually needs before pitching a solution.
  • Persistent through follow-up and negotiation, keeping deals moving without letting relationships go cold.
  • Clear and persuasive with the people who own the decision, from a founder or CEO to a VP of sales, and able to make the financial case when a CFO is in the room.
  • Disciplined about where you spend your time, and organized enough to run several opportunities at once without dropping any.

Technical Skills

  • Comfortable working in a CRM to manage your pipeline, track activity, and report on progress. We use HubSpot; experience with it is a plus.
  • Able to work with syndicated and store-level data, including SPINS, and turn it into a clear, persuasive case for a brand.
  • Confident building polished pitches and proposals that hold up in front of brand decision-makers.
  • Proficient in Google Workspace or Microsoft Office.

Travel & Physical Requirements

  • Willingness to travel up to 12 weeks per year to attend trade shows, client meetings, time in the field with our merchandising teams, and other in-person events.
  • Able to work in a seated position for extended periods of time.

Benefits:

  • Competitive pay with eligibility for yearly merit-based wage increases.
  • Eligibility for commission.
  • Comprehensive benefits package including partially company-paid medical insurance, and fully company-paid dental, vision, life and disability insurance.
  • FREE First Stop Health: virtual care and mental health coverage.
  • Three weeks of paid time off per year. In addition to paid time off, 9 paid holidays and one additional floating holiday.
  • 401k plan with company match.
  • Use of company-owned devices to complete assigned tasks.
  • An exceptional company culture with opportunities for engagement and growth.

Posting close date: 10/1/2026.

Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice due to our business, industry, and/or market changes.

Our fully remote team of strategists, analysts, engineers, and designers works across industries including eCommerce, fintech, nonprofit, and hospitality. Our proprietary platform, Iris, unifies analytics, testing, creative, and roadmaps in one system.

Cro Metrics is hiring a production and brand designer to support paid media, lifecycle marketing (email/SMS), and website creative across our client roster.

You'll take briefs, hypotheses, and creative direction and turn them into on-brand, production-ready creative, including paid social and display ads, email and SMS campaigns, landing pages, and experiment variations. This is a production and brand execution role, not a UX/product design role: you're not wireframing user flows or owning journey mapping, you're producing high-quality, on-brand creative fast, across every channel a growth marketing agency touches.

With more experience, the role has room to grow into client-facing creative leadership and brand systems ownership, but the core of the job is high-quality production at pace.

What You'll Do

  • Produce paid media ad creative for Meta, Google, LinkedIn, and programmatic, to platform specs.
  • Design email and SMS creative for email platforms (Klaviyo, Braze, Iterable, or similar), including responsive layouts and template systems.
  • Build landing pages and A/B test variations from written briefs and hypotheses.
  • Work within established brand systems and guidelines, keeping every deliverable visually consistent across clients.
  • Use AI tools throughout your workflow, including ideation, asset generation, ad variants, and iteration. Manage multiple concurrent projects and clients, communicating proactively about capacity and timelines.
  • Prepare clean, well-organized files for handoff to developers, media buyers, or lifecycle marketers.
  • Explain the reasoning behind your creative choice, such as how a deliverable addresses the brief, hypothesis, or brand.

With more experience, you may also lead creative for complex multi-channel campaigns, present concepts directly to clients, and contribute to evolving brand systems across channels.

What We're Looking For

  • 3–6+ years experience designing for brand, paid media, lifecycle/email, or similar.
  • Hands-on experience designing paid social/display ad creative to platform specs.
  • Hands-on experience designing email and/or SMS creative for an ESP.
  • Strong Figma proficiency: fast, clean, well-organized files.
  • A portfolio showing production-quality work across paid media, email/SMS, and web.
  • Comfort working within existing brand systems rather than designing from scratch.
  • Active, demonstrated use of AI tools in your daily design workflow.
  • Self-directed, detail-oriented, and reliable under deadline.

AI is a hard requirement, not a preference. This role requires active, demonstrated use of AI tools in your daily workflow. You'll be expected to build and manage brand-specific AI agents that the team can use at scale. You'll be asked to show concrete AI-integrated workflows and agent-building experience during the interview process. Candidates who cannot demonstrate practical AI tool use and agent creation will not advance.

Nice to Haves

  • Experience at a CRO, experimentation, or growth marketing agency.
  • Familiarity with A/B testing or personalization platforms (Optimizely, VWO, or similar).
  • Basic motion/video ad creative experience.
  • Bonus points for experience in digital, UX or UI design.

What Success Looks Like

  • You consistently deliver polished, on-brand, test-ready creative across paid media, email/SMS, and web, on time and with minimal revision cycles.
  • Strategists, media buyers, and lifecycle marketers trust your output and view you as a reliable production partner.
  • You manage a steady cadence of deliverables across multiple clients and channels without quality dipping.
  • Your files are clean and easy for teammates to work from.

Compensation

This is a 1099 independent contractor position. The hourly rate for this role ranges from $45–$70, depending on qualifications, relevant experience, and the specific scope of work assigned. As an independent contractor, you will be responsible for your own tax withholdings, and this engagement does not include employee benefits (e.g., health insurance, paid time off, or retirement contributions).

jobs.excerpt: At Counterpart Health, we are transforming healthcare and improving patient care with our innovative primary care tool, Counterpart Assistant.
jobs.description:
At Counterpart Health, we are transforming healthcare and improving patient care with our innovative primary care tool, Counterpart Assistant. By supporting Primary Care Physicians (PCPs), we are able to deliver improved outcomes to our patients at a lower cost through early diagnosis and longitudinal care management of chronic conditions.

We're looking for a Director of Engineering to lead our Data Products pillar, serving as the technical engine for Counterpart Health's (CPH) clinical-data foundation. You will own the technical strategy and execution for the Data Products roadmap—encompassing clinical data ingestion, canonical data modeling, and ingestion scalability—while building scalable, reusable data capabilities that serve as a foundational platform for driving clinical insight generation. You will own the technical strategy for our Data Products platform—ensuring our clinical data foundations (using standards like FHIR, LOINC, and RxNorm) effectively drive business outcomes. You will serve as a critical leader and partner to the VP of Engineering and cross-functional leaders in Product, Data Science, and Design.

As a Director of Engineering, Data Products, you will:

  • Own the Data Products technical roadmap, canonical data modeling, and ingestion scalability.
  • Manage and optimize the clinical data ingestion pipeline.
  • Oversee the scaling of customer data onboarding processes and the continuous improvement of data hygiene, canonical storage standards, and observability and monitoring of the data pipelines.
  • Enable shared funnel visibility across the organization and support the development of a robust enterprise reporting framework.
  • Drive the adoption of an AI-powered Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC), leveraging AI tools to accelerate coding, testing, and deployment processes while maintaining stringent code quality and security standards.

Success in this role looks like:

  • Successfully achieving improved clinical data coverage and freshness targets across all patient populations.
  • Predictable and repeatable multi-customer scaling with standardized playbooks for rapid data readiness.
  • Broad adoption of the Data Products platform and its capabilities
  • Data infrastructure is robust, stable, and serves as a reliable source of truth during rapid organizational growth and customer expansion.

You should get in touch if:

  • You possess 10+ years of engineering experience with a deep focus on building high-scale data platforms, distributed systems, and interoperability standards (e.g., FHIR, CCDA).
  • Proven track record in managing and scaling engineering teams that handle data-heavy workloads and complex clinical data pipelines.
  • Proven experience leading cross-functional teams of engineers to deliver complex software in regulated environments.
  • Experience implementing and scaling AI-assisted development workflows (e.g., AI code assistants, automated testing, or AI-driven SDLC) to improve engineering productivity.
  • Demonstrated experience building and managing engineering systems in highly regulated healthcare environments, with a strong operational understanding of HIPAA and SOC 2 compliance requirements.
  • Passionate about the healthcare sector and committed to utilizing technical expertise to drive meaningful improvements in patient outcomes.
  • Deeply familiar with the inherent complexities and lack of standardization in clinical datasets, with a proactive focus on enhancing data integrity.
  • Motivated by intricate technical challenges and dedicated to architecting pragmatic, high-quality engineering solutions through continuous intellectual exploration.
  • Thrives in dynamic, high-growth environments, demonstrating the ability to navigate ambiguity and align technical priorities with overarching strategic objectives.
  • Action-oriented leader who assumes full ownership of system sustainability, willing to address operational gaps to ensure the team achieves its delivery milestones.

Engineering Leadership Skills:

  • Proven track record of directly hiring, mentoring, and developing engineering managers, Tech Leads (TLs), and Principal Engineers (PELs).
  • Demonstrated ability to cultivate a high-performance engineering culture focused on velocity, quality, and psychological safety.
  • Experience leading organizational change, including structural re-orgs and process evolution.
  • Strong proficiency in strategic resource allocation, capacity planning, and managing technical debt in a fast-paced product environment.
  • Exceptional stakeholder management skills, with the ability to translate complex technical constraints into clear, actionable business strategies (e.g., impact on HEDIS/RADV outcomes) for non-technical leadership.

Benefits Overview:

  • Financial Well-Being: Our commitment to attracting and retaining top talent begins with a competitive base salary and equity opportunities. Additionally, we offer a performance-based bonus program and regular compensation reviews to recognize and reward exceptional contributions.
  • Physical Well-Being: We prioritize the health and well-being of our employees and their families by offering comprehensive group medical coverage that include coverage for hospitalization, outpatient care, optical services, and dental benefits.
  • Mental Well-Being: We understand the importance of mental health in fostering productivity and maintaining work-life balance. To support this, we offer initiatives such as No-Meeting Fridays, company holidays, access to mental health resources, and a generous annual leave policy. Additionally, we embrace a remote-first culture that supports collaboration and flexibility, allowing our team members to thrive from any location.
  • Professional Development: We are committed to developing our talent professionally. We offer learning programs, mentorship, professional development funding, and regular performance feedback and reviews.

Additional Perks:

  • Reimbursement for office setup expenses
  • Monthly cell phone & internet stipend
  • Flexibility to work from home, enabling collaboration with global teams
  • Paid parental leave for all new parents
  • And much more!

About Counterpart Health: In 2018, Clover Health set out to do something unprecedented: build a clinically intuitive, AI-enabled solution that fits within physicians' workflows to help support the earlier diagnosis and management of chronic conditions.

Years later, that vision is a reality, with thousands of practitioners using Counterpart Assistant during patient visits to improve disease management, reduce medical expenses, and drive success in value-based care.

With an exceptional team of value-based care and technology experts, Counterpart Health is driving value-based care at the speed of software.

Counterpart Health is a subsidiary of Clover Health. From Clover’s inception, Diversity & Inclusion have always been key to our success. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and our employees are people with different strengths, experiences, perspectives, opinions, and backgrounds, who share a passion for improving people's lives. Diversity not only includes race and gender identity, but also age, disability status, veteran status, sexual orientation, religion and many other parts of one’s identity. All of our employee’s points of view are key to our success, and inclusion is everyone's responsibility.

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. We are an E-Verify company.

Final pay is based on several factors including but not limited to internal equity, market data, and the applicant’s education, work experience, certifications, etc.

A reasonable estimate of the base salary range for this role is:
$223,100—$290,000 USD

jobs.description:
About Us

The Movement Innovation Collaborative (MIC) is a new time-limited entity that will deepen and expand the capacity, impact, and sustainability of California's grassroots movements for racial justice and social transformation. Through offerings that are additive and synergistic with existing movement efforts, the MIC will support changemakers and organizations in catalyzing innovations in movement strategy, power-building, intergenerational leadership development, and collective long-term sustainability and resilience. Through a network of physical and virtual "centers," the MIC will also contribute a key piece of infrastructure to fuel transformative structural change across California. This network will comprise new and existing centers serving hundreds of organizations and tens of thousands of grassroots leaders across California.

Position Summary

The Director of Finance Administration is a strategic and operational leader who helps ensure Finance operates efficiently, effectively, and in service of the organization’s mission. Reporting to the Deputy Director of Finance, this role partners closely with Finance leadership to translate strategy into execution by strengthening Finance operations, improving systems and processes, supporting financial planning, and leading cross-functional initiatives.

The Director serves as a key thought partner in building a finance function that is collaborative, responsive, and solutions-oriented. This position balances operational leadership with financial management responsibilities, helping to connect financial stewardship with organizational priorities while fostering strong relationships across the organization.

Who You Are

Success in this role requires someone who enjoys building systems and relationships, improving processes, solving complex problems, and creating clarity in dynamic environments. The ideal candidate is both strategic and hands-on, equally comfortable supporting budgeting and financial planning, leading initiatives, and developing the infrastructure that enables Finance to operate as a trusted organizational partner.

What You’ll Be Doing

In this role, you will:

Lead and Strengthen the Finance Function

  • Partner with the Deputy Director of Finance to execute team priorities and long-term initiatives
  • Direct the day-to-day operations of the Finance team, including outsourced accounting
  • Supervise Finance staff and support professional development
  • Monitor team workload, priorities, and project timelines
  • Develop tools, guidance, and resources that improve the staff experience with Finance
  • Translate financial policies and processes into practical guidance for non-finance staff
  • Coordinate recurring finance processes including cycle of action, reporting timelines, and departmental communications
  • Promote collaborative service-oriented approach to financial stewardship

Build Better Systems & Processes

  • Lead implementation of Finance projects from planning through execution
  • Coordinate work across Finance, Programs, Operations, and external partners
  • Track deliverables, milestones, risks, and organizational commitments
  • Ensure projects move forward with clear accountability and follow-through
  • Design, document, and continuously improve finance policies, procedures, and workflows
  • Identify opportunities to streamline finance operations and strengthen internal controls
  • Support implementation and optimization of financial systems and technology
  • Lead change management and staff training related to new processes

Support Financial Planning & Stewardship

  • Direct Finance planning, budgeting, and operational initiatives
  • Develop and review financial reports, budget-to-actuals, and spending to identify trends and elevate issues
  • Manage cashflow planning and other financial planning activities
  • Prepare presentations, dashboards, and materials for leadership and board committees as needed
  • Lead coordination of annual audit and other strategic priorities
  • Contribute to building a scalable Finance function that supports the organization’s continued growth and impact

Qualifications

  • 7+ years of progressively responsible experience in operations, project management, finance administration, business operations, or organizational administration, or a related field
  • Experience working with financial systems such as Expensify, Bill.com, or similar platforms
  • Demonstrated experience leading complex projects from planning through implementation, including managing timelines, dependencies, stakeholders, communications, and follow through
  • Strong experience designing, documenting, and improving workflows, procedures, and administrative systems
  • Demonstrated ability to take broad strategic direction and independently translate into clear plans, processes, and deliverables
  • Experience developing SOP’s, guidance documents, training materials, and other tools that support consistent organizational practices
  • Experience supporting or working within a Finance, Accounting, or nonprofit administrative function
  • Strong understanding of financial processes and internal controls, with the ability to translate requirements into practical and user-friendly processes
  • Proven ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously while maintaining strong attention to detail and follow-through
  • Demonstrated success building systems, improving processes, and managing multiple priorities simultaneously
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills and ability to follow up with staff and external partners
  • Interest in supporting organizations working toward social change
  • Deep alignment with MIC’s mission, values, and movement-centered approach
  • Familiarity with financial systems, expense management platforms, contract management tools, or similar technology
  • Experience supporting remote teams or distributed organizations

Employment Classification and Salary

  • This is a full-time, exempt position starting as soon as possible. This role is remote; however, the candidate must be in California.
  • The starting salary for this position is $160,000.
  • The MIC has a 90-day trial period policy for all new hires. This allows both the organization and the employee to ensure a great fit. During this period, performance, adaptability, and cultural alignment will be assessed through ongoing feedback and a formal review.

Benefits

  • 100% organization-funded medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees, their spouses or domestic partners, and their children. Coverage begins on the first day of employment.
  • Paid Time Off: As a full-time employee, you will receive 15 days of vacation, 12 sick days per year, and a generous paid family leave policy. Accrual of this benefit begins on the first day of employment and becomes available upon completion of the 90-day trial period.
  • Paid Holidays: 21 days total, including a 10-day Winter Break overlapping with Christmas and New Year’s Day. Additionally, 4 Floating Holidays will be made available upon completion of the 90-day trial period.
  • Retirement Plan: MIC offers a 403b retirement plan. MIC contributes an employer-paid amount equal to 5% of your salary. Vesting for this contribution is immediate. Employees are autoenrolled with a 3% personal contribution rate and may adjust it at any time.

MIC’s salaries and benefits reflect our commitment to collective care and sustainability. They may evolve as the organization grows, and employees will be updated as changes occur. Additional details will be provided upon hiring.

The ideal candidate will play a critical role in collecting, analyzing, and interpreting data from a diverse range of sources, including IoT sensors, GIS systems, utility asset registries, and client platforms.

This position involves developing actionable insights to optimize processes, improve decision-making, and enhance operational efficiency. The Senior Data Analyst will manage and analyze large datasets, maintain utility asset data in Esri geodatabases, design and implement data visualization dashboards, and maintain integrations across various systems. This role also contributes to the ongoing development of McKim & Creed's data platform—collaborating with engineers and project managers to refine analytics, algorithms, and reporting tools that drive our mission of water conservation and smart resource management.

Data Quality Assurance and Control

  • Conduct daily QA/QC of incoming meter, SCADA, and telemetry feeds to ensure consistency, accuracy, and completeness.
  • Identify and resolve discrepancies or anomalies to maintain data integrity and reliability.

GIS Asset Data Management

  • Maintain and edit utility asset data in Esri geodatabases — including Utility Network and other water/wastewater asset data models — keeping attribution, connectivity, and asset hierarchies accurate and current.
  • Support asset registry workflows: as-built and plan-sheet incorporation, attribute population, condition and criticality fields, and reconciliation against client systems of record (Cityworks, Maximo, Lucity, Cartegraph, or similar).
  • Run and document data validation, topology and network error resolution, and versioned editing workflows; maintain the supporting data dictionaries and QA checklists.

Client Communication and Insights Delivery

  • Provide daily updates to clients regarding event notifications, significant trend identifications, and actionable insights derived from data analysis.
  • Establish strong communication channels to foster collaboration and trust.

Inventory Monitoring and Management

  • Perform daily inventory checks across all project locations, ensuring minimum field-deployable sensor inventory thresholds are maintained.
  • Collaborate with relevant teams to address inventory shortages proactively.

Maintenance Coordination

  • Maintain daily correspondence with maintenance staff to coordinate product allocations and schedule maintenance activities.
  • Ensure timely interventions to minimize downtime and improve operational efficiency.

Client Relationship Management

Job Title: Senior Health Data Analyst - Compass
