jobs.description:
About our group:

The Etail/Retail Route-to-Market team ensures the company’s go-to-market plans are successfully executed across global etail/retail channels. The team manages and aligns the 4Ps — product, pricing, placement, and promotion — to ensure plans support business targets and drive revenue growth.

Working closely with product marketing, sales, analytics, and global marketing teams, the group coordinates product launches, pricing strategy, channel placement planning, and promotional activation across regions. The team also monitors channel performance, analyzes business results, and surfaces insights that inform pricing, investment, and growth decisions.

About the role - you will:

Are you interested in ecommerce, data analysis, and understanding what drives business performance?

As the Ecommerce Marketing Intern – B2B Insights & Optimization, you'll work on a focused global analysis of Seagate's B2B ecommerce efforts across our Direct Store and eTail/Retail channels. You'll use available program data, business results, and input from global teams to understand how B2B ecommerce capabilities are being utilized and performing across different markets.

You'll help compare results, identify patterns and differences, investigate potential drivers behind performance, and turn your analysis into insights and recommendations that can help our teams make more informed decisions.

This internship provides hands-on experience working with real-world ecommerce programs and data while collaborating with marketing and business teams across a global organization.

Primary Project

Global B2B Ecommerce Capability Performance & Optimization Analysis

The project will focus on understanding how B2B ecommerce capabilities are being utilized across Seagate's Direct Store and global eTail/Retail channels, where performance differs across markets, and what factors may be contributing to those differences.

The intern will analyze available data and program learnings across retailers, regions, customer segments, products, and activation approaches to identify trends, gaps, and opportunities for continued optimization.

What You'll Do

  • As part of your internship, you will support a Global B2B Ecommerce Capability Performance & Optimization Analysis by:
  • Gathering and organizing available B2B ecommerce data and program results across Seagate's Direct Store and global eTail/Retail channels.
  • Comparing how B2B ecommerce capabilities are being utilized across retailers, regions, and channels.
  • Analyzing performance to identify trends, differences, and potential drivers of stronger or weaker results.
  • Examining performance across relevant dimensions such as customer segments, products, use cases, messaging, content, and activation approaches.
  • Conducting deeper analysis into selected areas where the data indicates a meaningful opportunity or unanswered question.
  • Gathering input from global and regional teams to provide context behind performance differences and capture key learnings.
  • Supplementing internal analysis with targeted competitive or market research where it helps explain findings or identify potential opportunities.
  • Identifying patterns or approaches that may be relevant across additional retailers, regions, or Direct Store.
  • Helping identify 1–3 areas where additional optimization, testing, or scale could be considered.
  • Preparing and presenting research findings, key insights, and recommendations at the conclusion of the internship.

What You'll Learn
During your internship, you'll gain experience in:

  • B2B ecommerce and business purchasing.
  • Ecommerce performance analysis.
  • Working with real-world business and marketing data.
  • Identifying trends and insights across multiple markets.
  • Translating data into actionable business recommendations.
  • Global eTail/Retail and Direct Store marketing.
  • Cross-functional collaboration within a global organization.
  • Executive presentation and communication skills.

About you:

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Strong research and organizational skills.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating with a broader team.

Your experience includes:

  • Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Business, Marketing, Economics, Data Analytics, Management, Information Systems, or a related field and returning to school in Fall 2027.
  • Comfortable working with data and identifying patterns, trends, and insight.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint.

Preferred

  • Interest in ecommerce, retail, B2B marketing, business analytics, or customer behavior.
  • Experience with class projects, internships, or extracurricular activities involving data analysis, research, or business problem solving.
  • Familiarity with ecommerce metrics or analytics tools is helpful but not required.
  • Interest in understanding how data and customer insights can be used to improve business and marketing decisions

Location:

Seagate is able to offer virtual employment for this position in the following states: AL, AZ, CA, CO, CT, FL, GA, ID, IL, IN, KS, KY, MA, MD, MI, MN, MO, NC, NH, NJ, NM, NY, NV, OH, OK, OR, PA, SC, SD, TN, TX, UT, VA, WA, WI, WY.

The estimated base wage range for this position is $20.00-29.50/hr. The individual base wage is based on work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. Our mission is to work with passion and purpose every day to improve lives and we are looking for others who value this same pursuit.

From our hands-on, accessible leaders, to our cohesive and supportive teams, we are committed to enabling professionals from all backgrounds and experiences to succeed. We prioritize cultivating a diverse and inclusive environment that continues to promote collaboration and creativity. Description

🤓 TripleTen is an EdTech company that designs and runs tech career learning programs for the US and Latin American markets. We've been doing it for over five years, teaching complete beginners — people with no prior tech background — through cohort-based programs built on our own platform and curriculum, developed in partnership with Nebius AI. Our team is fully remote and globally distributed, and we serve a large, active student base across both regions.

We're launching a program for experienced engineers transitioning into system architecture roles. The curriculum is being built by a team of senior authors. What we need now is the person who brings it to life for students: hosts the live sessions, reviews the work, runs the architecture review boards, and sets the technical bar for the people supporting alongside you.

This is a teaching and review role. You'll be the senior technical presence the cohort learns from week to week. You'll run live sessions and office hours, give real architectural feedback on student deliverables, and act as the escalation point for a team of supporting instructors who handle first-line questions. The best person for this is someone who has actually designed and shipped systems at scale, has opinions about what good architecture looks like, and can tell an experienced engineer why their design is wrong, not just whether it runs.

Your audience: experienced engineers leveling up to system architecture roles. Many already write production code daily. They will spot shallow feedback instantly, so the bar here is real seniority, not familiarity.

Format: Async-first with scheduled live sessions. Live sessions and office hours are timed around a US-based cohort. Estimated 15 to 25 hrs/week.

Areas of expertise

We will bring on three Experts, each focused on one of the following areas.

Expert A — System Foundations, API & Data

  • Module 1 — Foundations of System Engineering (Architecture principles, OpenTelemetry, distributed systems)

About Intermedia

Are you looking for a company where YOUR VOICE is heard? Where you can MAKE A DIFFERENCE? Do you THRIVE in a FAST-PACED work environment? Do you wake every morning EXCITED to work with GREAT PEOPLE and create SUCCESS TOGETHER? Then Intermedia is the place for you.

Intermedia has established itself as a leading provider of cloud communications and collaboration tech that allows companies to connect better. We have a strong track record of growth, profitability, and creating an environment where everyone matters. Everyone. While we are fast-paced and optimistic at Intermedia, we invite passionate, creative, and talented people to join us — here you can indulge your passion for creating and supporting great cloud technology. Culture at Intermedia is built on teamwork and transparency. We hold each other accountable and always have each other's back!

Are you ready to make your mark?

Key Responsibilities

So what is this job?

You know that feeling when you finally find the one row that broke everything? Or when a pipeline you built runs perfectly for weeks without a single alert? We live for that.
We take messy data from source systems, move it into Snowflake, shape it into something people can actually use, and make sure it stays that way. SQL is your main weapon. The stack is Snowflake, dbt, MSSQL, S3 — and if you haven’t used all of it, that is totally fine. What we really care about: you pick things up fast, you finish what you start, and when something goes wrong, you are the kind of person who figures out why.

Our stack

Snowflake · dbt · MSSQL (SQL Server) · S3 · MuleSoft · Git
A typical week

• Build and fix pipelines — ingestion, transformation, consumption, all of it
• Write dbt models that actually have tests and docs (yes, we check)
• Chase down a data issue from the report all the way back to the source
• Jump on an incident — MSSQL job died, Snowflake task hung, S3 file vanished — and fix it
• Run a backfill, validate the results, confirm the fix actually worked
• Help move data from MSSQL into Snowflake without losing anything along the way
• Keep an eye on monitoring so users don’t find problems before you do

Skills, Knowledge & Expertise

The non-negotiables

• Incremental loads are not scary: watermarks, MERGE vs INSERT, you know the trade-offs
• Git is just how you work: branches, PRs, code review — no big deal

Nice extras

• Snowflake: stages, file formats, Snowpipe, performance tricks

AI tools

• You already use Copilot, Claude, ChatGPT — to code faster, debug smarter, write better docs
• We use them too. Every day. Not as a gimmick.

What you get

jobs.excerpt: Position SummaryThe Regional Chief Revenue Officer (CRO) holds accountability for aggregate portfolio growth outcomes across five operating-company brands and owns the regional growth agenda and commercial operating system.
jobs.description:
Position Summary
The Regional Chief Revenue Officer (CRO) holds accountability for aggregate portfolio growth outcomes across five operating-company brands and owns the regional growth agenda and commercial operating system. Operating-company presidents retain direct accountability for firm-level bookings, net revenue, client relationships, and execution of their local go-to-market actions. The CRO ensures adherence to Trilon's commercial standards for CRM, dashboards, data, and reporting; establishes clear market and client priorities, a consistent business-development cadence, rigorous pursuit governance, actionable key-account plans with named owners and near-term commitments, and stronger selling capability in every logo.
This is a federated, leadership-through-influence role. Most client-development, marketing, and delivery resources remain within the operating companies and may not report directly to the CRO. Each operating company may retain a distinct go-to-market strategy, voice, and relationship model, provided its priorities and actions are grounded in regional priorities and Trilon's broader go-to-market philosophy. The CRO creates alignment and accountability, mobilizes cross-firm capabilities, and coaches local leaders and seller-doers to win the right work—without imposing a one-size-fits-all market strategy or displacing local ownership of the client.


What Success Looks Like
• One trusted regional view of clients, opportunities, pursuits, forecast, and growth risks, supported by strong CRM adoption and data quality.
• Five differentiated go-to-market action agendas that roll up to one coherent regional growth strategy, each translated into named priorities, owners, near-term actions, due dates, and measurable outcomes.
• A disciplined business-development rhythm that improves focus, follow-through, forecast confidence, and win rates.
• Named key accounts with executive sponsors, quantified growth goals, relationship maps, whitespace opportunities, rolling 90-day actions, named owners, and quarterly performance reviews.
• Stronger seller-doers in every logo, with a visible bench of seller-distributors who open doors, mobilize the right capabilities, and create opportunities for others to deliver.
• A fit-for-purpose commercial talent model in each logo, including dedicated lead-generation, business-development, capture, or sales capacity where the seller-doer model alone is insufficient.
• Visible cross-brand collaboration that expands services within existing clients, brings the best regional capabilities to priority pursuits, and provides a scalable commercial-integration path for acquired firms.

Core Responsibilities

1. Regional growth strategy and portfolio alignment
• Translate enterprise growth priorities into a three-year regional commercial strategy and an annual execution agenda, with clear choices by market, geography, service line, client segment, and operating company—then convert those choices into quarterly actions, owners, deadlines, and measurable outcomes.
• Partner with each operating-company president to develop an evidence-based go-to-market action plan that preserves local differentiation while aligning with regional priorities and Trilon's growth philosophy, with a small number of explicit priorities, named owners, 90-day actions, and measurable outcomes.
• Partner with operating-company presidents to establish targets for bookings, backlog, net revenue, pipeline, cross-brand growth, and strategic client expansion. Logo leadership retains direct accountability for firm-level results; the CRO holds accountability for aggregate portfolio outcomes and leads through visibility, challenge, coaching, intervention, and portfolio-level coordination.
• Identify regional whitespace, emerging demand, and adjacent services; build practical market-entry action plans with accountable owners, near-term milestones, measurable tests, and investment cases.
• Keep every regional, logo, market, account, pursuit, and capability plan lightweight and execution-focused: no plan is complete without prioritized actions, named owners, due dates, measurable outcomes, and a defined review cadence.
2. Trilon commercial standards, CRM, and dashboard governance
• Ensure every operating company adheres to Trilon's enterprise commercial standards, including use of the designated CRM, common client and opportunity taxonomy, stage definitions, required fields, opportunity ownership, probability rules, next-step discipline, data stewardship, and reporting cadence.
• Maintain the Trilon-designated CRM as the authoritative source for client, contact, opportunity, pursuit, and forecast information, integrated with Trilon's project and financial systems as appropriate.
• Deploy and maintain Trilon-standard, role-based dashboards for operating-company presidents, market leaders, business developers, seller-doers, and the regional leadership team. Local views may be added when useful, provided they preserve common definitions, data integrity, and portfolio comparability.
• Measure and enforce adherence to Trilon's CRM and dashboard standards through training, workflow design, adoption metrics, data-quality inspection, coaching, and clear consequences—not administrative reporting for its own sake.
• Partner with technology, finance, and operations to ensure pipeline signals inform backlog, hiring, capacity, and resource decisions.

3. Business-development rhythm and pursuit discipline
• Lead a consistent operating cadence: weekly priority-pursuit and pipeline reviews within operating companies; monthly regional growth reviews; quarterly key-account reviews; and annual market priority-setting translated into quarterly actions.
• Define and enforce fit-for-purpose qualification and go/no-go standards so pursuit resources are concentrated on strategically aligned, winnable, and economically attractive work.
• Improve opportunity strategy, competitive intelligence, capture action plans, teaming, client engagement, and executive sponsorship for major pursuits, with named actions, owners, and deadlines.
• Clarify handoffs among marketing, business development, seller-doers, proposal teams, operations, and project delivery; ensure lessons learned are captured and reused.
• Intervene directly on a limited number of region-defining pursuits and client situations where executive access, cross-firm coordination, or commercial judgment materially changes the outcome.

4. Key-account growth
• Create a regional key-account framework and select the accounts that warrant coordinated investment based on strategic fit, revenue potential, relationship strength, cross-service whitespace, and risk.
• Require a named account leader and executive sponsor for every key account, with a current relationship map, client priorities, competitive position, opportunity portfolio, revenue goal, and 90-day actions.
• Run quarterly account reviews that measure completion of committed actions, relationship coverage, opportunity conversion, revenue quality, client concentration risk, and expansion across brands and service lines.
• Resolve account ownership and channel conflicts transparently, protecting the client experience and rewarding cross-firm origination and collaboration.
• Build feedback loops from client listening, win/loss reviews, and project delivery into account and pursuit strategy.

5. Seller capability and commercial organization
• Assess the commercial maturity, market coverage, relationship concentration, seller capacity, and talent needs of each operating company; convert the findings into a practical 90/180-day capability roadmap for each logo with named actions, owners, timing, and measures of progress.
• Coach operating-company presidents, market and practice leaders, account leaders, and technical seller-doers through live account action planning, client strategy, opportunity qualification, capture action planning, pursuit reviews, and field-based practice.
• Establish a practical seller-doer curriculum focused on client discovery, relationship development, account action planning, opportunity qualification, capture strategy, cross-selling, and disciplined follow-through.
• Identify and develop high-potential seller-doers into seller-distributors—leaders who originate opportunities, understand client needs, route work to the best-qualified team or logo, mobilize other professionals, and create opportunities for others to deliver.
• Define role expectations, specific development actions, coaching, succession, and measures of effectiveness for seller-doers, seller-distributors, account leaders, dedicated business developers, and other growth roles.
• Determine where the seller-doer model is sufficient and where a logo requires dedicated lead-generation, business-development, capture, strategic-account, marketing, or sales capacity. Build the business case and role design, participate in selection and hiring decisions alongside partner-firm leadership, and support onboarding.
• Create a regional commercial community of practice so strong sellers across the five logos share methods, market intelligence, relationships, lessons learned, and opportunities.

6. Portfolio leadership, collaboration, and integration
• Lead through influence across the five operating companies, directly lead and develop regional business-development and growth resources, and clarify roles, decision rights, expectations, and talent priorities.
• Create a culture of shared credit, transparent pipeline information, client-first collaboration, and disciplined follow-through.
• Partner with marketing to align market intelligence, thought leadership, events, campaigns, proposals, and brand investments with priority clients and markets.
• Support onboarding and integration of acquired firms through a repeatable commercial playbook covering CRM, pipeline, account ownership, key relationships, market positioning, and cross-firm introductions.

Skills, Knowledge and Expertise


Required experience
• Senior commercial leadership experience in architecture, engineering, environmental, infrastructure, construction, or another relationship-led, project-based professional-services business.
• Demonstrated accountability for meaningful organic growth across multiple offices, business units, brands, or acquired companies in a decentralized environment.
• Strong command of the A&E business-development lifecycle: market strategy, client development, capture, qualification, proposals, contracting interfaces, and delivery handoff.
• Proven ability to design and embed CRM discipline, pipeline governance, forecast processes, dashboards, and executive operating rhythms with high user adoption.
• Track record building and executing strategic/key-account programs that expand existing relationships and coordinate multiple capabilities around client needs.
• Demonstrated ability to coach technical seller-doers, develop senior sellers who distribute opportunities across a broader team, and create measurable changes in commercial behavior.
• Experience assessing and designing commercial organizations, including decisions about seller-doer coverage, dedicated lead generation, business development, capture, marketing, strategic-account, and sales roles.
• Demonstrated leadership through influence: experience leading dedicated BD professionals and mobilizing technical seller-doers, operating leaders, marketing, and delivery teams without relying solely on direct authority.
• Experience in a sponsor-backed, acquisitive, or rapidly integrating business strongly preferred; successful post-acquisition commercial integration is especially relevant.
• Bachelor's degree required; advanced business or technical degree and relevant professional credentials preferred.

Leadership attributes
• Enterprise-minded, locally respectful: creates scale and consistency while protecting the relationships and identities that generate trust.
• Commercially rigorous: converts strategy into priorities, owners, metrics, decisions, and follow-through.
• Client-centered: understands that durable growth in A&E begins with client outcomes, credibility, and long-cycle relationships.
• Influential operator: leads through influence, aligns strong local leaders, resolves ambiguity, and changes behavior through clarity, coaching, and evidence.
• Collaborative and low-ego: shares credit, brokers resources, and makes the portfolio more valuable than the sum of its parts.
• Comfortable with pace and change: thrives in a PE-backed environment with acquisitions, evolving structures, ambitious goals, and high accountability.
• Data-informed, not data-bound: uses CRM and financial signals to improve decisions while staying close to clients and markets.
• People-first: develops others, communicates directly, and models integrity, collaboration, inclusion, and safety.

About Ritual

Ritual is a personal health brand that is raising the bar for daily wellness. Known for our best-selling, clinically backed prenatal, we create science-backed supplements with transparency at their core. We believe women deserve products they can trust, backed by real evidence—not just promises.

We started by reinventing the multivitamin with the first visible supply chain of its kind. Today, we’re expanding into new categories with the same high standards that built our reputation. Hundreds of thousands trust Ritual, and we’re growing fast.

Our team of 120+ scientists, creatives, and skeptics is raising the bar for women’s health. We’re venture-backed, based in sunny Los Angeles, and always looking for people ready to challenge the industry—and do the best work of their careers.

About the role

We're hiring a Director of Engineering to own the Shopify platform that runs ritual.com. This is bigger than the storefront: Shopify is the commercial operating system of our business, and this role owns it end to end—catalog and store configuration, the app stack, subscription commerce, and the integrations that connect the store to fulfillment, operations, finance, and marketing.

You'll lead our in-house engineering and QA team, own the technical roadmap for the platform in partnership with product, and represent engineering with senior stakeholders across the company. Critically, this role sits at the intersection of every team that plugs into the Shopify platform: growth and retention marketing (pixels, conversion tracking, catalog syncing, lifecycle and CRM integrations), customer support (helpdesk and customer data tooling), supply chain and logistics (fulfillment, order and inventory flows), and accounting (revenue recognition and finance data). Each of these teams depends on the platform working for them—you'll be their technical leader, translating their needs into sound integrations and keeping the whole system coherent as it grows.

This is a platform-owner role with a leadership mandate. Our engineering team already carries strong Liquid theme development skills—your job is to direct that work and hold the quality bar, while personally owning the back-end and administrative depth of the platform: how the catalog is modeled, how subscriptions are configured, how orders flow to fulfillment, and how revenue data reaches finance. You won't be heads-down on feature work day to day, but you'll review PRs, and you can run the codebase, debug a production issue, ship a quick fix, or delegate with precision. We're an AI-forward engineering team—AI development tools like Cursor and Linear are central to how we plan, build, and ship—and we're looking for a leader who works this way natively and raises the bar for how the whole team leverages them.

What you'll do

  • Own the Shopify platform end to end, including catalog setup and product data architecture, store settings, markets and checkout configuration, and overall store health. Establish clear, scalable platform standards and help the broader team understand how and why the Shopify instance is configured.
  • Lead subscription commerce configuration through Recharge, overseeing plans and pricing, discount logic, customer portal experiences, and the connections between subscriptions, promotions, and international markets.
  • Build, maintain, and evolve integrations connecting Shopify with critical business systems, including supply chain and logistics platforms, fulfillment, order and inventory synchronization, accounting and revenue recognition workflows, webhooks, APIs, and custom applications.
  • Manage and continuously improve the Shopify app ecosystem, evaluating third-party solutions across functionality, performance, security, privacy, and cost. Partner with stakeholders to make thoughtful build-vs.-buy decisions and simplify the technology stack when appropriate.
  • Guide Shopify theme development by partnering with an experienced engineering team with strong Liquid expertise. Collaborate with digital product management and web design to bring new features and experiences to life, while contributing to code reviews and fostering a high standard for performance, accessibility, maintainability, and polish.
  • Shape the storefront as a flexible content platform, owning metaobject and metafield data models, the CMS experience for content editors (including the blog), and a reusable library of sections and components that empowers non-engineering teams to create and update pages efficiently.
  • Partner closely with growth and retention marketing as a technical leader, overseeing the implementation and health of marketing pixels and conversion tracking, product catalog synchronization with advertising platforms, lifecycle and CRM integrations, and the data flows that support them. Help teams identify and execute effective technical solutions that support growth and retention goals.
  • Connect teams across the business through the platform, partnering with customer support, CRM, supply chain and logistics, accounting, and other stakeholders who rely on Shopify and its surrounding systems. Help ensure customer, order, subscription, and financial data flows reliably to the teams that need it, while representing cross-functional needs in engineering planning and roadmap discussions.
  • Champion web accessibility for , helping maintain the storefront in alignment with WCAG 2.1 AA standards. Embed accessibility into design reviews and definitions of done, and coordinate the annual manual accessibility audit with an external partner—from planning and triage through remediation and follow-through in the sprint cycle.
  • Help lead an AI-native development practice, using modern AI development tools such as Cursor and Linear to support thoughtful, efficient delivery. Establish team practices for using AI-assisted development responsibly, including standards for code quality, review, testing, security, and safe deployment.
  • Facilitate the team's sprint cycles from planning through delivery, helping groom and scope work, manage capacity, clarify priorities, and foster accountability across engineering and cross-functional partners contributing to the roadmap. Create the conditions for teams to deliver high-quality work predictably and sustainably.
  • Lead, hire, and develop the engineering and QA organization, supporting an in-house team of front-end engineers and a QA function led by a Senior QA Manager. Foster a collaborative, inclusive team culture and take shared ownership of quality and delivery across the full lifecycle, from planning and development through testing and release.
  • Build and manage strong vendor and partner relationships across the platform ecosystem, including app providers, agencies, and audit partners. Oversee budgets and contracts, set clear expectations, and create productive partnerships focused on measurable outcomes and long-term value.

Who you are

  • Clear Communicator: You express ideas clearly and thoughtfully—whether in writing, speaking, or storytelling. You tailor messages to your audience and make complex concepts easy to understand.
  • Empowered Collaborator: You work across teams with trust and respect. You challenge ideas constructively, co-create solutions, and move projects forward through collective effort.
  • Curious Thinker: You're naturally inquisitive and always eager to learn more. You ask questions, explore new ideas, and seek to understand the "why."
  • Self-Starter: You take initiative and move work forward independently. You bring fresh thinking that aligns with the team's goals.
  • Proactive: You anticipate needs, take ownership, and ask for support when needed. You keep momentum even without constant direction.
  • Systems Thinker: You recognize patterns, anticipate downstream impact, and build for scalability.
  • Detail-Oriented: You care about the details—because you know they add up to better, more trustworthy outcomes.
  • Resourceful (Scrappy): You figure things out with limited resources. You take initiative and find creative paths forward.
  • Technical Acumen: You bring deep engineering knowledge and apply it to real-world challenges.
  • Operational Excellence: You build and manage processes that make things run smoothly, reliably, and at scale.

What you'll need

  • 8+ years of software engineering experience, including 4+ years of deep Shopify platform experience spanning administration and development: catalog and product data architecture, store and checkout configuration, markets, and app stack management for a high-volume brand.
  • Proven back-end/platform ownership: fluency with the Shopify Admin and Storefront APIs, webhooks, and app extensions, and hands-on experience building and maintaining custom Shopify apps and integrations that stay reliable over time.
  • Experience integrating Shopify with operational and financial systems.
  • Strong Liquid theme development fluency.
  • Hands-on experience supporting growth and retention marketing as a technical resource. You're comfortable leading these conversations, not just executing tickets.
  • Comfort operating as the technical hub for many non-technical teams at once—marketing, customer support, supply chain, accounting—translating between business goals and technical constraints, and managing competing integration needs without losing platform coherence.
  • 5+ years of engineering management experience—you know how to hire, set expectations, review work, develop engineers, and hold a quality bar across a team, and you've owned delivery outcomes at the team level, not just the ticket level.
  • Strong agile fundamentals: you've run sprint cycles, groomed backlogs, scoped and estimated tickets, and managed delivery accountability across a team and its stakeholders.

Nice to have:

  • Experience managing external contractors or agencies alongside an in-house team, including scoping their work, reviewing deliverables, and holding an outside partner to the same quality bar.

We encourage you to apply even if you don't meet every qualification listed above. We're committed to building a diverse team and recognize that skills can be developed in many different ways.

Description

🤓 TripleTen is an EdTech company that designs and runs tech career learning programs for the US and Latin American markets. We're launching a program for experienced engineers transitioning into system architecture roles. The curriculum is being built by a team of senior authors. What we need now is the person who brings it to life for students: hosts the live sessions, reviews the work, runs the architecture review boards, and sets the technical bar for the people supporting alongside you.

This is a teaching and review role. You'll be the senior technical presence the cohort learns from week to week. You'll run live sessions and office hours, give real architectural feedback on student deliverables, and act as the escalation point for a team of supporting instructors who handle first-line questions. The best person for this is someone who has actually designed and shipped systems at scale, has opinions about what good architecture looks like, and can tell an experienced engineer why their design is wrong, not just whether it runs.

Your audience: experienced engineers leveling up to system architecture roles. Many already write production code daily. They will spot shallow feedback instantly, so the bar here is real seniority, not familiarity.

Format: Async-first with scheduled live sessions. Live sessions and office hours are timed around a US-based cohort. Estimated 15 to 25 hrs/week.

Areas of expertise

We will bring on three Experts, each focused on one of the following areas.

Expert A — System Foundations, API & Data

  • Module 1 — Foundations of System Engineering (Architecture principles, OpenTelemetry, distributed systems)
  • Module 2 — API & Service Architecture (REST, GraphQL, gRPC, service boundaries, DDD)
  • Module 3 — Data Architecture & Storage Patterns (SQL/NoSQL, sharding, replication, Redis caching)

Expert B — Cloud, Distributed Systems

  • Module 4 — Cloud Infrastructure & Platform Engineering (Kubernetes, Terraform, GitOps, CI/CD, FinOps)
  • Module 5 — Distributed Systems & Event-Driven Architecture (CAP theorem, event-driven, Kafka, alert routing)

Expert C — Security, AI Systems & Architecture Leadership

  • Module 6 — Security & Compliance Architecture (Zero-trust, threat modeling, compliance, secure CI/CD)
  • Module 7 — AI Systems Design & Integration (LLM integration, RAG, ML reliability, AI governance)
  • Module 8 — Architecture Documentation & Leadership (ADRs, C4 diagrams, technical communication)

Please indicate in your application which area fits you best. If you have overlapping skills, don’t hesitate to apply and indicate it in your application. Submit all resumes or CV's in English.

What you will do

  • Mentor students through 1:1 video calls, Q&A sessions, and group events, helping them clarify concepts and navigate assignments.
  • Host webinars and workshops on program topics, industry insights, and extracurricular skills.
  • Review and assess student projects, providing clear, constructive feedback aligned with program standards.
  • Engage with students on the Hub through written guidance, ongoing communication, and curated learning resources.
  • Share professional expertise to equip students with practical skills and career strategies.
  • Foster a collaborative learning environment that builds confidence, encourages interaction, and supports student growth.
  • Conduct Mock Interviews providing constructive feedback on both their technical responses and interview skills.
  • Record instructional videos for the curriculum, clearly explaining key concepts, methodologies, and course topics to support student learning.

Requirements

  • 5+ years as a senior software/systems architect, platform engineer, or senior backend/infrastructure engineer
  • Has designed and shipped systems at scale in a real company, not just coursework or side projects
  • Depth across the architectural spine: system design, API and service architecture, cloud and infrastructure (AWS, Kubernetes, Terraform, CI/CD), and distributed systems
  • Can explain why a decision was made, not just how it was implemented, and can diagnose and critique someone else's architecture live
  • Strong technical communication: comfortable leading a live session and writing clear, specific review feedback
  • Strong English C1+ — instruction and review are in English for a US-based audience
  • Comfortable using AI tools in day-to-day technical work

  • Fully remote work with flexible hours
  • A digital office — we use modern tools (Notion, Miro, Slack, Figma) to keep collaboration smooth

IREN is a vertically integrated AI Cloud provider, delivering large-scale data centers and GPU clusters for AI training and inference. IREN’s platform is underpinned by its expansive portfolio of grid-connected land and power in renewable-rich regions across North America, Europe and APAC.

With 100% renewable energy, we build, own and operate our data centers and take pride in being at the forefront of sustainable solutions for the ever-evolving applications of high-performance compute. We believe that human progress is invaluable, but it should be done in the right way: responsibly, sustainably and having a positive impact on the communities we operate in.

We are hiring a Business Operations Manager to run the business of Cloud Operations and SRE, and to work 1:1 with the VP who leads it. One role, two halves that reinforce each other: you own how the org plans, reports and follows through, and you own the executive’s time, attention and follow-through as a system you design and continuously improve.

We are looking for someone who already runs their own stack of agents and automations, who treats “a human did this manually” as a bug, and who measures themselves by what moved forward — not by what got scheduled.

If you have been the person on your team quietly building the workflows everyone else asks to borrow, read on.

What This Role Actually Is
  • A business operations owner. You run the planning and reporting spine of the org: goals and OKRs, the roadmap, the cross-functional programs, and the metrics that say whether Cloud Operations and SRE are healthy. You know the numbers before anyone asks for them, and you chase down the ones that do not make sense.
  • A program driver. For initiatives that cross teams, you own the plan, the dependencies, the risks and the uncomfortable status update. Nobody should have to ask “what happened with that?”
  • An operator. You will run the operating cadence: staff meetings, business reviews, planning cycles, offsites. You will run these end to end: agenda, pre-reads, decisions captured, owners assigned, follow-ups driven to closure.
  • A force multiplier to the executive, not a filter. The executive support half of this job is a core part of it, not a legacy attachment. You will own the VP’s calendar, inbox, travel and follow-through, and you will make decisions on their behalf inside clearly defined boundaries widening those boundaries as trust compounds. You understand what good looks like for implementing an agentic stack to be the filter, and the organizational change management necessary to drive the teams to that filter.
  • An org operations partner. Headcount and requisition tracking, hiring loops, onboarding that does not depend on tribal knowledge, team communications, and offsites you own outright.
  • An automation builder. Every recurring task you touch is a candidate for an agent. Weekly reports, status roll-ups, meeting prep briefs, inbox triage and drafting, travel logistics, expense reconciliation, doc hygiene — you build it once, monitor it, and move on to the next thing. Your job is to work yourself out of your own to-do list, repeatedly. There is plenty more to do after all of this is automated; it is why you are a force multiplier and an operator.
  • A judgment layer. Automation is cheap; taste is not. You will know which emails only the executive can answer, which meeting genuinely needs 60 minutes, which “urgent” request can wait until Thursday, and which agent output is subtly wrong and must never go out the door.

Responsibilities

Business operations, programs and reporting
  • Own the operating cadence for Cloud Operations & SRE from staff meetings, business reviews, planning cycles and offsites
  • Drive cross-functional programs and initiatives to completion on behalf of the VP, tracking plans, dependencies, risks and status, and escalating early when something is off track.
  • Build and maintain leadership reporting: KPI and SLO roll-ups, dashboards, weekly status and business review packages and keep the underlying data trustworthy.
  • Run the goal setting and OKR cycle for the org: drafting, tracking and reporting against commitments.
  • Coordinate invoice management for the teams, including vendor tracking, approval workflows, payment follow-up and record keeping.

Organisational and team operations
  • Track headcount and open requisitions, coordinate hiring loops and candidate scheduling, and own onboarding for new team members.
  • Maintain team records, distribution lists, organizational documents and shared files to ensure key information is accurate, accessible and well organised.
  • Own internal team communications, all hands content and team offsites end to end.
  • Support the processes and activities of the teams, applying judgment and discretion to identify operational needs, adapt to shifting priorities, and contribute directly to the effective management of the team’s business operations.

Executive support
  • Manage the complex calendar of the VP, Cloud Operations & SRE, including scheduling meetings, appointments, travel arrangements (domestic and international), and speaking engagements.
  • Organize and prepare for meetings by gathering documents, creating agendas, taking minutes, and coordinating logistics.
  • Act as a liaison between the teams and external parties, screening calls and visitors, answering inquiries with professionalism, and directing communications as needed.
  • Draft, review and send communications on behalf of the team as required.
  • Manage department credit cards, ensuring sufficient funds are available and receipts are logged accordingly.
  • Provide additional support to other departments, administrators or executives as needed.
  • Other duties as assigned by the company.

Requirements

  • 5 or more years in business operations, program management, chief-of-staff or senior executive support roles, including direct experience supporting a senior executive, and at least some of it in a fast-moving, high-ambiguity environment (startup, scale-up, or a team inside a larger company operating like one).
  • Genuinely AI-native. You use AI assistants and agentic tools every day, not occasionally. You can describe — in specifics — a workflow you automated, what broke, and how you fixed it. Prompting is not a party trick to you; it is how you work. Bonus points if you are well beyond prompting and operating with context and graph loop engineering.
  • Hands-on with agentic tooling. Personal AI agents and assistants for calendar, inbox and scheduling; general-purpose assistants (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini) as daily drivers; and connective tissue between systems. You do not need to be an engineer. You do need to be unafraid of documentation and have a high level of taste.
  • The ability to run a cadence and a program. Agendas, pre-reads, decision logs, status that is honest when it is bad. You are comfortable holding senior people to commitments they made, in writing, in front of their peers.
  • Comfort with numbers. You can build a reporting roll-up, spot the metric that is lying, and explain a trend to leadership without dressing it up.
  • Judgment under incomplete information, or with swinging-door outcomes. You would rather make a reversible decision now than wait for permission.
  • Instinctive discretion. You will sit close to board material, compensation, org changes and unannounced strategy. This is table stakes.

Nice to have:
  • You have built something small and useful with low-code tools — a script, a dashboard, a bot — because it was faster than asking.
  • You have run a planning or OKR cycle for a technical org and lived with the result.
  • You have been given scope beyond a traditional remit: a project, a budget, a vendor relationship, a team offsite you owned outright.
  • Experience in an org where AI adoption was a stated strategy, not a pilot.
  • Comfort with data infrastructure, energy, or high-growth technical businesses.
  • You have opinions about which tools are overrated.
  • You know how to speak clanker.

What will make you unhappy here:
  • You want a stable, predictable week.
  • You prefer to be told exactly what to do.
  • You expect the executive-support half of this role to disappear once the operations half gets interesting. Both are the job.
  • “That’s not my job” is in your vocabulary.

These offerings are part of our broader Total Rewards package, thoughtfully designed to support your health, well-being, and long-term success.

jobs.description:
About Magic
Magic is a leading modern outsourcing platform that connects SMBs to high-quality remote workers, from SDRs to virtual assistants and more. With roots in Silicon Valley and backing from top venture capitalists, our workers are supercharged with a combination of the latest AI technology and training. We came out of Y Combinator in 2015, have grown to 1,000+ remote workers, and are backed by Sequoia Capital with over $30M in funding.

Background
Our company came out of Y Combinator in 2015. Since then we've grown to 1000+ remote workers, with strong venture-backing (including Sequoia Capital) and over $30M in funding to date. We are fully remote across Asia and US time zones.
  • Check out Magic's Business Profile
  • Know more about our Team via Magic's Careers Page﻿﻿
Why does this role exist?
Every client Magic serves depends on being matched with the right assistant — and that match only happens because someone made a smart, well-informed call on candidate readiness. That someone is you. As a Recruitment Associate (Matcher), you are the final quality checkpoint before a candidate meets a client. You're not just screening — you're making judgment calls that directly affect client satisfaction and Magic's reputation. When you get it right, clients stay. When clients stay, Magic grows. This role exists because quality placements don't happen by accident — they happen because someone owns the process end to end.

Our Hiring Process
  1. Application + Pre-Qualifying Questions
  2. Skills Assessment — short video interview
  3. First Interview — communication skills and role expectations (with Recruiting Team)
  4. 24-Hour Reflection Period — If we advance you, we'll ask you to take 24 hours to seriously consider the schedule, compensation, and commitment before moving forward
  5. Hiring Manager Interview — practice candidate assessment + career goals discussion
  6. Final Interview with the Head of People Product
  7. Background Check + Vetting
  8. Job Offer
  9. 2-Week Training Program

What Winning Looks Like
  • You consistently endorse candidates who meet client expectations — your placement quality score reflects your judgment, not just your effort
  • You complete your daily interview targets without sacrificing the accuracy of your evaluation reports
  • You catch candidate readiness issues before they reach the client — you flag concerns proactively, not after the fact
  • Your evaluation reports are structured, concise, and client-ready — the hiring manager can make a decision from your summary alone without needing edits
  • You show up with the same level of energy and engagement in your sixth interview as your first
  • After a difficult call or a mistake, you're back to full capacity within minutes — not hours
Who This Role Is NOT For
  • You are not available for shifting schedules including nights, evenings, or days — schedules are assigned based on business needs and are not self-selected
  • You have low natural energy — this role requires sustained enthusiasm across 4–6 consecutive interviews every single shift
  • You take days to recover emotionally from a difficult conversation or a mistake — this role requires quick reset and forward momentum
  • You're proud of how fast you work, not how accurately — this role rewards precision over speed, every time
  • You need constant supervision to stay on task — this role requires genuine independence and self-direction
  • You don't have a professional home office setup right now with reliable internet (25+ Mbps) and a quiet environment for confidential interviews
  • You treat daily targets as optional — performance expectations are real from Day 1
  • You've held multiple roles for under a year — we're looking for someone building a career, not collecting experience
  • You see feedback as personal criticism rather than part of learning
  • You are currently freelancing as a VA/EA and plan to keep those clients — exclusivity is non-negotiable

Core Responsibilities

Work toward daily and monthly targets with consistency, support different recruitment teams as needed, and apply feedback quickly to improve over time.
Finding the Right People
  • Look through Magic's existing pool of potential hires to find good matches for what clients need — no external sourcing required
  • Keep a backup list ready in case your first choices don't work out
Interviewing Candidates
  • Set up interview times that work for everyone
  • Conduct final interviews before candidates meet clients
  • Decide if they're ready and a good fit — this is your call
Coordinating with Your Team
  • Pass candidate information to Sales, Support, and Customer Success teams
  • Ensure smooth handoffs so everyone has what they need
Writing Reports
  • Write clear, detailed reports about each candidate
  • Make sure your reports give clients everything they need to make a hiring decision
Meeting Your Targets
  • Work toward monthly goals and daily deadlines
  • Ensure all recommendations meet Magic's quality standards
Being Flexible
  • Help other recruitment teams when needed
  • Adjust to changing priorities throughout your shift
  • Learn different parts of the hiring process over time
The RealityEvery shift you'll handle 4–6 candidate interviews — while managing real-time scheduling requests and team coordination, and running ATS, HubSpot, and Magic systems simultaneously. The result of getting this right is direct: client satisfaction goes up, candidates succeed, and Magic grows.

Schedules are assigned based on businessneeds and may include night, evening, or day hours — make sure you've seriously considered your availability for any shift before applying. You will feel overwhelmed in Month 1 — that's normal. What separates people who succeed is the willingness to learn fast, reset quickly, and ask good questions.

What You Bring

  • Bachelor's degree (any field) or equivalent work experience
  • Excellent English — strong speaking, writing, and structured communication for client-facing outputs
  • Strong attention to detail — your reports directly affect client hiring decisions
  • Full availability for assigned shifts — schedules may include nights (9 PM–6 AM or 10 PM–7 AM PHT), evenings (2 PM–10 PM PHT), or days (8 AM–5 PM or 9 AM–6 PM PHT), Monday–Friday or Tuesday–Saturday, with advance notice for changes
  • Reliable home office: computer, headset, video conferencing setup, quiet environment, 25+ Mbps internet with backup
  • Demonstrated ability to commit — we look for people who finish what they start
Your Superpowers
  • Sustained Energy — you show up with the same enthusiasm in your sixth interview as your first; this is not a low-energy role
  • Precision Over Speed — you take pride in getting it exactly right; accuracy over volume, every time
  • Emotional Reset — after a tough conversation or a mistake, you're back to full capacity within minutes
  • Ownership — you take responsibility for your work and fix mistakes without being told twice
  • Learning Agility — you absorb feedback fast, apply it immediately, and get measurably better with every shift
  • People Instinct — you enjoy talking to candidates and have a natural sense for readiness and fit
  • Figure It Out Mentality — when your plan stops working, you find another way; outcomes over effort
Before You Apply — Ask Yourself
  1. Am I genuinely available for any assigned shift — nights, evenings, or days — not just the schedule I prefer?
  2. Do I have a professional home office setup with reliable internet right now — not "almost ready"?
  3. Am I the kind of person who takes pride in precision and accuracy, not just speed?
  4. Can I reset quickly after a difficult conversation and bring full energy to the next one?
  5. Can I commit exclusively to Magic — no other VA/EA clients during training or production?
  6. Am I ready to start within a few weeks — no major transitions or life events blocking me?
If you answered yes to all six — we want to hear from you. If you answered "maybe" or "I'll figure it out" to any of them — the timing might not be right yet, and that's okay.

What's In It For You

Your Offer TypeNot all candidates will receive the same offer. Your offer type depends on your recruitment experience, proven skills, and overall qualifications. Both paths lead to the same role — the difference is how you start.

  • Performance-based growth opportunities
Your Growth Path
  • Associate (0–6 months): Learn processes, conduct interviews, meet quality standards
  • Recruitment Specialist (6–12 months): Higher targets, more complex assessments, full autonomy
  • Senior Specialist (1–2 years): Mentor new hires, handle VIP clients, lead quality initiatives

A Sr. Creative Strategist will be the lead ideator on strategic accounts. Sr. Creative Strategists know how to act fast to capitalize on good results, or on the flip side know what to change if an ad isn’t performing to goal. This means testing with the intention of moving the needle on key performance metrics — from improving CPA, CTR, or ROAS to driving brand awareness.   • Utilize and leverage Power Digital's Nova ecosystem as it relates to your department

Role Requirements:

  • Proficiency with Meta Ads Manager, and/or similar performance data tools (TikTok, YouTube, Pinterest, etc)
  • Technically skilled at pulling and using creative performance data to analyze trends, insights, and inform creative roadmaps
  • Understanding of best practices for performance-driven creative & ability to apply these insights in work
  • Ability to write effective ad copy, structure a script, and see through on the execution with corresponding visuals
  • Ability to communicate and collaborate with clients, production, and post-production teams to deliver best possible creative output
  • Ability to yield strong campaign results for clients through strategizing top performing creative

  • Highly organized with the ability to manage complex workflows and project work. Demonstrates strong time management and desk management skills.

  • Ability to collaborate with internal and external experts, including legal, underwriting, and other stakeholders, to ensure thorough evaluation.
  • Designs empathetic customer service strategies; recognized for exceptional service.
  • Ability to quickly assess customer concerns and anticipate questions, communicate and translate complex and technical terms clearly with easily understood language; deliver difficult messages when needed.
  • Skilled in using claims systems and Microsoft Office Suite.
  • Ability to use a personal computer and other standard office equipment.
  • Ability to sit and/or stand for extended periods.
  • Required to work on-site as needed.
  • Ability to travel as necessary.
  • Ability to work in a fast paced, changing or stressful environment.
  • Ability to perform work in a noisy/loud work environment.
  • May be required to have and maintain sufficient home-based internet connection.
  • Ability to operate a motor vehicle 4-5 hours per day and to get in and out of the vehicle numerous times during the day.
  • Ability to load and unload equipment and supplies weighing up to 30 pounds from a motor vehicle as needed to perform field work.
  • Ability to bend, walk, and climb for several consecutive hours while inspecting damaged buildings, often with utilities turned off or inoperable.
  • Ability to use a ladder safely to get on and off roofs and maintain balance while inspecting roofs.

jobs.excerpt: About TelnyxTelnyx is an industry leader that's not just imagining the future of global connectivity—we're building it.
jobs.description:
About Telnyx

Telnyx is an industry leader that's not just imagining the future of global connectivity—we're building it. From architecting and amplifying the reach of a private, global, multi-cloud IP network, to bringing hyperlocal edge technology right to your fingertips through intuitive APIs, we're shaping a new era of seamless interconnection between people, devices, and applications.

We're driven by a desire to transform and modernize what's antiquated, automate the manual, and solve real-world problems through innovative connectivity solutions. As a testament to our success, we're proud to stand as a financially stable and profitable company. Our robust profitability allows us not only to invest in pioneering technologies but also to foster an environment of continuous learning and growth for our team.

Our collective vision is a world where borderless connectivity fuels limitless innovation. By joining us, you can be part of laying the foundations for this interconnected future. We're currently seeking passionate individuals who are excited about the opportunity to contribute to an industry-shaping company while growing their own skills and careers.

Inference Infrastructure Architect
Senior / Staff · Remote — mainland China · Founding China team

Telnyx runs its own B300 fleet — our hardware, in our facilities, operated from the metal up, and expanding globally. This role exists to turn that fleet into useful throughput: Telnyx's own AI-agent traffic on the voice and messaging network, and external customers' inference behind the token gateway, dedicated deployments and tuned models.

You have two mandates:

  1. Operate and expand the fleet efficiently. Maximize useful inference throughput per GPU-dollar while meeting latency and reliability SLOs, and continuously reduce cost per token.
  2. Make the product run on it. Serverless inference for the open-weight catalog, and dedicated, tuned model deployments for enterprises.

The stack is open source, bare metal to OpenAI-compatible endpoint. You work upstream in it.

What you'll build

  • Serverless serving pools. vLLM / SGLang engines with continuous batching, prefix caching, low-precision serving (FP8, FP4, INT4) and MoE expert parallelism, serving the head of the open-weight catalog at multi-tenant scale.
  • The fleet layer. llm-d / NVIDIA Dynamo on the Kubernetes Gateway API: KV-cache-aware routing, prefill/decode disaggregation, KV tiering (Mooncake), and multi-LoRA serving so hundreds of customer adapters share one base pool.
  • The platform under it. Kubernetes on bare metal: GPU Operator, topology-aware scheduling, LeaderWorkerSet, Kueue; Kata Containers for isolated dedicated tenants; bare-metal lifecycle with OpenStack Ironic.
  • Weight logistics and elasticity. P2P model distribution (Dragonfly, safetensors streaming), warm pools, and autoscaling driven by inference metrics — queue depth, KV occupancy, TTFT — never CPU.
  • The dedicated tier. Per-tenant pools, GPU-hour metering, latency SLOs, private networking; and the serving side of the model-tuning loop: adapter versioning, canary rollout, rollback on outcome regression.
  • Observability and economics. DCGM and engine metrics into Prometheus / OpenTelemetry; capacity planning grounded in roofline math — bandwidth-bound decode, batching curves, utilization versus cost per token.

The stack you'll work in

Some of this is committed direction: Kubernetes on bare metal, vLLM / SGLang, an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Much of the rest is candidates you'll evaluate. You'll select, benchmark and integrate the components that earn their place in production. We value depth in the core serving stack and sound architectural judgment, not prior experience with every project listed.

  • Engines: vLLM · SGLang
  • Serving techniques: prefill/decode disaggregation · wide expert parallelism · speculative decoding (MTP, EAGLE-3) · low precision (FP8, FP4, INT4)
  • MoE & attention libraries: DeepEP · DeepGEMM · EPLB · FlashMLA
  • Routing & serving: llm-d · NVIDIA Dynamo · Kubernetes Gateway API · Envoy · Ray Serve / KubeRay
  • KV cache & weights: Mooncake · HiCache · 3FS · Dragonfly
  • Scheduling & GPU sharing: Kubernetes · Volcano · Kueue · LeaderWorkerSet · HAMi
  • Isolation & bare metal: Kata Containers · OpenStack Ironic · NVIDIA GPU Operator
  • Observability: Prometheus · Grafana · DCGM · OpenTelemetry

What we look for

  • You have owned production LLM serving under meaningful traffic and latency constraints, and can explain the architecture, the bottlenecks you diagnosed, the changes you made, and the resulting improvements in latency, reliability or cost. Scale on the order of thousands of GPUs or millions of requests a day is a strong signal, not a hard requirement.
  • Kubernetes on GPU fleets, operated end to end: GPU Operator, device plugins, node pools and topology-aware placement, gang scheduling (LeaderWorkerSet, Kueue), GitOps rollouts, and the ability to debug why a pod landed where it did.
  • Deep operational command of vLLM or SGLang: deploying, tuning and upgrading it (parallelism with TP / EP, quantization, batch and KV-cache settings, prefix caching, disaggregation), and knowing which knob moves which metric.
  • Performance engineering at the system level: you read engine and DCGM metrics, reason from roofline, and size deployments with numbers.
  • Python and Go for automation; real Linux, networking and storage depth. You don't need to write CUDA; you need to know when a problem is one, and route it upstream.
  • You work with the community in English and Chinese, and write runbooks and design docs people actually read.

Experience we especially value

  • Operated inference platforms at the scale of Ant Group, Alibaba Cloud / PAI, Tencent, ByteDance, Baidu, Huawei, DaoCloud, Moonshot, DeepSeek, or comparable teams.
  • Contributor to, or heavy production user of, any of: vLLM, SGLang, llm-d, NVIDIA Dynamo, Ray / KubeRay, Kata Containers, Volcano, Kueue, HAMi, Dragonfly, Mooncake, Envoy.
  • Presence in the CNCF / OpenInfra community: talks at KubeCon China, OpenInfra Days, vLLM or SGLang meetups.

Nice to have

  • Fine-tuning / RL infrastructure: LoRA pipelines, evaluation harnesses, champion/challenger rollout.
  • Real-time voice latency work: sub-second time-to-first-token budgets on live calls.
  • Multi-region deployments and data-residency requirements.

What we offer

  • The newest hardware, ours from the metal up. A globally expanding B300 fleet that Telnyx builds and operates end to end. Bring your experience optimizing demanding production workloads to a fleet where you shape the architecture from bare metal to customer endpoint.
  • Own the platform, build the team. A greenfield inference platform where you set the pattern others follow. As a founding member of our China team, you also get a say in who joins next and how the team works.
  • Open-source first. Upstream contribution is part of the job, and conference travel is supported.
  • Based in mainland China, no relocation required. You work remotely with a global, async-friendly team. Should you ever choose to move, we have hiring entities in the Netherlands, the United States, Ireland and Saudi Arabia, and we sponsor visas.

When you apply

Include a brief description of an inference system you personally improved: the bottleneck, your intervention, and the measured result. An anonymized example is welcome.

jobs.description:
DevOps Staff Platform Engineer

Location: Remote (Canada)

Compensation: $135,000 - $170,000 CAD + bonus + meaningful equity

About Orion Digital

Orion Digital Corp (NASDAQ/TSX: ORIO) is a publicly listed Canadian fintech operating a multi-engine financial platform spanning lending (Mogo), payments (Carta), and wealth (Intelligent Investing).

We have moved past the traditional fintech model. Capital allocation, decisioning, and risk management sit at the core of how the business creates value, and AI runs as an enabling layer across the platform rather than as a standalone product narrative. That layer is real and in use, and the work now is making it faster, safer, and harder to break.

Why this role exists

This role builds that layer.

Platform engineering here is not a support function. Multiple business lines, regulated entities, and a public company's reporting obligations all run on infrastructure this team owns. Every deployment path, permission boundary, and audit trail either makes faster decisioning possible or quietly caps how fast the business can move.

Which means the platform is where the strategy succeeds or stalls. If deploying takes a day, if an agent cannot safely touch production, if nobody can tell what changed and why, the enabling layer stays theoretical. We are hiring a Staff Platform Engineer to build it properly.

The shift we are hiring for

Most platform teams build for human developers. Ours builds for humans and agents, across multiple business lines and regulated entities. That changes the job:

  • Golden paths become machine-executable contracts, not wiki pages. An agent has to be able to discover them, invoke them, and verify the result.
  • Every probabilistic step needs a deterministic gate behind it. Tests, policy checks, and schema validation stop being hygiene and become the control system that lets autonomy scale safely.
  • Agents are identities. They need scoped credentials, bounded blast radius, and audit trails that hold up across lending, payments, and securities regulation.
  • Observability has to answer a new question. Not just "is the service healthy" but "did the agent do the right thing, and how do we know."

If that is already how you think about the problem, keep reading.

What you will do

Build the substrate for agentic engineering

  • Design and run the execution environments agents work in: sandboxed, reproducible, permissioned, disposable.
  • Stand up and own our MCP and tool-gateway layer so agents reach infrastructure through governed interfaces instead of ad hoc credentials.
  • Turn CI/CD into a validation loop: fast deterministic gates an agent can retry against until it passes, with humans on the loop rather than in it.

Own the platform

  • Multi-cloud Kubernetes, infrastructure as code, and GitOps (ArgoCD) delivery. Hands on keyboard, not diagrams.
  • Drive infrastructure modernization across our cloud environments, including the unglamorous parts: dependency mapping, and documentation that survives your absence.
  • Serve every product line without building a separate platform for each one. Where they genuinely differ, respect it. Where they have drifted for no reason, converge them.
  • Treat security and compliance as design constraints from the first commit rather than a review at the end.

Take toil off the company

  • Push autonomous remediation into the paths that page people today. The target is alerts that resolve themselves and incidents where the first responder is an agent arriving with a hypothesis already tested.
  • Own the numbers: deploy frequency, lead time, change failure rate, MTTR, and the share of operational work running without a human in the middle. Move them quarter over quarter.
  • Work outside engineering too. Operations, compliance, and support are full of repetitive work a well-built platform can absorb.

What you need

Non-negotiable

  • Deep, current production experience with Kubernetes, Terraform, and a modern GitOps deployment stack. You have owned what you built, including running it in production rather than handing it off once it shipped.
  • Real cloud depth. We run across AWS and OCI, so experience in both is an advantage, but what matters is genuine production depth in at least one and the appetite to get fluent in the other quickly.
  • You run coding and ops agents as part of your daily work, and you can show us. Sustained real use on real systems (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or equivalent, plus whatever you have wired together yourself), not a trial and an opinion. Be ready to walk through something you shipped this month where an agent did most of the typing and you did the judging.
  • Strong opinions about where autonomy belongs and where it does not, informed by having been burned at least once.
  • Writing clear enough to be read by a junior engineer and a model.

Advantage

  • You have built internal developer platforms, MCP servers, or agent tooling that other engineers actually adopted.
  • Non-human identity, secrets architecture, or policy-as-code in a regulated environment.
  • Re-platforming at scale, especially where the old system could not go down.
  • Opinions about how to evaluate infrastructure agents. Almost nobody has these yet.

We are not screening on years of experience as a proxy for capability. We will look at what you have built and how fast you build.

How we work

  • Small teams, high ownership, short distance between decision and deployment.
  • We would rather collaborate than dictate, and we know when to do it well versus when to do it quickly.
  • Output is the measure.

About the Role

At Pavago, one of our clients is hiring an E-commerce Operations & Data Analyst to support the day-to-day logistics, inventory management, operational reporting, and data analysis of a growing e-commerce business.

This is an operations-first role, not a highly technical data engineering position. You’ll coordinate freight and inventory, maintain accurate operational data, manage Shopify information, build reports and dashboards, and use spreadsheets to help the business make better operational decisions.

You’ll also use modern AI tools such as ChatGPT and Claude to streamline repetitive work, improve reporting, and make internal processes more efficient.

The ideal candidate combines logistics and e-commerce experience with strong spreadsheet and analytical skills and enjoys continuously improving how operations are run.

What You’ll Own

Logistics & Freight Coordination

  • Manage freight and shipment coordination from start to finish.
  • Track shipments, deliveries, and fulfillment timelines.
  • Coordinate closely with warehouses and logistics partners.
  • Maintain visibility into shipment status and proactively address delays.
  • Keep accurate and organized logistics records.
  • Ensure day-to-day logistics workflows run smoothly.

Inventory & Purchase Order Management

  • Monitor inventory levels and stock availability.
  • Create and manage purchase orders based on inventory needs.
  • Use sales trends and forecasting data to support purchasing decisions.
  • Help prevent stockouts and unnecessary overstock.
  • Maintain accurate inventory trackers and records.

E-commerce Operations

  • Manage and update product and operational data within Shopify.
  • Maintain accurate product information and internal records.
  • Support day-to-day e-commerce operational workflows.
  • Coordinate information across inventory, logistics, sales, and customer operations.
  • Identify operational issues and help resolve them before they impact customers.

Reporting & Data Analysis

    • Sales
    • Inventory
    • Returns
    • Customer service
    • Product performance
    • Logistics

  • Build and maintain dashboards that give leadership clear visibility into performance.
  • Support inventory forecasting and operational planning using reliable data.

AI & Workflow Improvement

  • Use AI to support:
    • Reporting
    • Data organization
    • Dashboard workflows
    • Analysis
    • Documentation
    • Repetitive task automation
  • Develop practical AI-assisted processes that improve speed and accuracy.
  • Collaborate with developers when more technical integrations or automations are required.
  • Continuously identify opportunities to make operations more efficient.

What Makes You a Strong Fit

  • You’re highly organized and comfortable managing multiple operational workflows.
  • You understand how logistics, inventory, and e-commerce operations connect.
  • You enjoy working with spreadsheets and turning operational data into useful insights.
  • You proactively identify problems rather than waiting for them to escalate.
  • You look for better, faster ways to complete repetitive work.
  • You’re comfortable experimenting with AI tools without needing to be a developer.
  • You can independently manage responsibilities in a remote environment.

Required Experience & Skills

  • Experience coordinating freight, shipments, warehouses, or inventory workflows.
  • Strong spreadsheet skills using Excel or Google Sheets.
  • Strong operational reporting and data management abilities.
  • Experience building or maintaining dashboards, reporting systems, or operational trackers.
  • Experience with Shopify or a similar e-commerce platform.
  • Practical experience using ChatGPT, Claude, or similar AI tools in a business environment.
  • Experience improving workflows or automating repetitive operational tasks.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal English communication.
  • Ability to work independently in a remote environment during U.S. business hours.

Nice to Have

  • Inventory forecasting or demand-planning experience.
  • Experience coordinating with third-party warehouses or fulfillment partners.
  • Experience creating automated reports or dashboards.
  • Familiarity with AI-assisted data analysis and workflow automation.
  • Experience collaborating with developers on operational integrations.

What a Typical Day Looks Like

You may:

  • Review inventory levels and upcoming stock requirements.
  • Track active freight shipments and follow up with warehouse partners.
  • Create or update purchase orders.
  • Update Shopify and operational records.
  • Maintain inventory and logistics spreadsheets.
  • Review sales, returns, and product performance data.
  • Prepare operational reports and dashboards.
  • Investigate discrepancies or unusual trends.
  • Use AI to streamline a repetitive reporting or administrative process.
  • Coordinate with developers when a workflow requires deeper automation.

In short: you keep logistics, inventory, reporting, and e-commerce operations accurate and organized while continuously finding smarter ways to run them.

Key Metrics for Success

  • High accuracy across logistics and inventory records.
  • Reliable and accurate operational reporting.
  • Timely freight and warehouse coordination.
  • Strong inventory visibility and planning.

Why This Role Stands Out

What Happens After You Apply

Instead of repeating yourself across multiple screening calls, you’ll introduce yourself once, and your video will be shared with the hiring team. You can record your video as many times as you’d like before submitting it — only your final submission will be reviewed.

Apply Now
