jobs.description:
As a Vision, Mission, and Driven company, VMD has been delivering information technology solutions to the Federal government in Agile Engineering, Cybersecurity, and Critical Infrastructure Protection since 2002. Our mission has now expanded, and we have merged with Xcelerate Solutions to revolutionize end-to-end enterprise security. Together we are committed to protecting our nation’s citizens, critical infrastructure, and resources.

Why Join VMD Corp?

At VMD, now a part of Xcelerate Solutions, you have the opportunity to thrive in your career and become a Game Changer. The quality and talent of our people is what drives our success. We embrace an employee-first culture and make it a priority to provide professional development opportunities that foster career growth.
We help protect American Citizens and the nation’s most critical infrastructure by working alongside our customers and delivering game changing solutions to strengthen their missions. We believe our passion and commitment to achieving our customers' goals and solve their most critical challenges defines who we are. We don’t just dream big, we act on it – through teamwork, dedication, and resilience.

Your Impact to the Mission:

As a Senior Cybersecurity Assessment Lead, you will support a government cybersecurity assessment and oversight program focused on strengthening enterprise security governance, operational resilience, and mission assurance. In this role, you will serve as a independent assessor, program contributor, and project leader responsible for evaluating the deployment, effectiveness, and operational maturity of cybersecurity implementations across government systems, enterprise platforms, cloud environments, and security programs, ensuring compliance with applicable federal requirements, mandates, and laws. You will be expected to actively participate in and lead assessments while also helping drive assessment-related initiatives from planning through completion. In addition, you will contribute to the development and communication of program strategy, translating strategic objectives into actionable plans, priorities, processes, and measurable outcomes.

You will support the continued evolution of the assessment program through the development of maturity models, assessment methodologies, strategic plans, and process documentation, while collaborating with a team of assessors to foster a culture of knowledge sharing, continuous improvement, and technical excellence. The successful candidate will be comfortable operating at both the strategic and tactical levels—helping define where the program needs to go while actively engaging in the work required to get there.

Responsibilities:

  • Conduct in-depth technical, operational, and programmatic inspections, assessments, and audits of agency systems, applications, and enterprise services.
  • Provide task and project leadership, work allocation, and mentorship to team members across assigned assessments and program initiatives; establish priorities, track actions and dependencies, remove obstacles, and drive work to timely completion. Perform quality assurance reviews of deliverables and ensure the timely, accurate completion of assessment activities and associated reporting milestones.
  • Collect, analyze, and present accurate, risk-informed IT and cybersecurity technical and programmatic information.
  • Support the maturation and continuous improvement of the cybersecurity assessment program, partnering closely with federal leadership and staff to strengthen methodologies, governance processes, reporting standards, and enterprise assessment capabilities.
  • Help define, develop, and communicate program strategy and strategic objectives, translating leadership priorities and mission requirements into actionable roadmaps, initiatives, and measurable outcomes.
  • Develop, document, and maintain program processes, procedures, standards, and assessment methodologies, with an emphasis on creating repeatable, scalable approaches that improve program effectiveness and execution.
  • Lead and/or contribute to projects and strategic initiatives supporting the assessment program, including developing project plans, coordinating stakeholders, managing action items and dependencies, monitoring progress, and driving deliverables through completion.
  • Support enterprise strategic planning and program oversight initiatives, including cybersecurity capability roadmaps, governance enhancements, performance measures, and long-range modernization objectives to strengthen cybersecurity posture, operational maturity, and implementation effectiveness.
  • Provide executive-level input on program status, risk posture, performance metrics, and trend analysis, including the identification of recurring findings, systemic gaps, and strategic improvement opportunities. Develop recommendations and supporting analysis to inform strategic decisions and program priorities.
  • Serve as a senior technical and programmatic advisor to assessment leadership and customer stakeholders, helping identify opportunities to improve cybersecurity governance, assessment effectiveness, operational maturity, and mission outcomes.
  • Obtain and maintain DOE Derivative Classifier certification(s) as required to support mission and program responsibilities.
  • Maintain required professional certifications through continuous professional education (CPE) and ongoing professional development, while remaining current on emerging threats, evolving technologies, federal mandates, and cybersecurity best practices.

Minimum Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related discipline, with 10+ years of relevant professional experience, including 8+ years of dedicated cybersecurity experience. Additional directly related experience may be substituted for the degree requirement.
  • At least one DoD 8570 / 8140 compliant certification at the IAT Level III or IAM Level III level, such as CISSP, CISM, CASP+, CISA, GSLC, or GCIH.
  • Demonstrated expert-level experience leading and conducting IT and cybersecurity inspections, independent assessments, compliance reviews, and audit activities, including the ability to independently plan, execute, and close assessment engagements.
  • Demonstrated experience leading projects or complex initiatives, with the ability to develop work plans, coordinate stakeholders, manage competing priorities and dependencies, track progress, and drive deliverables to completion.
  • Demonstrated ability to contribute to and/or develop organizational or program strategy, including translating mission objectives and leadership priorities into actionable plans, roadmaps, initiatives, and measurable outcomes.
  • Deep working knowledge of federal cybersecurity requirements, mandates, and compliance frameworks, including FISMA, NIST SP 800-37, NIST SP 800-53, NIST SP 800-115, CNSSI 1253, and applicable OMB policies and memoranda.
  • Exceptional verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to clearly and professionally engage with senior stakeholders, customers, technical teams, and executive leadership.
  • Active or current DOE Q Clearance or Top Secret clearance with SCI eligibility, and the ability to successfully obtain and maintain a polygraph, as required.
  • U.S. Citizenship required.

Desired Qualifications and Skills:

  • Demonstrated subject matter expertise in federal cybersecurity baseline requirements, with preferred experience supporting Department of Energy (DOE) environments, directives, and mission systems.
  • Strong knowledge of organizational maturity assessment models, particularly those used to evaluate cybersecurity, information technology, and enterprise risk management capabilities.
  • Demonstrated experience developing strategic plans, capability roadmaps, program strategies, or similar strategic planning artifacts for cybersecurity, information technology, or enterprise security programs.
  • Exceptional written communication skills, including proven experience developing cybersecurity policies, standards, procedures, implementation guidance, strategic documentation, and process documentation for technical and executive stakeholders.
  • Demonstrated project management experience, including planning and executing cross-functional initiatives, coordinating stakeholders, managing schedules and dependencies, tracking risks and action items, and driving projects to successful completion.
  • Hands-on experience in secure configuration management and system hardening, including application, validation, and tailoring of appropriate DISA STIGs, CIS benchmarks, and other secure baseline standards across enterprise environments.
  • Demonstrated experience securing cloud environments, including implementation and assessment of secure configurations across AWS, Azure, or hybrid federal cloud platforms.
  • Working knowledge of Zero Trust principles, architectures, and maturity frameworks, with experience evaluating or supporting implementation aligned to federal Zero Trust strategies.
  • Experience supporting enterprise vulnerability management programs, including demonstrated proficiency with Tenable Security Center / Tenable.sc, vulnerability analysis, prioritization, and remediation validation workflows.
  • Prior experience serving in an Information System Security Manager (ISSM) or equivalent cybersecurity leadership role, with responsibility for governance, risk oversight, strategic planning, and enterprise security program execution.

The Ideal Candidate Will Excel By Demonstrating

  • A high level of initiative, professionalism, and self-motivation, with the ability to independently drive complex cybersecurity assessment activities, projects, and strategic initiatives from planning through completion.
  • The ability to operate effectively at both the strategic and tactical levels—helping define strategy and direction while actively participating in assessments and executing the work necessary to achieve program objectives.
  • Strong project leadership and execution skills, with the ability to establish priorities, organize work, coordinate stakeholders, manage dependencies, resolve obstacles, and consistently drive commitments and deliverables to completion.
  • Strategic thinking and strong business judgment, with the ability to translate broad mission objectives into practical strategies, actionable plans, and measurable outcomes.
  • Exceptional attention to detail.
  • A commitment to continuous learning, with the ability to remain current on emerging cybersecurity technologies, threat trends, assessment methodologies, and federal security mandates.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate technical findings and complex programmatic issues into clear, actionable guidance for both technical and executive audiences.
  • Natural leadership and team influence, with the ability to lead assessment efforts, facilitate stakeholder engagement, build consensus, and positively influence outcomes without relying solely on formal authority.
  • A willingness to remain hands-on as an assessor, contributing directly to assessments, analysis, interviews, evidence review, findings development, and reporting activities as needed.

Travel and Telecommuting:

  • Travel: Significant (between 25%-50%)
  • Telecommute Options: Remote, with frequent travel. Work will be conducted at various sites across the continental US. Position is currently considered remote when not traveling.

The ideal candidate is comfortable working in a growing environment where priorities can change, takes ownership without needing constant reminders, and can independently identify what needs to be done next.

Key Responsibilities

1. Executive, Administrative & Calendar Support

  • Manage and organize the physician's calendars, ensuring meetings, deadlines, agendas, links, documents, and preparation materials are consolidated in one place.

  • Attend administrative and vendor meetings as needed, take clear notes, document action items, and help ensure important follow-ups are completed.

  • Serve as a proactive accountability partner by tracking deadlines, projects, tasks, and outstanding items without requiring constant reminders.

2. Front Office & Patient Communication

  • Manage incoming patient calls, emails, texts, voicemails, and initial inquiries professionally once the clinic begins accepting patients.

  • Assist prospective and existing families with scheduling, follow-ups, basic questions, and other front-office communication needs.

  • Provide a warm, professional first point of contact that reflects the patient-centered experience expected from a pediatric practice.

3. Patient Scheduling, Intake & Registration

  • Coordinate end-to-end patient scheduling, including new patient appointments, follow-ups, rescheduling, and appointment-related communication.

  • Support patient intake and check-in by ensuring required demographic, administrative, and insurance information is collected accurately.

  • Maintain organized patient information and appointment records within eClinicalWorks (eCW) while following established clinic workflows.

4. Insurance Verification & Administrative Support

  • Verify commercial insurance coverage and determine whether patient insurance plans are active, pending, or require additional follow-up.

  • Complete insurance eligibility and benefit verification before appointments and document findings accurately for the practice.

  • Assist with insurance-related administrative tasks and potentially prior authorizations as clinic processes expand.

5. Vendor, Research & Project Coordination

  • Research vendors, clinic equipment, software, and other operational needs and compare available options based on cost, features, and suitability.

  • Organize research findings, pricing comparisons, project updates, and recommendations using spreadsheets and other tracking tools.

  • Follow up with vendors and internal stakeholders to keep clinic setup projects progressing according to established timelines.

6. Process Documentation & SOP Development

  • Document recurring workflows and administrative processes as the clinic develops its operating procedures.

  • Create clear step-by-step SOPs for tasks such as scheduling, patient communication, insurance verification, and other recurring activities.

  • Continuously identify opportunities to organize, standardize, and improve workflows as the practice grows.

Must-Have Qualifications

  • Hands-on experience with eClinicalWorks (eCW) is REQUIRED. Candidates without prior eCW experience should not be considered.

  • 1+ years previous experience as a Medical Virtual Assistant, Medical Assistant, Healthcare Administrative Assistant, or similar healthcare support professional.

  • Strong administrative, organizational, calendar-management, and task-management skills.

  • Excellent written and spoken English with the confidence to communicate professionally with patients, families, vendors, and healthcare professionals.

  • Strong spreadsheet skills and the ability to organize information, research, projects, and workflows independently.

  • Highly proactive and able to recognize what needs attention without waiting to be reminded.

  • Comfortable working in a startup-style environment where responsibilities and priorities may evolve.

  • Able to multitask effectively while maintaining strong attention to detail.

  • Comfortable using required secure networks, clinic systems, and productivity tracking software.

Strongly Preferred

  • Previous experience working in pediatrics.

  • Experience performing commercial insurance verification.

  • Experience handling prior authorizations for commercial insurance or HMO plans.

  • Experience supporting a physician, clinic owner, executive, or small medical practice.

  • Basic Canva or graphic-editing skills for simple social media or clinic content.

Tools & Systems

Candidates may work with:

  • eClinicalWorks (eCW) EMR, REQUIRED EXPERIENCE

  • RingRX or similar HIPAA-compliant phone systems

  • Google Calendar or other multi-calendar systems

  • Google Sheets or similar spreadsheet tools

  • Canva

  • Secure private networks/VPNs

  • Productivity tracking software

What Success Looks Like

You will succeed in this role if you become someone the physician can trust to take ownership of responsibilities, anticipate what needs to happen next, and keep important tasks from falling through the cracks.

You should be able to work independently, organize competing priorities, communicate professionally with families, and help create systems that allow the physician to focus more heavily on patient care.

As the practice grows, success will also mean helping create a smooth patient experience from the first phone call through scheduling, intake, insurance verification, and ongoing follow-up.

jobs.title: Engineering Manager, Infrastructure
jobs.excerpt: Omada Health is on a mission to bend the curve of chronic disease.
jobs.description:
Omada Health is on a mission to bend the curve of chronic disease.

Job overview:

We are hiring a Engineering Manager to lead two squads building Omada’s Platform and Engineering Systems. These squads own problems from prototype to production, including the maintenance and the on-call rotation for what they ship. You are responsible for those squads: what they work on, in what order, and how your people and teams grow.

As a Engineering Manager, you ship code alongside your AI-powered engineers. You own the execution and will run the squad’s rituals: iteration shaping, prioritization, backlog refinement, and initiative estimation are your calls. Being in charge means you have an opinion about the tradeoffs you and the squad are making, and are comfortable partnering with the squad’s stakeholders and finding solutions to problems, should they arise.

You partner closely with stakeholders across Engineering, Product, Design, IT, InfoSec, Legal, Compliance, Procurement, and beyond. Your relationships with the people in those departments will be very important. You will manage millions of dollars in annual vendor budget and spending, through key contracts including Amazon Web Services, Datadog, Gitlab, and Anthropic. You will be responsible for annual internal and external audit controls, and must help your teams develop automation and evidence management processes to streamline audit responses.

About you:

You are comfortable being accountable for what your squad ships. You still write code, and you want to. This role ships production work every sprint, off the critical path, in the same codebase and the same agentic workflows as your squad: you’ll feel the friction your people feel because you experience it first-hand.

You are an experienced engineering leader, and you are opinionated about the systems you maintain. You understand why the most important work must be done, and you own the roadmap that will get it done. You are respected technically, but do not need to be the strongest engineer in the squad: your work generally stays off the critical path, but you must possess the fundamental understanding to know what great looks like, and the communication skills to build strong relationships with your teams and colleagues.

You are opinionated about where AI-assisted development helps and where it produces work someone else has to redo, because you have first-hand experience from doing the work rather than from reading about it.

Above all, you are enthusiastic about providing the best possible care for our members, and building the best engineering team of your career.

What you'll be doing:

  • Managing, Hiring, and Mentoring. You will lead 5 people. You will quickly find opportunities to expand your teams, and must have a strong perspective on how to hire amazing people. Meanwhile, you must ensure that the people who work on your teams today continue growing and challenging themselves.
  • Own the squad's delivery. Sprint shaping, prioritization, backlog grooming, and estimation are yours. Make the calls, write them down, and be accountable for them.
  • Own cycle time at constant or better quality. Your squad's contribution to it is yours to move and yours to explain.
  • Ship code. Production work every sprint, off the critical path, using the same agent workflows your squad uses. This is what keeps the standing to review their work and the credibility to defend the model.
  • Grow your engineers. Omadans care about each other: we believe everyone can grow, and you will provide your reports with the best leadership they have ever experienced.
  • Own the operational health of your squad. On-call rotations, MTTR and post-incident analysis are shared work you lead.
  • Escalate early, often, and precisely. You bring tradeoffs, you use your engineering and product taste to come up with recommendations.
  • You will hire the new generation of AI-augmented Omadans. We believe in co-intelligence: we will continue hiring amazing humans, and help them build a career with us.

What you need for this role:

  • 8+ years in software engineering, including at least 2 years managing engineers, or equivalent experience leading delivery for a team you were accountable for.
  • A track record shipping mission-critical software to production, and living with it afterwards: we all make mistakes, what separates you from others is that you own these, and use this as an opportunity to build something even greater.
  • The ability to build a roadmap, plan for capacity, evaluate trade-offs, and know how to negotiate with your stakeholders.
  • Experience owning prioritization and estimation for a team, including saying no, not now, and explaining why.
  • Experience giving direct developmental feedback, and at least one case where you managed someone through underperformance with real support attached.
  • Currently shipping, or recently shipping production code in at least one layer of our stack (Multi-account AWS, self-managed continuous integration, k8s, backend (Ruby, Python, ...), GitOps release management, internal tools and services) with enough range to follow the conversation in the others and review architecture decisions critically.
  • Hands-on experience directing AI agents through real world production changes, and a considered view on where they help and where they produce work someone else has to redo.
  • Understanding of CI/CD, logging, monitoring, and telemetry, at the level where you can tell whether your squad's operational story checks out or falls short.
  • A Security-mentality in everything you design and build
  • Excellent written communication. Much of this job is writing things down clearly once so they do not have to be discussed four times.

Technologies we use:

Architecture & Infrastructure: AWS (EKS, IAM, RDS, SQS, etc), Docker, GitLab, Argo/Kargo, Vault, Datadog, PagerDuty.

Application Engineering: Ruby on Rails, Python (Flask, FastAPI), React, native iOS (Swift, SwiftUI), native Android (Kotlin), PostgreSQL, GraphQL, Claude

Benefits:

  • Competitive salary with generous annual cash bonus
  • Equity grants
  • Employee stock purchasing plan (ESPP)
  • Remote first work from home culture
  • Flexible Time Off to help you rest, recharge, and connect with loved ones
  • Generous parental leave
  • Health, dental, and vision insurance (and above market employer contributions)
  • 401k retirement savings plan
  • Lifestyle Spending Account (LSA)
  • Mental Health Support Solutions
  • ...and more!

It takes a village to change health care. As we build together toward our mission, we strive to embody the following values in our day-to-day work. We hope these hold meaning for you as well as you consider Omada!

  • Cultivate Trust. We listen closely and we operate with kindness. We provide respectful and candid feedback to each other.
  • Seek Context. We ask to understand and we build connections. We do our research up front to move faster down the road.
  • Act Boldly. We innovate daily to solve problems, improve processes, and find new opportunities for our members and customers.
  • Deliver Results. We reward impact above output. We set a high bar, we’re not afraid to fail, and we take pride in our work.
  • Succeed Together. We prioritize Omada’s progress above team or individual. We have fun as we get stuff done, and we celebrate together.
  • Remember Why We’re Here. We push through the challenges of changing health care because we know the destination is worth it.

About Omada Health: Omada Health (Nasdaq: OMDA) is reverse engineering the way healthcare is delivered in America, putting the space between doctor visits–where health is won or lost–at the center of care. Today's healthcare system poorly serves chronic conditions that require ongoing support outside of the exam room, like obesity, diabetes, hypertension, cholesterol, and musculoskeletal conditions. Omada’s virtual-first model combines human-led care teams, connected devices, and AI-enabled technology to deliver personalized care at scale, including support for GLP-1 therapy. Omada has served more than two million members since launch across 2,000+ employers, health plans, pharmacy benefit managers, and health systems. Learn more at omadahealth.com.

Omada is thrilled to share that we’ve been certified as a Great Place to Work! Please click here for more information.

We carefully hire the best talent we can find, which means actively seeking diversity of beliefs, backgrounds, education, and ways of thinking. We strive to build an inclusive culture where differences are celebrated and leveraged to inform better design and business decisions. Omada is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and affirmative action employer. We are committed to equal opportunity regardless of race, color, religion, sex, gender identity, national origin, ancestry, citizenship, age, physical or mental disability, legally protected medical condition, family care status, military or veteran status, marital status, domestic partner status, sexual orientation, or any other basis protected by local, state, or federal laws.

jobs.description:
LOCATION:Remote – must live in or near Vaya’s Western NC region. Incumbent in this role must maintain residency in North Carolina or within 40 miles from the NC border. This is a home-based position that requires community travel.

GENERAL STATEMENT OF JOB

The Transitions to Community Living (TCL) Community Liaison’s primary objectives are to provide education to members/recipients and entities stakeholders about TCL, educating providers on how to identify and report barriers, aid in eliminating barriers, provide and create training opportunities and how to access TCL and via the RSVP (Referral Screening Verification Program) process. This position works with various community stakeholders such as the individual, family, LRPs, community/state hospitals, providers, shelters, and adult care homes. This position will work closely and collaboratively with members of the TCL Team in order to meet the established time frames with requests for required documentation as needed through the process. This position ensures that the specific functions related to the Department of Justice and RSVP are followed. This is a mobile position that will require working in various locations throughout and beyond Vaya Health’s catchment area.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS

Community Education/Liaison Responsibilities:

A high level of diplomacy and discretion is required to effectively create buy in, negotiate, and resolve concerns or issues, this requires exceptional interpersonal skills, highly effective communication ability, and the propensity to make prompt independent decisions based upon relevant facts. Problem solving, and conflict resolution skills are essential. Demonstrated effective leadership presence is required, with demonstrated confidence in dealing with unknown and complex issues. Awareness of and sensitivity to the complexities of stakeholder and participant concerns.

  • Educate individuals members/recipients and referral entities (hospitals, providers, FCH, ACH, ALF and other key stakeholders) about the TCL eligibility requirements and the RSVP process.
  • Educate and provide training opportunities to internal and external stakeholders regarding TCL program process and how to identify and report barriers.
  • Cascade information to applicable departments within Vaya Health (Vaya) to assist with eliminating TCL barriers
  • Coordinates with referral entities to address and assess the needs of the members/recipients, educate on appropriate services and levels of care as needed.
  • Identifies gaps in services and intervenes to ensure that the individual receives appropriate care, can refer to MHSU Care Management, if appropriate.
  • Ensures that services for the individual are identified and coordinated across the LME/MCO’s system and with other systems, including primary care.
  • Provides education and assistance in collaboration with local hospitals (and other stakeholders) as appropriate to RSVP.
  • While providing outreach and education in the community, the Liaison may also provide potential members/recipients with information on TCL process.
  • Educate facilities stakeholders when members/recipients do not meet TCL eligibility and provide additional community resources when inquiries are received.
  • Other specific functions as they relate to Diversion, In-Reach, Transition Process and Post-Transition responsibilities as indicated from DMA/DMH.
  • Performs related tasks as required.

Collaboration:

  • Collaborates with other members of TCL team and the community to identify areas of need and provides outreach and education in these areas.
  • Serves as a collaborative partner in identifying system barriers. Attends monthly Vaya Local Barriers Committee as a “voting” member to discuss, collaborate and resolve TCL barriers.
  • Sets up, manages, and facilitates meetings with community stakeholders as appropriate to TCL and RSVP process.
  • Facilitates and coordinates the quarterly ACT/CST Collaborative Meeting with assistance across Vaya departments including Quality Management and Provider Network
  • The TCL Community Liaison will work with consumers members/recipients and providers in multiple communities both within and outside the Vaya catchment
  • Works in partnership with other LME/MCO departments to address identified needs within the catchment area.
  • Collects data from concerning TCL via staff report of concerns and collaborates within teams to find resolution of needs.

Documentation:

The TCL Community Liaison is responsible for documenting in an accurate manner that is clear and concise. This documentation will serve to inform the local organization, state, and federal government. All contacts and interventions with members/recipients will be documented in the consumer’s administrative health record if related to a specific individual need. The TCL Community Liaison is anticipated to support Vaya in meeting monthly reporting requirements required by the Department of Justice Settlement.

Other duties as assigned:

Work is performed with considerable independence, with most work performed in the community and away from the office. Employee is familiar with values and goals of TCL and Care Management and minimal daily instruction is required. Formal supervision is scheduled monthly on an ongoing basis and informal supervision occurs as needed.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, & ABILITIES

  • Exceptional interpersonal and communication skills.
  • Thorough knowledge of TCL requirements, waiver and contractual requirements, and knowledge of the TCLD database.
  • Knowledge and understanding of the Diagnostic and Statistical manual of Mental Disorders (current version).
  • Considerable knowledge of the MHSU/IDD service array provided through the network of the LME/MCO’s providers.
  • Knowledge of Medicaid eligibility determinations.
  • Ability to independently identify, implement and assess system and organizational priorities relative to TCL Initiatives.
  • Ability to be responsive to team members, internal LME/MCO staff, members/recipients, families, and external partners; communicate clearly and concisely through both verbal and writing skills and case formulation.
  • Ability to make prompt independent decisions based upon relevant facts and established processes.
  • Skill in problem solving, negotiation and conflict resolution to balance the needs of both internal and external customers.
  • High level of diplomacy and discretion is required to effectively negotiate and resolve issues with menial assistance.
  • Ability to independently organize multiple tasks and priorities and to effectively manage and assigned caseload under the pressure of deadlines.
  • Skill in Microsoft Office products (such as Word, Excel, Outlook, Forms, etc.) and Vaya Information Systems is required.

A high level of diplomacy and discretion is required to effectively negotiate and resolve issues with minimal assistance. This will require exceptional interpersonal skills, highly effective communication ability, and the propensity to make prompt independent decisions based upon relevant facts. Problem solving, negotiation, and conflict resolution skills are essential to balance the needs of both internal and external stakeholders. Must be highly skilled at shifting between macro and micro level planning, maintaining both the big picture and seeing that the details are covered.

EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS

  • A minimum of a Bachelor’s degree from an appropriately accredited university or college in public service administration, psychology, sociology, or social work or a human service programmatic field, preferably with coursework in human service planning and four years of experience in directly related human services program;

OR

  • Graduation from a four-year college or university and four years of administrative or consultative experience in a human service program;

OR

  • A Master’s degree from an appropriately accredited university or college in a related human services field and two years of supervised clinical experience;

Or equivalent combination of education and/or experience.

*Direct related experience is defined a human services experience in the areas of case management, assessment and referral, supportive counseling, intervention, psycho-social therapy, and treatment planning.

AND in addition to one of the above qualifications being met, incumbent:

  • Should have experience working with children, adolescent, and adults with MHSU and IDD diagnoses.
  • Must have an operational knowledge of funding sources and access to existing funds or ability to develop (if needed) or present specialized funding requests.

MENTAL/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

  • Close visual acuity to perform activities such as preparation and analysis of documents; viewing a computer terminal; and extensive reading.
  • Physical activity in this position includes crouching, reaching, walking, talking, hearing and repetitive motion of hands, wrists and fingers.
  • Sedentary work with lifting requirements up to 10 pounds, sitting for extended periods of time.
  • Mental concentration is required in all aspects of work.

RESIDENCY REQUIREMENT: The person in this position is required to reside in North Carolina or within 40 miles of the North Carolina border

SALARY:Depending on qualifications & experience of candidate. This position is exempt and is not eligible for overtime compensation.

DEADLINE FOR APPLICATION:Open Until Filled

APPLY:Vaya Health accepts online applications in our Career Center, please visit.

Vaya Health is an equal opportunity employer.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES | About the role

The Asia Credit Manager is responsible for leading credit risk management across the region, supporting profitable growth while protecting cash flow and minimizing bad-debt exposure. The role establishes consistent credit standards, provides independent and timely credit decisions, and drives disciplined management of customer receivables and overdue balances.

The role reports to the APAC CFO with a dotted reporting line into the Group Director of Credit Management, and works closely with Finance, Sales, Operations, Legal and Treasury across the Group, Regional and Countries organizations. The Asia Credit Manager will oversee the regional credit framework, assess material exposures, monitor portfolio risk, support country teams on deal structuring & complex cases, and provide clear reporting and recommendations to senior stakeholders.

As the Asia Credit Manager, you will lead the following activities:

Credit Risk Governance

  • Develop, implement and maintain a consistent credit risk framework, policies, approval authorities and operating procedures across Asia.
  • Ensure credit decisions comply with internal policies, delegated authorities, contractual requirements and applicable local regulations.
  • Promote strong governance, documentation quality and audit readiness across country credit and collections processes.
  • Review regional credit practices and recommend improvements to strengthen controls, consistency, speed and commercial relevance.
  • Leverage automation and AI to streamline credit processes, improve productivity, strengthen controls and accelerate decision-making.
  • Act as the regional escalation point for significant, complex or non-standard customer credit matters.
  • Manage credit insurance coverage across Asia, including customer-limit applications, policy compliance, renewals, claims and relationships with insurers and brokers.

Credit Assessment and Decision-Making

  • Lead or independently review credit assessments for new and existing customers, including financial statements, payment history, market information, ownership structure and security available.
  • Recommend and approve credit limits, payment terms, guarantees and other risk mitigants within delegated authority; escalate matters requiring higher approval with a clear recommendation.
  • Support commercial teams in structuring transactions that balance growth opportunities, customer needs and acceptable risk.

Portfolio Monitoring and Collections Oversight

  • Monitor customer exposures, overdue receivables, concentration risks, limit utilization and emerging portfolio trends across Asia.
  • Identify deteriorating accounts early and coordinate action plans with Country Finance, Sales, Legal and other stakeholders.
  • Provide oversight and challenge on collections priorities, dispute resolution, payment plans, provisioning, write-offs and recovery strategies.

Stakeholder Partnership and Capability Building

  • Build effective relationships with country finance and commercial teams, while maintaining independent credit judgment.
  • Coach and support local teams to strengthen credit analysis, negotiation, collections discipline and risk awareness.
  • Communicate decisions and risk positions clearly, including the rationale, conditions, mitigation actions and follow-up requirements.

Reporting, Controls and Projects

  • Prepare accurate and timely regional credit reporting, portfolio analysis, risk dashboards and management commentary for senior stakeholders.
  • Support internal and external audits, system or process implementations, policy updates and other regional Finance projects as required.

QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE | About you

The ideal Asia Credit Manager will have

  • A degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business or a related discipline; a relevant professional qualification is an advantage.
  • Substantial experience in commercial credit risk / credit control within a regional distribution technology environment.
  • Demonstrated experience in credit management within the IT distribution, technology or cybersecurity industry is required. Applications from candidates without relevant sector experience are unlikely to be considered.
  • Strong financial statement analysis skills and the ability to translate financial, operational and market information into sound credit decisions.
  • Practical knowledge of credit limits, payment terms, guarantees, letters of credit, credit insurance, provisioning, collections and recovery processes.
  • Experience working across multiple countries and legal or business environments, with the judgment to balance regional consistency and local requirements.
  • Proven ability to influence senior commercial and finance stakeholders, challenge constructively and communicate difficult decisions clearly.
  • Strong analytical capability, attention to detail and proficiency in ERP systems, credit reporting tools and Microsoft Excel.
  • A hands-on, proactive and collaborative working style, with the ability to prioritize effectively and operate in a fast-paced regional environment.
  • Excellent written and spoken English. Additional Asian language capability is an advantage.

We are people focused and strongly believe that talent empowers us to continue our dynasty of disruption and growth in the future. Our Mission is to drive the transition to a totally trusted digital world for all people and organizations. Visit our website www.exclusive-networks.com.

Retrieval Operations Lead

Remote

About Reveleer

Reveleer delivers a unified platform spanning risk adjustment, quality improvement, clinical intelligence, and member management for health plans and provider organizations navigating the complexity of value-based care. Trusted by 80+ customer organizations nationwide, the platform integrates data, analytics, and intelligent workflow automation into one governed system designed to support traceable documentation across diagnoses, quality measures, and submissions. With regulatory expertise and transparent, human-in-the-loop AI at its core, Reveleer supports organizations working to advance care quality, strengthen documentation integrity, and sustain the operational readiness needed to navigate audits with confidence.

POSITION OVERVIEW:

The Retrieval Lead drives frontline execution of Reveleer's retrieval program, covering approximately 500,000 chases beginning with the October 2026 go-live.

This role owns the day-to-day relationship with the program's largest AIDs, distributes and rebalances chase work assignments across the PSR team, and trains new and existing PSRs on retrieval workflows, standard processes, and provider outreach best practices.

This role is the first line of response for provider escalations, resolving access and outreach issues directly and escalating only what requires the Retrieval Manager's involvement.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

Large AID Relationship & Provider Contact

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for a program's highest-volume AIDs, maintaining direct relationships with provider office staff.
  • Monitor retrieval performance for large AIDs and proactively address barriers before they affect chase completion.
  • Coordinate directly with provider offices on record request logistics, portal access, and recurring retrieval issues.

Work Assignment & Queue Management

  • Distribute and rebalance daily chase assignments across the PSR team based on AID priority, chase age, and retrieval deadlines.
  • Monitor individual PSR workloads and adjust assignments to keep the queue moving and prevent aged chases from stalling.
  • Partner with the Retrieval Manager on weekly volume planning and flag capacity gaps before they affect throughput.

PSR Training & Development

  • Onboard and train new PSRs on chase workflows, AID ownership, pend code handling, and platform agent hand-offs.
  • Deliver ongoing coaching and refreshers on retrieval best practices, call quality, and documentation standards.
  • Maintain training materials and job aids, updating them as workflows or systems change.

Provider Escalation Management

  • Own first-line resolution of provider escalations related to retrieval outreach, record requests, or access issues.
  • Document escalation patterns and root causes and recommend workflow or script changes that reduce recurring issues.
  • Escalate unresolved or systemic provider issues to the Retrieval Manager with a clear summary and recommend next step.

Performance Monitoring & Coaching

  • Track individual and team-level retrieval rate, pend rate, and productivity against program targets.
  • Provide day-to-day feedback and coaching to PSRs based on chase outcomes and call quality.
  • Flag underperformance or training gaps to the Retrieval Manager and support corrective action plans.

Process Adherence & Documentation

  • Ensure PSR adherence to standard retrieval processes, procedures, and documentation requirements.
  • Maintain accurate, current records on AID assignments, escalation status, and chase ownership.
  • Support the Retrieval Manager with input on process updates and standard operating procedure revisions.

ABOUT YOU:

  • 2+ years of experience in healthcare operations, chart retrieval, risk adjustment, or HEDIS/quality program support.
  • 1+ years of experience training, coaching, or leading the daily work of other individual contributors.
  • Working knowledge of risk adjustment and HEDIS retrieval workflows, including chase, AID, and pend code concepts.
  • Experience managing provider-facing communication, including resolving access or outreach escalations directly.
  • Strong organizational skills, with the ability to manage and rebalance work assignments across a team in a fast-paced environment.
  • Proficiency in Excel and comfort working within chase or case management systems.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience delivering training or coaching.

Preferred

  • Direct experience supporting Medicare Advantage or ACA health plan retrieval programs.
  • Prior experience formally training or onboarding new hires in a call center or retrieval operations setting.

WHAT YOU’LL RECEIVE:

•• Medical, Dental and Vision benefits 

•• 401k match

jobs.description:
AI Solutions Architect / Copilot Developer

Human-centered problem-solving meets Microsoft AI technology

Role Overview

We're looking for someone who thinks like a strategist, debates like a philosopher, and builds like an engineer. This role sits inside our AI Solutions Group, where the individual will need to reason clearly about ambiguous problems, build consensus among stakeholders, and translate that thinking into working solutions on the Microsoft Power Platform.

You'll partner directly with clients to figure out where AI can provide tangible improvements, gather and interpret requirements (even when clients aren't sure what they need), build solutions using Power Platform tools, help test and validate what you've built, and keep it optimized over time. This role is about people, logic, and persuasion as much as it is about implementation.

Why This Role Is Different

We believe the core skills for working effectively with AI aren't primarily technical. They're:

  • Creative problem solving: finding non-obvious paths through ambiguous, messy, or "less than optimal" situations
  • Strategic thinking: seeing the whole system, not just the ticket in front of you
  • Logic and structured reasoning: the same discipline that makes a good philosopher makes a good prompt engineer and a good solution architect
  • Communication and diplomacy: building consensus among stakeholders with competing priorities, teaching non-technical teams, and handholding through change

If you have a background in philosophy, strategy consulting, teaching, mediation, debate, logic, systems thinking, or similar disciplines, and you're excited by AI tools, we want to talk to you, even if your technical resume looks nontraditional.

What You'll Actually Do

With Clients

  • Act as a trusted advisor: ask the right questions, challenge assumptions, and help clients articulate problems they haven't fully defined yet
  • Build consensus across stakeholders with different, sometimes conflicting, priorities. This is often the hardest part of the job
  • Teach and support end users through change, including patient handholding for less AI-fluent teams
  • Translate business problems into technical requirements, and technical constraints back into plain language

Building the Solution

  • Design and develop solutions in Power Automate, Microsoft Copilot Studio, and related Power Platform tools
  • When necessary, integrate adaptive cards, connectors, triggers, and APIs to extend functionality
  • Craft effective prompts and grounding strategies for Copilot, Claude, and related AI tools. This is applied logic and language craft as much as coding
  • Build and prototype using Copilot-related AI tools for development and automation, always within strict data-control guardrails
  • Where possible, apply this same workflow to working with Anthropic’s Claude

Keeping It Working

  • Participate in testing, validation, and quality assurance
  • Support ongoing maintenance, troubleshooting, and enhancement of deployed solutions
  • Document decisions and create user guides that make adoption easier, not harder
  • Escalate and resolve issues, mentoring teammates along the way

Staying Sharp

  • Continuously evaluate new AI tools and platforms, with a healthy respect for compliance, governance, and data protection in a regulated environment
  • Bring an "AI mindset": curious, experimental, but never careless with sensitive data

What We're Looking For

Core (non-negotiable) skills:

  • Strong critical thinking and structured reasoning: you can break down a fuzzy problem into a clear plan
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, including the ability to present to and persuade skeptical or non-technical audiences
  • Diplomacy and consensus-building, with comfort navigating disagreement without avoiding it
  • A genuine curiosity about AI and a track record of picking up new tools quickly
  • Comfort improvising solutions to non-technical problems, including political, organizational, or human friction, not just code bugs

Technical qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree or real-world experience equivalent, any field, with philosophy, humanities, and social sciences welcome, and 3+ years of relevant professional experience
  • Hands-on experience (or strong aptitude to quickly gain it) with Microsoft Power Platform (Power Apps, Power Automate, Dataverse) and Copilot Studio
  • Familiarity with modern AI tools, especially Microsoft Copilot and Claude, including prompt engineering and LLM behavior
  • Ability to work within a regulated environment with strict data controls, balancing experimentation against compliance

Preferred:

  • Background in strategy consulting, teaching, philosophy, logic, mediation/facilitation, or debate
  • Understanding of Microsoft Graph API, REST APIs, and system integrations
  • Experience with RAG-based architectures
  • Certifications in Power Platform, AI, or Copilot-related specialties
  • Experience with Agile/Scrum delivery

Work Environment

  • Location: United States, Eastern Time Zone
  • Travel: None required
  • Schedule: Remote-first, asynchronous-friendly, with some real-time overlap for meetings and collaboration

The Bigger Picture

This is a strategic development role on a high-performing team helping organizations reimagine how they work with AI, using Microsoft Power Platform, Copilot, Claude, and beyond. The technology moves fast, and we have a need for people who can think clearly, communicate persuasively, and navigate ambiguity with grace. If that's you, let’s talk.

jobs.description:
Everpure (NYSE: P) has evolved from storage pioneer to data platform, closing fiscal 2026 with $3.7 billion in revenue, its first billion-dollar quarter, and accelerating growth into FY27. Our strategic agenda spans the companies defining the next era of technology - hyperscalers, AI labs, the AI hardware supply chain, data platform providers, and the broader AI ecosystem.

This type of work—work that changes the world—is what the tech industry was founded on. So, if you're ready to seize the endless opportunities and leave your mark, come join us.

THE ROLE

Everpure (formerly Pure Storage) is hiring a Senior Pre-Sales Systems Engineer to support our Higher Education business, with a focus on R1 research universities.

R1 institutions are not one customer. A single campus can behave like a dozen different organizations at the same time: central IT running enterprise applications, research computing and HPC teams, genomics and imaging cores, AI and machine learning labs competing for GPU time, an academic medical center with its own rules and its own budget, and faculty groups buying infrastructure directly with grant money. Decisions move through CIOs, research computing directors, principal investigators, sponsored programs offices, procurement, and consortium contract vehicles, often in parallel and not always in agreement.

That environment rewards someone who can hold a lot of context at once, translate between very different audiences, and connect technology to the outcomes these institutions actually care about: time to result for researchers, compliance with sponsor and grant requirements, data that stays usable for a decade or more, and budgets that have to stretch further every year.

You will be the technical lead on these accounts, working alongside account managers, specialists, and partners to build solutions customers can defend internally, both technically and financially.

Location: MD / VA

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Develop a real understanding of what drives each institution: research priorities, funding cycles, capital versus operating constraints, and who actually makes the decision
  • Connect technology, including the Everpure portfolio and the broader ecosystem, to measurable research and institutional outcomes
  • Move fluently between principal investigators, research computing staff, central IT, CIOs, finance, and procurement, adapting the conversation to each audience instead of delivering the same presentation
  • Build the business case alongside the technical one: total cost of ownership, power and cooling, data center footprint, staff time, and the real cost of the current environment
  • Support research workloads end to end, from instrument and sequencer output through HPC and AI pipelines to long-term retention and archive
  • Help customers work through data management questions: lifecycle and retention, reproducibility, sponsor and funding agency data sharing expectations, research data governance, and security requirements such as NIST 800-171 and CMMC where they apply
  • Partner closely with account managers, specialists, channel partners, and higher education purchasing consortia and contract vehicles
  • Take ownership of evaluations, benchmarks, proofs of concept, and system configurations, and secure the technical win
  • Capture requirements and translate them into solutions that help institutions grow their research capability rather than just their capacity
  • Author responses to RFIs, RFPs, and RFQs, which in this segment are frequent and detailed
  • Stay current on the competitive landscape and make sure our positioning reflects it honestly
  • Follow market and research computing trends closely enough to bring that thinking back into our organization
  • Lead by example living the Pure Values: Persistence, Creativity, Teamwork, Ownership and Customer-first

WHAT YOU'LL BRING

Required

  • 8 or more years of relevant experience across technology, solution design, and customer-facing communication
  • Pre-sales or customer-facing technical experience
  • Broad technical depth across two or more of: cloud, HPC, AI and machine learning infrastructure, data management, core infrastructure, analytics, or financial and business applications. A career built entirely inside storage is not what we are looking for
  • A track record of selling on value: uncovering what the customer is trying to accomplish and connecting technology to business, operational, and financial outcomes
  • The ability to hold credible conversations with engineers, architects, executives, finance teams, and procurement, and to adjust the message for each
  • Comfort with ambiguity, and the judgment to challenge assumptions and help customers think through complicated decisions
  • Curiosity, empathy, an open mind, and a genuine appetite for continuous learning
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills
  • BS in CS, EE, another technical degree, or equivalent experience

Helpful, but not required

  • Experience with higher education, research computing, academic medical centers, or the public sector
  • Familiarity with HPC and AI environments: parallel and distributed file systems, GPU-attached storage, schedulers such as Slurm, and data pipelines for genomics, imaging, or simulation
  • Knowledge of current and emerging storage architectures (FC, iSCSI, NAS, SAN, object) and file systems
  • Linux, NFS, and distributed Linux environments
  • VMware, Ethernet, TCP/IP, and general networking
  • AWS, Azure, or GCP, and hybrid or cloud-native architectures
  • Containers, Kubernetes, and microservices
  • Data-intensive applications such as structured databases (SQL, Oracle) and analytics platforms
  • Experience with grant-funded procurement, consortium purchasing, or public sector contract vehicles

If you meet most of the required list and few of the second list, we would still like to hear from you.

Salary ranges are determined based on role, level and location. For positions open to candidates in multiple geographical locations, the base salary range is reflective of the labor market across the applicable locations.

This role may be eligible for incentive pay and/or equity.

There is no application deadline and we accept applications on an ongoing basis until the job is filled.

The annual base salary range is:
$141,400—$212,100 USD

WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT FROM US:

  • Innovation: We celebrate those who think critically, like a challenge, and aspire to be trailblazers.
  • Growth: We give you the space and support to grow along with us and to contribute to something meaningful. We have been named Fortune's Best Workplaces in Technology™, Fortune's Best Workplaces in the Bay Area™, and certified as a Great Place to Work®!
  • Team: We build each other up and set aside ego for the greater good.

And because we understand the value of bringing your full and best self to work, we offer a variety of perks to manage a healthy balance, including flexible time off, wellness resources, and company-sponsored team events. Check out for more information.

ACCOMMODATIONS AND ACCESSIBILITY:

Candidates with disabilities may request accommodations for all aspects of our hiring process. For more on this, contact us at if you’re invited to an interview.

OUR COMMITMENT TO A STRONG AND INCLUSIVE TEAM:

We’re forging a future where everyone finds their rightful place and where every voice matters. Where uniqueness isn’t just accepted but embraced. That’s why we are committed to fostering the growth and development of every person, cultivating a sense of community through our Employee Resource Groups and advocating for inclusive leadership.

Everpure is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. 22.000+ Unternehmen verlassen sich auf easybill. Wir sorgen dafür, dass Rechnungen, Prozesse und Integrationen im Alltag einfach laufen. Das ideale Profil? Du bist Freelancer und in TypeScript, React Native und Expo richtig tief drin, verstehst die Besonderheiten mobiler Anwendungen und möchtest ein Produkt in einer frühen Entwicklungsphase entscheidend prägen. Idealerweise bringst du außerdem Kenntnisse in PHP und Symfony mit, um Funktionen auch auf Seiten unserer REST-API mitzugestalten.

Aufgaben

Du entwickelst easybill-mobile auf Basis von React Native, Expo und TypeScript für iOS und Android weiter. Eine technische Grundlage mit Anmeldung, Dashboard und Dokumentenübersichten ist bereits vorhanden. Darauf baust du auf und gestaltest die nächsten Schritte gemeinsam mit dem Team.

  • Du übersetzt Anforderungen rund um Rechnungen und Dokumente in verständliche mobile Abläufe und hochwertige native Oberflächen.
  • Du entwickelst die App-Architektur weiter und schaffst wartbare Strukturen für Navigation, wiederverwendbare Komponenten, Formulare und Datenzugriffe.
  • Du bindest unsere REST-API an und sorgst für verlässliches Datenmanagement: von typisierten Schnittstellen und Validierung bis zu Caching, Ladezuständen und Fehlerbehandlung.
  • Du arbeitest an der Schnittstelle zwischen App und Backend. Bei Bedarf erweiterst du unsere REST-API auf Basis von PHP und Symfony, damit neue mobile Funktionen durchgängig umgesetzt werden können.
  • Du arbeitest an sicherer Authentifizierung, Session-Verwaltung und dem sorgfältigen Umgang mit sensiblen Kunden- und Geschäftsdaten.

  • Du sicherst Änderungen mit automatisierten Tests und prüfst das Verhalten auf Simulatoren und echten Geräten. Du gestaltest Build-, Release- und Monitoring-Prozesse bis zur Veröffentlichung in den App Stores mit.
  • Du hinterfragst Anforderungen, bringst eigene Lösungsvorschläge ein und begleitest Funktionen von der Idee bis zur Veröffentlichung und Weiterentwicklung.
  • Du nutzt KI-Werkzeuge wie Claude Code intensiv im Entwicklungsalltag und übernimmst Verantwortung für die Qualität, Verständlichkeit und Korrektheit der Ergebnisse.

Unser Mobile-Stack umfasst React Native, Expo, Expo Router und TypeScript. Dazu kommen TanStack Query und TanStack Form, Zod und NativeWind. Für Tests setzen wir auf Jest und React Native Testing Library. Unsere bestehende Plattform und die REST-API basieren auf PHP und Symfony.

Qualifikation

  • Du musst nicht jede Bibliothek bereits kennen. Entscheidend ist, dass du deinen Stack verstehst, gute technische Entscheidungen triffst und dich selbstständig in neue Themen einarbeitest.
  • Du hast fundierte Erfahrung mit TypeScript, React Native und Expo auf Senior-Level und hast mobile Anwendungen über die reine Implementierung hinaus bis zum Release begleitet.
  • Du verstehst React, Komponentenarchitektur, Zustandsverwaltung und asynchrone Datenflüsse und kannst komplexe Zusammenhänge verständlich strukturieren.
  • Du kennst die Besonderheiten von iOS und Android und gehst systematisch an Performance-Probleme, Plattformfehler und Debugging heran.
  • Du bist sicher in der Anbindung von REST-APIs und verstehst API-Verträge, Authentifizierung, Validierung und Fehlerbehandlung.
  • Idealerweise bringst du zusätzlich Kenntnisse in PHP und Symfony mit. Du kannst bestehende API-Endpunkte verstehen, Fehler zwischen App und Backend analysieren und Schnittstellen eigenständig erweitern.
  • Automatisierte Tests, nachvollziehbare technische Entscheidungen und wartbarer Code gehören für dich zum Entwicklungsalltag.
  • Du arbeitest eigenständig und pragmatisch, kommunizierst klar und behältst den Nutzen für unsere Kundinnen und Kunden im Blick.
  • Du sprichst fließend Deutsch und hast gute Englischkenntnisse.

Zusätzliche Pluspunkte sind Erfahrung mit EAS, nativen Modulen in Swift oder Kotlin sowie App-Store-Veröffentlichungen und mobilen Release-Prozessen. Auch eigene veröffentlichte Apps, Open-Source-Beiträge oder öffentliche Experimente auf GitHub sind willkommen.

Wenn du nicht jedes Kästchen erfüllst, aber ein außergewöhnlich starker Engineer bist: Bewirb dich trotzdem und zeig uns, was du gebaut hast. Zeig uns, was du gebaut hast!

Benefits

  • Remote-First Team – keine Bindung an einen Standort
  • Eine inspirierende und flexible Arbeitsumgebung, die auf Vertrauen und Eigenverantwortung basiert
  • Die Möglichkeit, an der Gestaltung der Unternehmensstrategie und -kultur mitzuwirken
  • Ein engagiertes Team und die Chance, gemeinsam an innovativen Lösungen zu arbeiten
  • Regelmäßige Teamevents

Du möchtest easybill auf iOS und Android mitgestalten? Dann freuen wir uns auf deine Bewerbung. Besonders interessieren uns Projekte, bei denen du technische Verantwortung übernommen hast: Was hast du gebaut, welche Entscheidungen hast du getroffen und was hast du dabei gelernt?

Wir freuen uns auf dich!

jobs.title: Senior Python Software Engineer/Open-Source Contributor - US Remote
jobs.excerpt: At Hugging Face, we're on a journey to democratize good AI.
jobs.description:
At Hugging Face, we're on a journey to democratize good AI. We are building the fastest growing platform for AI builders with over 11 million users who collectively shared over 4 million models, 1 million datasets & 1.5 million Gradio apps. Our open-source libraries have more than 700,000 stars on Github.

About the Role

Roles at Hugging Face are very fluid and dynamic — we are looking for someone who is comfortable taking on different challenges that will evolve over time.

You'll join the Applications team, whose goal is to build the tooling that helps developers create machine learning applications on top of the primitives we offer on the Hub: Gradio, Spaces, Inference Providers, Datasets, Xet, and more. Concretely, that means maintaining and growing libraries like Trackio, a local-first, agent-friendly experiment tracking platform, FastRTC, our library for real-time audio and video streaming in Python, and Gradio itself, used by more than 1 million developers each month. These tools have made machine learning accessible to a wide audience — for the first time in history, anyone with an internet connection can use cutting-edge models right from their browser.

Several of these libraries are still early in their life, and new ones will start from scratch. A large part of this role is taking a project from its first users to widespread adoption: shaping the API, shipping fast, and getting it into developers' hands.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Designing, developing, and maintaining core features across the team's libraries, ensuring scalability, reliability, and ease of use for ML developers.
  • Architecting complex Python projects and frameworks that serve as foundational tools for the ML community.
  • Growing early-stage libraries: defining the API surface, writing the demos and documentation that make them click, and driving adoption in the developer community.
  • Working on real-time streaming and networking capabilities, a core priority for Gradio 7 and beyond.
  • Collaborating with open-source contributors and engaging with the broader community through code reviews, discussions, and support.
  • Integrating modern frontend technologies to create seamless and intuitive user experiences for Python-based web applications.
  • Adapting to evolving engineering challenges and contributing to the direction of our developer tools as the landscape changes.

Requirements

About You

If you love open-source, are passionate about making machine learning more accessible, have experience building Python frameworks, and want to contribute to some of the fastest-growing libraries in the ML ecosystem, then we can't wait to see your application!

What you'll need

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent in Computer Science or a related field
  • 5+ years of professional Python development experience
  • Experience architecting complex Python projects or frameworks
  • A track record of taking early-stage libraries or products from first users to broad adoption
  • Professional experience with JavaScript or TypeScript
  • Professional experience with a modern frontend framework such as React or Svelte
  • Experience core-contributing to or maintaining open-source software projects

Nice to have

  • Experience with real-time audio/video streaming or networking (WebRTC, WebSockets)
  • Familiarity with libraries such as pipecat, LiveKit, FastAPI, or Starlette

If you're interested in joining us, but don't tick every box above, we still encourage you to apply! We're building a diverse team whose skills, experiences, and backgrounds complement one another. We're happy to consider where you might be able to make the biggest impact.

One more thing

At Hugging Face we believe great AI shouldn't require a massive cluster, we build for everyone, especially the GPU-poor. And because we read every application, here's a small sign that you read this one too: start your answer to the first application question with the words “GPU-poor and proud 🤗”. No trick, no catch, it just tells us a real person is on the other side.

More about Hugging Face

We are actively working to build a culture that values diversity, equity, and inclusivity. We are intentionally building a workplace where people feel respected and supported—regardless of who you are or where you come from. We believe this is foundational to building a great company and community. Hugging Face is an equal opportunity employer and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

We value development. You will work with some of the smartest people in our industry. We are an organization that has a bias for impact and is always challenging ourselves to continuously grow. We provide all employees with reimbursement for relevant conferences, training, and education.

We care about your well-being. We offer flexible working hours and remote options. We offer health, dental, and vision benefits for employees and their dependents. We also offer parental leave and flexible paid time off.

We support our employees wherever they are. While we have office spaces in NYC and Paris, we're very distributed and all remote employees have the opportunity to visit our offices. If needed, we'll also outfit your workstation to ensure you succeed.

We want our teammates to be shareholders. All employees have company equity as part of their compensation package. If we succeed in becoming a category-defining platform in machine learning and artificial intelligence, everyone enjoys the upside.

We support the community. We believe major scientific advancements are the result of collaboration across the field. Join a community supporting the ML/AI community.

jobs.title: Cloud Engineer AWS ( CDK / Serverless) ( 102-09SENG-01 )
jobs.excerpt: This role modifies a live serverless gateway in production — no downtime, no change in behaviour — leaving a clean handoff point for a downstream build managed in Terraform.
jobs.description:
This role modifies a live serverless gateway in production — no downtime, no change in behaviour — leaving a clean handoff point for a downstream build managed in Terraform. This is careful surgery on production infrastructure with active external consumers, not a greenfield build.

The scope includes modernizing a CDK estate made up of four stacks, six Lambda functions, a WAF web ACL, an mTLS custom domain/truststore, and a REST API — preserving resource identity during consolidation and coordinating two sequenced deployments with a tested rollback path.

What you will do

  • Inventory the CDK estate and build a modernization plan: upgrade the CDK library/CLI, replace deprecated constructs, move hardcoded context into per-environment config.

  • Consolidate duplicated stacks into shared constructs without losing resource identity — map logical IDs before and after, pick a preservation method, and confirm nothing gets replaced before touching production.

  • Run the library upgrade and the stack refactor as two separate, ordered deployments, with a rollback path tested in dev and test first.

  • Migrate all six Lambda functions from Node 18 to Node 24, close an open PII logging finding, and regression-test each one.

  • Re-verify the security perimeter after both deployments — WAF, the mTLS domain and truststore, X-Ray tracing, upstream timeouts — working directly with the customer's POS team across all six external callers.

  • Build deployment pipelines for dev/test/prod with OIDC federation, approval gates, and a ServiceNow change step. Add CDK assertion tests, drift detection, and API access log retention.

  • Publish the SQS queue ARN and KMS key ARN via Parameter Store, and grant send permission to the downstream Terraform-managed system — this is the key ordering dependency for that team's build.

  • Align naming, tagging, and documentation with the customer's internal standards, and document your identity-preservation decisions clearly enough for the next engineer to follow.

Requirements

  • 5+ years with AWS, including 3+ years working in infrastructure-as-code.

  • Hands-on AWS CDK experience in TypeScript — construct trees, logical ID derivation, and what happens when a construct path changes.

  • Real experience with CloudFormation resource identity: stack refactoring, logical ID overrides, cdk diff against deployed state, drift detection.

  • Working Terraform knowledge — comfortable operating across the CDK/Terraform boundary.

  • Solid AWS serverless background: Lambda, API Gateway (REST), SQS and DLQs, Parameter Store, KMS, Secrets Manager.

  • Experience with AWS edge and security services — WAF web ACLs, mutual-TLS custom domains and truststores, cross-account/cross-boundary IAM.

  • Practical experience migrating Nodejs runtimes (e.g. Node 18 → 24), including dependency and deprecation handling.

  • CI/CD pipeline experience with OIDC federation and approval gates (GitHub Actions or equivalent).

  • Working knowledge of observability tools — X-Ray, CloudWatch metrics and alarms, log retention.

  • Comfortable communicating clearly with non-engineers, and working well when parts of the scope are still being figured out.

  • Fluent English (C1 level) for daily communication with the client.

Engagement details

  • Hourly contractor

  • 100% remote

  • Estimated duration: 6–8 weeks

  • Time zone: EST or MST

Highlights

AWS CDK , CloudFormation, Terraform, AWS Serverless (Lambda, API Gateway REST, SQS/DLQ, Parameter Store, KMS, Secrets Manager), AWS Edge & Security (WAF, mTLS, cross-account IAM), Node.js, CI/CD

What you’ll do

  • Drive modular backend, service, data, and platform architecture, including modernization of the monolith and legacy backends while preventing fragmentation and service sprawl.

What you’ll bring
